title.zh: 卷七十六 列傳第一 后妃上
title.raw: 卷七十六 列傳第一 后妃上 Volume 76 Biographies 1: Empresses and Consorts 1

sentences.zh: 25%唐制：皇后而下，有貴妃、淑妃、德妃、賢妃，是為夫人。

translations.literal: Under the Tang system: below the empress were the Noble Consort, the Cultivated Consort, the Virtuous Consort, and the Worthy Consort—these were called Ladies.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang regulations, ranking below the empress were four consorts—the Noble, Cultivated, Virtuous, and Worthy Consorts—collectively termed Ladies.

sentences.zh: 昭儀、昭容、昭媛、修儀、修容、修媛、充儀、充容、充媛，是為九嬪。

translations.literal: The Bright Lady, Bright Beauty, Bright Fair Maiden, Cultivated Lady, Cultivated Beauty, Cultivated Fair Maiden, Fulfilling Lady, Fulfilling Beauty, and Fulfilling Fair Maiden—these were the Nine Concubines.
translations.idiomatic: The nine ranks of concubine were the Bright, Cultivated, and Fulfilling groups, each with Lady, Beauty, and Fair Maiden titles.

sentences.zh: 婕妤、美人、才人各九，合二十七，是代世婦。

translations.literal: There were nine each of the Fair Lady, the Beauty, and the Talented Lady, twenty-seven in all—these stood in for the royal wives of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Nine Fair Ladies, nine Beauties, and nine Talented Ladies made twenty-seven in all, corresponding to the royal wives of former ages.

sentences.zh: 寶林、御女、采女各二十七，合八十一，是代御妻。

translations.literal: There were twenty-seven each of the Treasure Grove, Palace Maid, and Selected Maid, eighty-one in all—these stood in for the imperial consorts of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-seven Treasure Grove attendants, twenty-seven Palace Maids, and twenty-seven Selected Maids totaled eighty-one, standing in for the imperial consorts of old.

sentences.zh: 自餘六尚，分典乘輿服御，皆有員次。

translations.literal: Besides these were the Six Chief Offices, which separately managed the imperial carriage, apparel, and furnishings, each with fixed quotas and ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining Six Chief Offices oversaw the emperor's carriage, wardrobe, and household goods, each with prescribed posts and seniority.

sentences.zh: 後世改復不常。

translations.literal: Later ages changed and restored these offices without fixed pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Later dynasties altered and restored these offices again and again without any stable pattern.

sentences.zh: 開元時，以後下復有四妃非是，乃置惠、麗、華三妃，六儀，四美人，七才人，而尚宮、尚儀、尚服各二，參合前號，大抵踵《周官》相損益云，然則尚矣。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era, because having four consorts below the empress was deemed improper, they established the three consorts of Grace, Beauty, and Splendor, the Six Ceremonial Ladies, four Beauties, and seven Talented Ladies, while the Chief of Palace, Chief of Ceremonies, and Chief of Apparel were each set at two; combining with earlier titles, they largely followed the Offices of Zhou with additions and reductions—thus the system was settled.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaiyuan, the court rejected restoring four consorts beneath the empress and instead created the Grace, Beauty, and Splendor Consorts, six Ceremonial Ladies, four Beauties, and seven Talented Ladies, doubling the Chiefs of Palace, Ceremonies, and Apparel and folding in older titles—largely an adaptation of the Rites of Zhou. By then the hierarchy was firmly established.

sentences.zh: 禮本夫婦，《詩》始后妃，治亂因之，興亡係焉。

translations.literal: Rites take husband and wife as their foundation; the Odes begin with empress and consorts; order and disorder depend on them, and rise and fall are bound to them.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual rests on the bond of husband and wife; the Book of Songs opens with empresses and consorts; on them hang good government and chaos, flourishing and ruin.

sentences.zh: 盛德之君，帷薄嚴奧，裏謁不忓於朝，外言不內諸閫，《關雎》之風行，彤史之化修，故淑範懿行，更為內助。

translations.literal: A ruler of great virtue keeps the inner quarters strict and secluded; private audiences do not disturb the court, and outside words do not enter the women's quarters. When the spirit of "Guanju" prevails and the lessons of the red histories are cultivated, then virtuous models and excellent conduct become inner support.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler of outstanding virtue keeps the inner palace disciplined and secluded: private audiences never disrupt court business, and outside talk never penetrates the women's quarters. Where the ethos of "Guanju" flourishes and the moral record of the harem is carefully kept, a consort's grace and conduct become a true help within.

sentences.zh: 若夫艷嬖之興，常在中主。

translations.literal: As for the rise of seductive favorites, it commonly occurs under middling rulers.
translations.idiomatic: The rise of alluring favorites, by contrast, usually afflicts rulers of merely average ability.

sentences.zh: 笫裯既交，則情與愛遷；

translations.literal: Once bed-mats are exchanged, affection and favor shift;
translations.idiomatic: Once rivals share the royal bed, affection and favor shift away;

sentences.zh: 顏辭媚熟，則事為私奪。

translations.literal: when countenance and speech grow skilled in flattery, affairs are seized for private ends.
translations.idiomatic: when looks and words grow practiced in flattery, state affairs fall to private seizure.

sentences.zh: 乘易昏之明，牽不斷之柔，險言似忠，故受而不詰，醜行已效，反狃而為好。

translations.literal: Taking advantage of a ruler's easily dimmed clarity and pulling at his unseverable softness, treacherous words seem loyal, so he accepts them without questioning; when ugly conduct has already taken effect, he instead grows accustomed and treats it as good.
translations.idiomatic: Exploiting a ruler's easily clouded judgment and his inability to cut off tender attachments, treacherous counsel masquerades as loyalty and goes unchallenged; once shameful conduct has succeeded, he grows used to it and calls it virtue.

sentences.zh: 左右附之，憸壬惎之，狡謀鉗其悟先，哀誓楗於寵初，天下之事已去，而恬不自覺，此武、韋所以遂篡弒而喪王室也。

translations.literal: Those at his side attach themselves, slanderers incite him, crafty plots clamp down his awakening beforehand, and pitiful oaths are wedged in at the first moment of favor; the affairs of the realm are already lost, yet he remains placid and unaware—this is how Wu and Wei were able to carry out usurpation and regicide and bring ruin on the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers cluster around her, flatterers stir trouble, cunning schemes forestall his waking too late, and tearful vows are fixed at the very start of favor. The realm is already lost while he remains serenely unaware—this is how Empress Wu and Wei were able to usurp the throne, murder their sovereigns, and destroy the Tang house.

sentences.zh: 至於楊氏未死，玄亂厥謀；

translations.literal: As for the Yang clan, before their death Xuan threw their plot into disorder;
translations.idiomatic: In the case of the Yang consorts, before they died An Lushan's revolt disrupted their designs;

sentences.zh: 張后制中，肅幾斂衽。

translations.literal: when Empress Zhang held sway at court, Emperor Suzong nearly straightened his robes in deference.
translations.idiomatic: when Empress Zhang dominated the court, even Emperor Suzong nearly bowed in submission.

sentences.zh: 吁，可嘆哉！

translations.literal: Alas, how lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: Alas—how lamentable!

sentences.zh: 中葉以降，時多故矣，外有攻討之勤，內寡嬿溺之私，群閹朋進，外戚勢分，后妃無大善惡，取充職位而已，故列著於篇。

translations.literal: From the mid-dynasty onward the times were full of troubles; outwardly there was the toil of campaigns, inwardly little room for indulgent attachment. Eunuch factions advanced together, and maternal kin lost consolidated power. Empresses and consorts showed no great good or evil—they merely filled their posts—so they are set forth in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: From the mid-Tang onward the age was troubled: campaigns abroad left little scope for harem excess at home. Eunuch cliques advanced in concert, and consort kin lost their grip on power. Queens and consorts thereafter did little good or ill—they simply held their titles—yet their names are recorded here.

sentences.zh: 高祖太穆順聖皇后高祖太穆順聖皇后竇氏，京兆平陵人。

translations.literal: Empress Taumu the Worthy and Sagely, consort of Emperor Gaozu: the Dou clan of Pingling in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Taumu, the Worthy and Sagely consort of Emperor Gaozu, née Dou, was a native of Pingling in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 父毅，在周為上柱國，尚武帝姊襄陽長公主，入隋為定州總管、神武公。

translations.literal: Her father Yi, in Zhou served as Pillar of the State, married Emperor Wu's elder sister the Princess of Xiangyang, and entering Sui became regional commander of Dingzhou and Duke of Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Dou Yi had been a Pillar of the State under Northern Zhou and married Emperor Wu's elder sister, the Princess of Xiangyang; under Sui he became regional commander of Dingzhou and Duke of Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 后生，髮垂過頸，三歲與身等。

translations.literal: When the lady was born, her hair hung past her neck; at three it equaled her height.
translations.idiomatic: At her birth her hair already reached past her neck; by age three it was as long as she was tall.

sentences.zh: 讀《女誡》、《列女》等傳，一過輒不忘。

translations.literal: She read the Admonitions for Women, Biographies of Exemplary Women, and similar works; one reading and she never forgot.
translations.idiomatic: She read the Admonitions for Women, the Biographies of Exemplary Women, and similar texts, and never forgot a passage after a single reading.

sentences.zh: 武帝愛之，養宮中，異它甥。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu loved her, raised her in the palace, and treated her differently from other nephews and nieces.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu doted on her, raised her in the palace, and favored her above his other nephews and nieces.

sentences.zh: 時突厥女為后，無寵，后密諫曰：「吾國未靖，虜且強，願抑情撫接，以取合從，則江南、關東不吾梗。

translations.literal: At the time a Turkic woman was empress but without favor; the lady secretly advised: "Our state is not yet settled and the barbarians are still strong. I beg you to restrain your feelings and treat her with kindness to win alliance—then Jiangnan and east of the Pass will not block us."
translations.idiomatic: A Turkic woman then held the title of empress but had fallen from favor. The young lady secretly urged him: "Our realm is not yet secure and the northern tribes remain strong. Please master your feelings and treat her with kindness to win their alliance—then Jiangnan and the lands east of the Pass will not stand in our way."

sentences.zh: 」武帝嘉納。

translations.literal: " Emperor Wu praised and adopted the advice.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Wu warmly approved her counsel.

sentences.zh: 及崩，哀毀同所生。

translations.literal: When the empress died, her grief and emaciation were as for a birth mother.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress died, she mourned with the same devastation as for her own mother.

sentences.zh: 聞隋高祖受禪，自投床下，曰：「恨我非男子，不能捄舅家禍。

translations.literal: Hearing that Emperor Wen of Sui had accepted the abdication, she threw herself from the bed, saying: "I regret I am not a man and cannot rescue my mother's clan from disaster."
translations.idiomatic: When she learned that Emperor Wen of Sui had taken the throne, she flung herself from her bed, crying, "I wish I were a man, that I might save my uncle's house from ruin!"

sentences.zh: 」毅遽掩其口，曰：「毋妄言，赤吾族！

translations.literal: " Yi hastily covered her mouth and said: "Do not speak rashly—you will exterminate our clan!"
translations.idiomatic: " Her father Dou Yi clapped a hand over her mouth: "Do not speak rashly—you will bring death upon our whole clan!"

sentences.zh: 」常謂主曰：「此女有奇相，且識不凡，何可妄與人？

translations.literal: " He often told the princess: "This daughter has an extraordinary countenance and uncommon understanding—how can she be given away casually?"
translations.idiomatic: " He often told the princess, "This girl has an extraordinary face and uncommon judgment—she must not be married off lightly."

sentences.zh: 」因畫二孔雀屏間，請昏者使射二矢，陰約中目則許之。

translations.literal: " Accordingly he painted two peacocks on a screen and had suitors shoot two arrows, secretly agreeing that only one who hit the eyes would be accepted.
translations.idiomatic: " He painted two peacocks on a screen and invited suitors to shoot two arrows, secretly resolving to accept only the man who struck both eyes.

sentences.zh: 射者閱數十，皆不合。

translations.literal: Several dozen archers tried; none qualified.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens of suitors tried their skill; none met the test.

sentences.zh: 高祖最後射，中各一目，遂歸於帝。

translations.literal: Gaozu shot last, hit each eye, and she was given to the future emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu shot last, struck each eye, and she was given to him in marriage.

sentences.zh: 始，元貞太后羸老有疾，而性素嚴，諸姒娣皆畏，莫敢侍。

translations.literal: At first the Dowager of Primordial Virtue was frail and aged with illness, yet by nature stern; all the sisters-in-law feared her and none dared attend her.
translations.idiomatic: When she first entered the household, the Dowager of Primordial Virtue was frail and ill yet stern by nature; the other daughters-in-law were afraid of her and none dared nurse her.

sentences.zh: 后事之，獨怡謹盡孝，或淹月不釋衣履。

translations.literal: The lady alone served her, cheerful and careful in filial duty, sometimes for a full month never removing her garments or shoes.
translations.idiomatic: She alone attended the dowager, cheerful and meticulous in filial service, sometimes going a full month without changing her clothes or shoes.

sentences.zh: 工為篇章規誡，文有雅體。

translations.literal: She was skilled at composing admonitory pieces; her writing had an elegant style.
translations.idiomatic: She excelled at writing admonitory essays in an elegant classical style.

sentences.zh: 又善書，與高祖書相雜，人不辨也。

translations.literal: She was also skilled at calligraphy; mixed with Gaozu's hand, people could not tell them apart.
translations.idiomatic: She was also an accomplished calligrapher; her hand mixed with Gaozu's was indistinguishable.

sentences.zh: 崩於涿郡，年四十五。

translations.literal: She died at Zhuo commandery, aged forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: She died at Zhuo commandery at the age of forty-five.

sentences.zh: 帝在煬帝時，多畜善馬，后見曰：「上性樂此，盍以獻？

translations.literal: When the emperor was under Emperor Yang he kept many fine horses; the lady saw this and said: "His Majesty delights in these—why not present them as gifts?
translations.idiomatic: While he served under Emperor Yang, he kept many fine horses. She urged him: "The emperor loves such horses—why not present them to him?

sentences.zh: 徒留之速罪，無益也。

translations.literal: Keeping them for yourself will only hasten punishment—it is of no benefit."
translations.idiomatic: Keeping them will only bring punishment sooner—it does you no good."

sentences.zh: 」不聽，頃果坐譴。

translations.literal: He did not listen; before long he was indeed punished.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to listen, and soon afterward was punished as she had warned.

sentences.zh: 帝後見隋政亂，多妄誅殛，乃為自安計，數奏鷹犬異駒，煬帝果喜，擢位將軍。

translations.literal: Later, seeing Sui government in disorder and many put to death without cause, he devised a plan for his own safety and repeatedly presented rare hawks, dogs, and horses; Emperor Yang was pleased and promoted him to general.
translations.idiomatic: Later, seeing the Sui regime in chaos and innocent men executed at whim, he devised a way to protect himself, repeatedly presenting rare hawks, dogs, and horses. Emperor Yang was delighted and promoted him to general.

sentences.zh: 因泣謂諸子曰：「早用而母言，得此久矣！

translations.literal: He wept and told his sons: "Had I followed your mother's words earlier, I would have had this long ago!"
translations.idiomatic: Weeping, he told his sons, "Had I listened to your mother sooner, I would have risen to this long ago!"

sentences.zh: 」帝有天下，詔即所葬園為壽安陵，謚曰穆。

translations.literal: When the emperor gained the realm, he ordered that the garden where she was buried become Shou'an Mausoleum and gave her the posthumous title Mu.
translations.idiomatic: After he won the empire, he designated her burial garden as Shou'an Mausoleum and gave her the posthumous title Mu.

sentences.zh: 及祔獻陵，尊為太穆皇后。

translations.literal: When she was enshrined at Xian Mausoleum, she was honored as Empress Taumu.
translations.idiomatic: When her spirit tablet was placed at Xian Mausoleum, she was honored as Empress Taumu.

sentences.zh: 始，太宗生，有二龍之符，后於諸子中愛視最篤。

translations.literal: At first, when Taizong was born, there was an omen of two dragons; among all her sons she loved and watched over him most deeply.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong was born, an omen of two dragons appeared; among all her sons she loved and favored him most deeply.

sentences.zh: 後即位，過慶善宮，覽觀梗欷，顧侍臣曰：「朕生於此，今母后永違，育我之德不可報。

translations.literal: After he took the throne, passing Qing Shan Palace he looked about and choked with sobs, turning to his attendants: "I was born here; now my mother is gone forever—the grace of raising me cannot be repaid."
translations.idiomatic: After his accession, passing Qing Shan Palace he looked around and wept aloud, telling his attendants, "I was born here. Now my mother is gone forever—the grace of her raising me can never be repaid."

sentences.zh: 」因號慟，左右皆流涕。

translations.literal: He then wailed aloud, and all those beside him wept.
translations.idiomatic: He broke into loud lamentation, and everyone present wept with him.

sentences.zh: 乃享后於正寢。

translations.literal: He then offered sacrifice to her in the main chamber.
translations.idiomatic: He then offered sacrifice to her spirit in the main palace chamber.

sentences.zh: 它日幸九成宮，夢后若平生，既悟，潸然不自勝。

translations.literal: Another day, visiting Jiucheng Palace, he dreamed of her as in life; on waking he could not restrain his tears.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion, while visiting Jiucheng Palace, he dreamed of her as in life; when he woke he could not hold back his tears.

sentences.zh: 明日，詔有司大發倉賑貧瘠，以為后報焉。

translations.literal: The next day he ordered the offices to open the granaries on a large scale to relieve the poor, as an offering in her memory.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he ordered the granaries opened on a grand scale to relieve the poor, as an act of merit in her memory.

sentences.zh: 上元中，益謚太穆神皇后。

translations.literal: In the Shangyuan era her title was further augmented to Empress Taumu the Sagely.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shangyuan era her title was further elevated to Empress Taumu the Sagely.

sentences.zh: 太宗文德長孫皇后太宗文德順聖皇后長孫氏，河南洛陽人。

translations.literal: Empress Wende the Worthy and Sagely, consort of Emperor Taizong: the Zhangsun clan of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wende, the Worthy and Sagely consort of Emperor Taizong, née Zhangsun, was a native of Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 其先魏拓拔氏，後為宗室長，因號長孫。

translations.literal: Her ancestors were the Tuoba of Wei; later one became chief of the imperial clan, and thus they took the surname Zhangsun.
translations.idiomatic: Her clan descended from the Tuoba of Northern Wei; an ancestor became chief of the imperial lineage, whence the surname Zhangsun.

sentences.zh: 高祖稚，大丞相、馮翊王。

translations.literal: Her great-grandfather Zhi was Grand Chancellor and King of Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Her great-grandfather Zhi was Grand Chancellor and King of Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 曾祖裕，平原公。

translations.literal: Her great-great-grandfather Yu was Duke of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Her great-great-grandfather Yu was Duke of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 祖兕，左將軍。

translations.literal: Her grandfather Si was General of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: Her grandfather Si was General of the Left.

sentences.zh: 父晟，字季，涉書史，趫鷙曉兵，仕隋為右驍衛將軍。

translations.literal: Her father Sheng, style Ji, was versed in books and histories, bold and fierce and skilled in warfare; under Sui he served as General of the Right Majestic Cavalry Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Sheng, courtesy name Ji, was learned in history, bold and fierce, and expert in military affairs; under Sui he served as General of the Right Majestic Cavalry Guard.

sentences.zh: 后喜圖傳，視古善惡以自鑒，矜尚禮法。

translations.literal: The empress delighted in illustrated histories, taking ancient good and evil as her mirror, and prized ritual and law.
translations.idiomatic: The empress loved illustrated histories, taking the virtues and vices of the past as her mirror, and held ritual propriety in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 晟兄熾，為周通道館學士。

translations.literal: Sheng's elder brother Chi was a scholar of the Tongdao Hall under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng's elder brother Chi had been a scholar at the Tongdao Hall under Northern Zhou.

sentences.zh: 嘗聞太穆勸撫突厥女，心誌之。

translations.literal: He had once heard how Empress Taumu urged conciliation with the Turkic empress and kept it in mind.
translations.idiomatic: He had heard how Empress Taumu urged conciliation with the Turkic empress and never forgot the lesson.

sentences.zh: 每語晟曰：「此明睿人，必有奇子，不可以不圖昏。

translations.literal: He often told Sheng: "This is a clear-sighted and wise person; she will surely bear an extraordinary son—you must not fail to arrange a marriage."
translations.idiomatic: He often told Sheng, "She is wise and discerning and will surely bear an extraordinary son—you must secure this match."

sentences.zh: 」故晟以女太宗。

translations.literal: Therefore Sheng gave his daughter to Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly Sheng gave his daughter in marriage to Taizong.

sentences.zh: 后歸寧，舅高士廉妾見大馬二丈立后舍外，懼，占之，遇《坤》之《泰》。

translations.literal: When the empress visited her family, her uncle Gao Shilian's concubine saw a great horse twenty feet tall standing outside the empress's quarters; frightened, she divined and obtained Kun changing to Tai.
translations.idiomatic: On a visit to her family, her uncle Gao Shilian's concubine saw a huge horse standing twenty feet tall outside the empress's quarters. Terrified, she cast the hexagrams and obtained Kun changing to Tai.

sentences.zh: 卜者曰：「《坤》順承天，載物無疆；

translations.literal: The diviner said: "Kun obediently receives Heaven and bears all things without limit;
translations.idiomatic: The diviner said, "Kun obediently receives Heaven and bears all things without limit;

sentences.zh: 馬，地類也；

translations.literal: the horse belongs to the category of earth;
translations.idiomatic: the horse belongs to the earthly trigram;

sentences.zh: 之《泰》，是天地交而萬物通也，又以輔相天地之宜。

translations.literal: changing to Tai means Heaven and Earth unite and the myriad things flow freely, and further that she will assist in harmonizing Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: changing to Tai means Heaven and Earth unite and all things flourish—she will help harmonize the cosmic order.

sentences.zh: 繇協《歸妹》，婦人事也。

translations.literal: The line texts accord with Marrying the Younger Sister—the business of a wife.
translations.idiomatic: The line texts accord with Marrying the Younger Sister—the work of a consort.

sentences.zh: 女處尊位，履中而居順，后妃象也。

translations.literal: A woman in an honored position, treading the center and dwelling in obedience—this is the image of empress and consort."
translations.idiomatic: A woman in a lofty place, treading the center and dwelling in obedience—this is the image of empress and consort."

sentences.zh: 」時隱太子釁鬩已構，后內盡孝事高祖，謹承諸妃，消釋嫌猜。

translations.literal: At that time strife with the Hidden Heir Apparent had already formed; within the palace the empress fulfilled filial service to Gaozu, respectfully attended all consorts, and dispelled suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: By then rivalry with the Hidden Heir Apparent had already flared. Within the palace she served Gaozu with full filial devotion, treated every consort with respect, and eased mutual suspicion.

sentences.zh: 及帝授甲宮中，后親慰勉，士皆感奮。

translations.literal: When the emperor donned armor in the palace, the empress personally encouraged the men, and all were stirred to ardor.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor armed his men within the palace, the empress personally encouraged them, and every soldier was stirred to fervor.

sentences.zh: 尋為皇太子妃，俄為皇后。

translations.literal: Soon she became consort of the Heir Apparent, and shortly after, empress.
translations.idiomatic: She soon became consort of the Heir Apparent and shortly thereafter empress.

sentences.zh: 性約素，服御取給則止。

translations.literal: By nature she was frugal and plain; for dress and furnishings she took only what sufficed.
translations.idiomatic: By nature she was frugal; for dress and furnishings she took only what she needed.

sentences.zh: 益觀書，雖容櫛不少廢。

translations.literal: She read all the more, never neglecting study even when dressing her hair.
translations.idiomatic: She read all the more diligently, never neglecting her books even while attending to her appearance.

sentences.zh: 與帝言，或及天下事，辭曰：「牝雞司晨，家之窮也，可乎？

translations.literal: When speaking with the emperor, if the talk touched on affairs of the realm, she declined: "When a hen crows at dawn, the household is ruined—how can that be allowed?"
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor spoke with her of state affairs, she refused: "When a hen crows at dawn, the household is ruined—how can I do that?"

sentences.zh: 」帝固要之，訖不對。

translations.literal: The emperor pressed her, but in the end she would not answer.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pressed her, but she would not answer.

sentences.zh: 後廷有被罪者，必助帝怒請繩治，俟意解，徐為開治，終不令有冤；

translations.literal: When someone in the rear palace was charged with an offense, she always joined the emperor's anger and asked that punishment be applied; when his mood eased, she gradually pleaded for leniency, and in the end allowed no injustice;
translations.idiomatic: When someone in the harem was accused of wrongdoing, she would echo the emperor's anger and urge punishment; once his temper cooled, she would gently plead for mercy, and never allowed an innocent person to suffer;

sentences.zh: 下嬪生豫章公主而死，后視如所生；

translations.literal: when a lower consort bore the Princess of Yuzhang and died, the empress treated the child as her own;
translations.idiomatic: when a lower consort bore the Princess of Yuzhang and died in childbirth, the empress raised the child as her own;

sentences.zh: 媵侍疾病，輟所御飲藥資之。

translations.literal: when attendant maids fell ill, she gave up her own food and medicine for them.
translations.idiomatic: when attendant maids fell ill, she gave them her own food and medicine.

sentences.zh: 下懷其仁。

translations.literal: Those below cherished her benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Those beneath her cherished her kindness.

sentences.zh: 兄無忌，於帝本布衣交，以佐命為元功，出入臥內，帝將引以輔政，后固謂不可，乘間曰：「妾托體紫宮，尊貴已極，不願私親更據權於朝。

translations.literal: Her brother Wuji had been the emperor's companion in commoner days; for aiding the founding mandate he was a chief merit-holder, entering and leaving the inner apartments. The emperor was about to bring him in to assist in government; the empress firmly said it must not be done and seized an occasion to say: "Your servant's body rests in the Purple Palace; my honor is already at its height. I do not wish private kin to hold power at court again."
translations.idiomatic: Her brother Zhangsun Wuji had been the emperor's friend in commoner days and, for aiding the founding of the dynasty, ranked among the greatest merit holders, with free access to the inner apartments. When the emperor was about to bring him into government, the empress firmly opposed it, saying on one occasion, "I already enjoy the highest honor in the Purple Palace. I do not want my kin to wield power at court again."

sentences.zh: 漢之呂、霍，可以為誡。

translations.literal: The Lü and Huo of Han may serve as a warning."
translations.idiomatic: The Lü and Huo clans of Han should be warning enough."

sentences.zh: 」帝不聽，自用無忌為尚書僕射。

translations.literal: The emperor did not listen and on his own appointed Wuji Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen and appointed Wuji Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 后密諭令牢讓，帝不獲已，乃聽，后喜見顏間。

translations.literal: The empress secretly instructed him to decline firmly; the emperor, unable to do otherwise, yielded, and joy showed in her countenance.
translations.idiomatic: The empress secretly urged Wuji to decline firmly. Unable to prevail, the emperor yielded, and her joy showed plainly on her face.

sentences.zh: 異母兄安業無行，父喪，逐后、無忌還外家。

translations.literal: Her half-brother Anye was without conduct; at their father's death he drove the empress and Wuji back to her natal family.
translations.idiomatic: Her half-brother Anye was a man of bad character. At their father's death he drove the empress and Wuji back to her natal family.

sentences.zh: 后貴，未嘗以為言。

translations.literal: After the empress rose in rank, she never spoke of it.
translations.idiomatic: After she rose to eminence, she never mentioned the matter.

sentences.zh: 擢位將軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to general.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general.

sentences.zh: 後與李孝常等謀反，將誅，后叩頭曰：「安業罪死無赦。

translations.literal: Later he joined Li Xiaochang and others in plotting rebellion and was to be executed; the empress kowtowed and said: "Anye's crime deserves death without pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Later he joined Li Xiaochang and others in plotting rebellion and was condemned to death. The empress kowtowed and said, "Anye's crime deserves death without mercy.

sentences.zh: 然向遇妾不以慈，戶知之；

translations.literal: Yet in the past he treated your servant without kindness—the household knows it;
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the past he treated me without kindness, as everyone in the household knows;

sentences.zh: 今論如法，人必謂妾釋憾於兄，無乃為帝累乎！

translations.literal: if he is now punished according to law, people will surely say your servant is venting old resentment on her brother—will that not be a burden on Your Majesty!"
translations.idiomatic: if he is punished by law now, people will surely say I am settling an old score with my brother—would that not reflect badly on Your Majesty?"

sentences.zh: 」遂得減流越巂。

translations.literal: He was thus spared and exiled to Yuexi.
translations.idiomatic: He was spared execution and banished to Yuexi instead.

sentences.zh: 太子承乾乳媼請增東宮什器，后曰：「太子患無德與名，器何請為？

translations.literal: The wet nurse of Heir Apparent Chengqian asked for more furnishings for the Eastern Palace; the empress said: "The heir's worry is lack of virtue and reputation—why ask for vessels?"
translations.idiomatic: The wet nurse of Heir Apparent Chengqian asked for more furnishings for the Eastern Palace. The empress said, "The heir should worry about lacking virtue and reputation—why ask for more vessels?"

sentences.zh: 從幸九成宮，方屬疾，會柴紹等急變聞，帝甲而起，后輿疾以從，宮司諫止，后曰：「上震驚，吾可自安？

translations.literal: Accompanying the emperor to Jiucheng Palace, she was just then ill when news came of the sudden crisis with Chai Shao and others; the emperor rose in armor, and the empress followed in her litter though ill. Palace officials urged her to stop; she said: "His Majesty is alarmed—how can I rest at ease?"
translations.idiomatic: While accompanying the emperor to Jiucheng Palace she fell ill. When news came of the sudden revolt led by Chai Shao and others, the emperor rose and armed himself; the empress followed in her litter despite her illness. Palace officials urged her to stop, but she said, "The emperor is in peril—how can I rest at ease?"

sentences.zh: 」疾稍亟，太子欲請大赦，汎度道人，祓塞災會。

translations.literal: Her illness grew worse; the heir wished to request a general amnesty, ordain Buddhist and Daoist clergy, and perform rites to ward off calamity.
translations.idiomatic: As her illness worsened, the heir wished to request a general amnesty, ordain Buddhist and Daoist clergy, and perform rites to ward off calamity.

sentences.zh: 后曰：「死生有命，非人力所支。

translations.literal: The empress said: "Life and death have their mandate; they are not within human power to sustain.
translations.idiomatic: The empress said, "Life and death are ordained by fate; they are not within human power to alter.

sentences.zh: 若修福可延，吾不為惡；

translations.literal: If cultivating merit could extend life, I have done no evil;
translations.idiomatic: If cultivating merit could prolong life, I have done no evil;

sentences.zh: 使善無效，我尚何求？

translations.literal: if goodness is ineffective, what more can I seek?
translations.idiomatic: if goodness avails nothing, what more can I ask for?

sentences.zh: 且赦令，國大事，佛、老異方教耳，皆上所不為，豈宜以吾亂天下法！

translations.literal: Moreover amnesty is a great affair of state; Buddhism and Daoism are foreign teachings—all things His Majesty does not do. How can I disorder the laws of the realm because of myself!"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, an amnesty is a grave affair of state, and Buddhism and Daoism are foreign teachings—things His Majesty does not practice. How can I disrupt the laws of the realm on my account!"

sentences.zh: 」太子不敢奏，以告房玄齡，玄齡以聞，帝嗟美。

translations.literal: The heir did not dare memorialize this but told Fang Xuanling; Xuanling reported it, and the emperor sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: The heir did not dare memorialize the request but told Fang Xuanling, who reported her words to the emperor, who sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 而群臣請遂赦，帝既許，后固爭止。

translations.literal: Yet when the ministers asked that the amnesty proceed, the emperor having already agreed, the empress firmly argued until it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When the ministers pressed for the amnesty and the emperor had already agreed, the empress argued firmly until the plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 及大漸，與帝決，時玄齡小譴就第，后曰：「玄齡久事陛下，預奇計秘謀，非大故，願勿置也。

translations.literal: As her illness grew grave, she took leave of the emperor; at the time Xuanling had been lightly punished and sent home. The empress said: "Xuanling has long served Your Majesty and shared in extraordinary plans and secret counsels. Unless for a grave offense, I beg that he not be set aside."
translations.idiomatic: When her illness turned critical, she bade the emperor farewell. Fang Xuanling had just been lightly punished and sent home. She said, "Fang Xuanling has served you for years and shared your most secret counsels. Unless he has committed a grave offense, please do not cast him aside."

sentences.zh: 妾家以恩澤進，無德而祿，易以取禍，無屬樞柄，以外戚奉朝請足矣。

translations.literal: Your servant's clan rose through favor; without merit they hold salary and easily invite disaster. Let them not hold the pivots of power—suffice it that maternal kin attend court as guests.
translations.idiomatic: My family rose through imperial favor without merit; such unearned privilege invites disaster. Let them not hold the levers of power—it is enough that they attend court as honored guests.

sentences.zh: 妾生無益於時，死不可以厚葬，願因山為壟，無起墳，無用棺槨，器以瓦木，約費送終，是妾不見忘也。

translations.literal: Your servant's life was of no benefit to the age; in death she must not receive lavish burial. I wish to be buried in a mound against the mountain, with no raised tomb, no coffin or outer case, vessels of tile and wood, and frugal expense for the funeral—this is how your servant will not be forgotten.
translations.idiomatic: I have done little good in life and should not receive a lavish burial. Bury me in a simple mound against the hillside—no raised tomb, no coffin, only vessels of tile and wood, and keep the funeral frugal. That is how I wish to be remembered.

sentences.zh: 」又請帝納忠容諫，勿受讒，省遊畋作役，死無恨。

translations.literal: She also asked the emperor to accept loyal remonstrance, not to heed slander, and to reduce hunting, travel, and corvée labor—then she would die without regret.
translations.idiomatic: She also urged him to welcome loyal counsel, reject slander, and cut back on hunting, travel, and forced labor—then she could die without regret.

sentences.zh: 崩，年三十六。

translations.literal: She died, aged thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: She died at the age of thirty-six.

sentences.zh: 后嘗采古婦人事著《女則》十篇，又為論斥漢之馬后不能檢抑外家，使與政事，乃戒其車馬之侈，此謂開本源，恤末事。

translations.literal: The empress once gathered ancient women's affairs and composed ten chapters of the Admonitions for Women, and also wrote a treatise condemning Empress Ma of Han for failing to restrain her maternal kin and letting them join in government, while only warning against the extravagance of their carriages and horses—this is called opening the source and caring for the branches.
translations.idiomatic: She had collected stories of exemplary women and written ten chapters of the Admonitions for Women, and also composed a treatise condemning Empress Ma of Han for failing to restrain her kin from politics while only fussing over their carriages and horses—attacking the root cause, not merely the symptoms.

sentences.zh: 常誡守者：「吾以自檢，故書無條理，勿令至尊見之。

translations.literal: She often warned the keepers: "I wrote this for my own self-examination, so the text has no order—do not let His Majesty see it."
translations.idiomatic: She often told her attendants, "I wrote this for my own self-examination, so it is disorderly—do not let His Majesty see it."

sentences.zh: 」及崩，宮司以聞，帝為之慟，示近臣曰：「后此書可用垂後，我豈不通天命而割情乎！

translations.literal: When she died the palace offices reported it; the emperor mourned deeply and showed the book to close ministers, saying: "This book of the empress can instruct posterity—how can I fail to understand Heaven's mandate yet cut off my feelings!"
translations.idiomatic: After her death the palace reported the book to him. He mourned deeply and showed it to his closest ministers, saying, "This book can instruct future generations. How can I fail to accept Heaven's decree yet still grieve?"

sentences.zh: 顧內失吾良佐，哀不可已已！

translations.literal: Yet within I have lost my fine assistant—my grief cannot be ended!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet I have lost my finest counselor within the palace—my grief cannot be stilled!"

sentences.zh: 」謚曰文德，葬昭陵，因九嵕山，以成后志。

translations.literal: Her posthumous title was Wende; she was buried at Zhaoling, following Jiufeng Mountain to fulfill the empress's wish.
translations.idiomatic: She was given the posthumous title Wende and buried at Zhaoling on Jiufeng Mountain, in accordance with her wishes.

sentences.zh: 帝自著表序始末，揭陵左。

translations.literal: The emperor himself composed a memorial preface recounting the whole course and had it posted at the left of the mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor himself wrote a memorial preface recounting her life and had it posted at the left of the mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 上元中，益謚文德聖皇后。

translations.literal: In the Shangyuan era her title was further augmented to Empress Wende the Sagely.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shangyuan era her title was further elevated to Empress Wende the Sagely.

sentences.zh: 太宗賢妃徐惠太宗賢妃徐惠，湖州長城人。

translations.literal: Worthy Consort Xu Hui of Emperor Taizong: the Xu clan of Changcheng in Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Worthy Consort Xu Hui of Emperor Taizong, née Xu, was a native of Changcheng in Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 生五月能言，四歲通《論語》、《詩》，八歲自曉屬文。

translations.literal: At five months she could speak; at four she mastered the Analects and the Odes; at eight she could compose prose on her own.
translations.idiomatic: At five months she could speak; at four she had mastered the Analects and the Odes; at eight she could compose prose on her own.

sentences.zh: 父孝德，嘗試使擬《離騷》為《小山篇》曰：「仰幽巖而流盼，撫桂枝以凝想。

translations.literal: Her father Xiaode once tested her by having her model the "Encountering Sorrow" as "The Lesser Hill," which read: "Gazing up at the dark cliff I let my eyes wander; stroking the cassia branch I sink in thought."
translations.idiomatic: Her father Xiaode once tested her by asking her to model Qu Yuan's "Encountering Sorrow" as "The Lesser Hill": "Gazing up at the dark cliff I let my eyes wander; stroking the cassia branch I sink in thought."

sentences.zh: 將千齡兮此遇，荃何為兮獨往？

translations.literal: A thousand years I shall meet here—why must the iris go alone?"
translations.idiomatic: A thousand years I shall meet here—why must the iris blossom go alone?"

sentences.zh: 」孝德大驚，知不可掩，於是所論著遂盛傳。

translations.literal: Xiaode was greatly astonished, knowing her talent could not be hidden; thereafter her writings spread widely.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaode was astonished, knowing her gift could not be hidden; from then on her writings circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞之，召為才人。

translations.literal: Taizong heard of her and summoned her as a Talented Lady.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong heard of her, he summoned her to court as a Talented Lady.

sentences.zh: 手未嘗廢卷，而辭致贍蔚，文無淹思。

translations.literal: Her hand never left a book; her phrasing was rich and lush, and her writing showed no delay in thought.
translations.idiomatic: She never set aside her books; her style was rich and fluent, and her compositions came without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 帝益禮顧，擢孝德水部員外郎，惠再遷充容。

translations.literal: The emperor treated her with increasing honor, promoted Xiaode to Vice Director of the Water Ministry, and Hui was again promoted to Fulfilling Fair Maiden.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor honored her increasingly, promoted Xiaode to Vice Director of the Water Ministry, and advanced Hui to Fulfilling Fair Maiden.

sentences.zh: 貞觀末，數調兵討定四夷，稍稍治宮室，百姓勞怨。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhenguan era troops were repeatedly mobilized to subdue the four barbarians, and palaces were gradually repaired; the common people grew weary and resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Zhenguan era the court repeatedly mobilized troops against the frontier peoples and gradually expanded the palaces; the people grew weary and resentful.

sentences.zh: 惠上疏極諫，且言：「東戍遼海，西討崑丘，士馬罷耗，漕饟漂沒。

translations.literal: Hui submitted a memorial of stern remonstrance, saying: "In the east we garrison Liaohai, in the west we campaign against Kunqiu; soldiers and horses are exhausted, and transport grain is swept away and lost."
translations.idiomatic: Hui submitted a stern memorial of remonstrance, saying, "In the east we garrison Liaodong, in the west we campaign against Kunlun; soldiers and horses are exhausted, and transport grain is lost at sea."

sentences.zh: 捐有盡之農，趨無窮之壑；

translations.literal: We abandon finite agriculture to rush into an bottomless abyss;
translations.idiomatic: We abandon finite agriculture to pour resources into a bottomless pit;

sentences.zh: 圖未獲之眾，喪已成之軍。

translations.literal: we scheme for peoples not yet won and lose armies already formed.
translations.idiomatic: we strive for peoples not yet conquered and destroy armies already raised.

sentences.zh: 故地廣者，非常安之術也；

translations.literal: Therefore broad territory is not the method of lasting peace;
translations.idiomatic: Expanding territory is therefore not the path to lasting peace;

sentences.zh: 人勞者，為易亂之符也。

translations.literal: when the people are weary, it is a sign of easy disorder.
translations.idiomatic: when the people are exhausted, it is a sign that disorder is near.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「翠微、玉華等宮，雖因山藉水，無築構之苦，而工力和僦，不謂無煩。

translations.literal: She also said: "Palaces such as Cuicui and Yuhua, though built by relying on mountains and water without the pain of construction, still require labor and hired service—not without trouble."
translations.idiomatic: She also wrote, "Palaces such as Cuicui and Yuhua, though built into mountains and streams without massive construction, still demand labor and expense—they are not without cost."

sentences.zh: 有道之君，以逸逸人；

translations.literal: A ruler with the Way lets the people rest in ease;
translations.idiomatic: A ruler who possesses the Way lets his people rest;

sentences.zh: 無道之君，以樂樂身。

translations.literal: a ruler without the Way seeks pleasure for himself.
translations.idiomatic: a ruler without the Way seeks pleasure only for himself.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「伎巧為喪國斧斤，珠玉為蕩心酖毒，侈麗纖美，不可以不遏。

translations.literal: She also said: "Craft and cleverness are the axe and adze that ruin a state; pearls and jade are poison that unsettles the heart—luxurious finery cannot go unchecked."
translations.idiomatic: She also wrote, "Craftsmanship is the axe that destroys a state; pearls and jade are poison to the mind—extravagant beauty must be restrained."

sentences.zh: 志驕於業泰，體逸於時安。

translations.literal: Ambition grows proud when enterprise flourishes; the body grows idle when times are peaceful.
translations.idiomatic: Ambition grows arrogant when the realm prospers; the body grows idle when times are peaceful.

sentences.zh: 」其剴切精詣，大略如此。

translations.literal: Her earnest precision was broadly of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: Her remonstrance was earnest and precise in roughly this vein.

sentences.zh: 帝善其言，優賜之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved her words and rewarded her generously.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved her counsel and rewarded her generously.

sentences.zh: 帝崩，哀慕成疾，不肯進藥，曰：「帝遇我厚，得先狗馬侍園寢，吾志也。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, grief and longing became illness; she refused medicine, saying: "His Majesty treated me generously; to go before him as his hound and horse and attend the garden mausoleum is my wish."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died, grief became illness; she refused medicine, saying, "His Majesty treated me generously. To follow him first and attend his tomb is my wish."

sentences.zh: 」復為詩、連珠以見意。

translations.literal: She again composed poems and linked pearls to express her intent.
translations.idiomatic: She composed poems and linked-pearl verses to express her grief.

sentences.zh: 永徽元年卒，年二十四，贈賢妃，陪葬昭陵石室。

translations.literal: She died in the first year of Yonghui, aged twenty-four; she was posthumously honored as Worthy Consort and buried in the stone chamber at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the first year of Yonghui at the age of twenty-four, was posthumously honored as Worthy Consort, and was buried in the stone chamber at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 惠之弟齊聃，齊聃子堅，皆以學聞，女弟為高宗婕妤，亦有文藻，世以擬漢班氏。

translations.literal: Hui's younger brother Qi Tan and Qi's son Jian were all famed for learning; a younger sister became a Fair Lady under Gaozong and was also accomplished in letters—the age compared them to the Ban clan of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's younger brother Qi Tan and his son Jian were renowned scholars; a younger sister became a Fair Lady under Emperor Gaozong and was also accomplished in letters—the age compared the family to the Ban clan of Han.

sentences.zh: 高宗廢后王氏高宗廢后王氏，并州祁人，魏尚書左僕射思政之孫。

translations.literal: The Deposed Empress Wang of Emperor Gaozong: the Wang clan of Qi in Bingzhou, granddaughter of Sima Zheng of Wei, Vice Director of the Left of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The Deposed Empress Wang of Emperor Gaozong, née Wang, was a native of Qi in Bingzhou and granddaughter of Wang Sima Zheng, Vice Director of the Left of the Imperial Secretariat under Wei.

sentences.zh: 從祖母同安長公主以后婉淑，白太宗以為晉王妃。

translations.literal: Her father's cousin the Princess of Tong'an, finding the lady gentle and virtuous, told Taizong to make her consort of the Prince of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Her father's cousin, the Princess of Tong'an, finding her gentle and virtuous, recommended her to Taizong as consort of the Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 王居東宮，妃亦進冊，擢父仁祐陳州刺史。

translations.literal: When Wang resided in the Eastern Palace, the consort was also advanced in rank, and her father Renyou was promoted to prefect of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang resided in the Eastern Palace as heir, she was formally invested as his consort, and her father Renyou was promoted to prefect of Chen.

sentences.zh: 帝即位，立為皇后。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne, she was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: When he ascended the throne, she was made empress.

sentences.zh: 仁祐以特進封魏國公；

translations.literal: Renyou was enfeoffed as Duke of Wei with special advancement;
translations.idiomatic: Renyou was enfeoffed as Duke of Wei with special advancement;

sentences.zh: 母柳，本國夫人。

translations.literal: her mother the Liu clan was originally Lady of the State.
translations.idiomatic: her mother, née Liu, was originally Lady of the State.

sentences.zh: 仁祐卒，贈司空。

translations.literal: When Renyou died, he was posthumously honored as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Renyou died, he was posthumously honored as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 初，蕭良娣有寵，而武才人貞觀末以先帝宮人召為昭儀，俄與后、良娣爭寵，更相毀短。

translations.literal: At first the Worthy Lady Xiao had favor, while the Talented Lady Wu, a former palace woman of the late emperor, was summoned at the end of Zhenguan as Bright Lady; soon she vied with the empress and the Worthy Lady for favor, each slandering the other.
translations.idiomatic: At first the Worthy Lady Xiao held the emperor's favor. Wu, a former palace woman of the late emperor, was summoned in late Zhenguan as Bright Lady; soon she was vying with the empress and Xiao for favor, each slandering the other.

sentences.zh: 而昭儀詭險，即誣后與母挾媚道蠱上，帝信之，解魏國夫人門籍，罷后舅柳奭中書令。

translations.literal: The Bright Lady was treacherous and crafty; she at once accused the empress and her mother of using seductive arts and witchcraft against the emperor. The emperor believed her, stripped the Lady of Wei of her household register, and removed the empress's uncle Liu Shi from the post of Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: The Bright Lady was treacherous and cunning. She accused the empress and her mother of witchcraft and seductive arts against the emperor. He believed her, stripped the Wang family's privileges, and removed the empress's uncle Liu Shi as Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: 李義府等陰佐昭儀，以偏言怒帝，遂下詔廢后、良娣皆為庶人，囚宮中。

translations.literal: Li Yifu and others secretly aided the Bright Lady; with one-sided words they enraged the emperor, and he issued an edict deposing the empress and Worthy Lady as commoners and imprisoning them in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yifu and others secretly aided the Bright Lady; with biased words they enraged the emperor, who issued an edict deposing the empress and Xiao as commoners and imprisoning them in the palace.

sentences.zh: 后母兄、良娣宗族悉流嶺南。

translations.literal: The empress's maternal kin and the Worthy Lady's clans were all exiled to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's maternal kin and Xiao's clan were all exiled to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 許敬宗又奏：「仁祐無他功，以宮掖故，超列三事，今庶人謀亂宗社，罪宜夷宗，仁祐應斫棺，陛下不窮其誅，家止流竄，仁祐不宜引庇廕宥逆子孫。

translations.literal: Xu Jingzong further memorialized: "Renyou had no other merit but rose to the three highest offices because of the inner palace. Now the commoner plots to overturn the altars of state; the crime should exterminate the clan. Renyou's coffin should be hacked open. Your Majesty does not carry the punishment to its limit and only exiles the family—Renyou should not shelter and grant favor to rebellious descendants."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jingzong further memorialized, "Renyou had no merit beyond palace connections yet rose to the highest offices. Now his daughter plots against the state; the clan should be exterminated and his coffin opened. Your Majesty has only exiled the family—Renyou should not shield rebellious descendants."

sentences.zh: 」有詔盡奪仁祐官爵。

translations.literal: An edict was issued stripping Renyou of all offices and titles.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stripped Renyou of all offices and titles.

sentences.zh: 而後及良娣俄為武后所殺，改后姓為「蟒」，良娣為「梟」。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the empress and Worthy Lady were killed by Empress Wu; the empress's surname was changed to "python" and the Worthy Lady's to "owl."
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the empress and Xiao were killed on Wu's orders; the empress's surname was changed to "python" and Xiao's to "owl."

sentences.zh: 初，帝念后，間行至囚所，見門禁錮嚴，進飲食竇中，惻然傷之，呼曰：「皇后、良娣無恙乎？

translations.literal: At first the emperor thought of the empress and went by a side path to the place of imprisonment; seeing the gates strictly barred, he sent food through a hole and was moved with pity, calling: "Are the empress and Worthy Lady well?"
translations.idiomatic: At first the emperor still thought of the empress and stole to the prison. Seeing the gates barred, he sent food through a hole and called out in pity, "Are the empress and Worthy Lady well?"

sentences.zh: 今安在？

translations.literal: Where are you now?"
translations.idiomatic: Where are you now?"

sentences.zh: 」二人同辭曰：「妾等以罪棄為婢，安得尊稱耶？

translations.literal: The two answered together: "Your servants were cast out as guilty maids—how can we bear honored titles?"
translations.idiomatic: Both answered, "We are guilty maids cast out from favor—how can we bear honored titles?"

sentences.zh: 」流淚嗚咽。

translations.literal: They wept and sobbed.
translations.idiomatic: They wept and sobbed.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「陛下幸念疇日，使妾死更生，復見日月，乞署此為『回心院』。

translations.literal: They also said: "If Your Majesty would kindly remember former days and let your servants die and live again, seeing sun and moon once more, we beg that this place be named the Court of Returning Hearts."
translations.idiomatic: They also said, "If Your Majesty remembers former days and restores us to life and light, we beg that this place be named the Court of Returning Hearts."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「朕即有處置。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I shall soon have arrangements."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I shall soon make arrangements."

sentences.zh: 」武后知之，促詔杖二人百，剔其手足，反接投釀甕中，曰：「令二嫗骨醉！

translations.literal: When Empress Wu learned of this, she hastily ordered both beaten a hundred strokes, cut off their hands and feet, bound them back to back, and cast them into a wine vat, saying: "Let the two old women' bones be drunk!"
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu learned of this, she ordered both beaten a hundred strokes, had their limbs cut off, bound them back to back, and cast them into a wine vat, saying, "Let the two old women' bones be drunk!"

sentences.zh: 」數日死，殊其屍。

translations.literal: Within days they died; their corpses were mutilated.
translations.idiomatic: Within days they died; their corpses were mutilated.

sentences.zh: 初，詔旨到，后再拜曰：「陛下萬年！

translations.literal: When the edict first arrived, the empress bowed twice and said: "May Your Majesty live ten thousand years!"
translations.idiomatic: When the edict first arrived, the empress bowed and said, "May Your Majesty live ten thousand years!"

sentences.zh: 昭儀承恩，死吾分也。

translations.literal: The Bright Lady enjoys favor; death is my portion.
translations.idiomatic: The Bright Lady enjoys favor; death is my portion.

sentences.zh: 」至良娣，罵曰：「武氏狐媚，翻覆至此！

translations.literal: When it came to the Worthy Lady, she cursed: "The Wu clan's fox-bewitching has overturned things to this point!"
translations.idiomatic: Xiao cursed, "The Wu clan's witchery has overturned everything to this point!"

sentences.zh: 我後為貓，使武氏為鼠，吾當扼其喉以報。

translations.literal: After death I shall be a cat and make the Wu clan mice—I shall seize their throats in revenge."
translations.idiomatic: After death I shall be a cat and make the Wu clan mice—I shall seize their throats in revenge."

sentences.zh: 」后聞，詔六宮毋畜貓。

translations.literal: When the empress heard this, she ordered that cats not be kept in the six palaces.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu heard this, she forbade cats throughout the six palaces.

sentences.zh: 武后頻見二人被髮瀝血為厲，惡之，以巫祝解謝，即徙蓬萊宮，厲復見，故多駐東都。

translations.literal: Empress Wu frequently saw the two with disheveled hair dripping blood as malign spirits; she loathed this and had shamans perform rites of release, then moved to Penglai Palace, but the spirits appeared again—therefore she often stayed at the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu often saw the two as vengeful spirits with disheveled hair dripping blood. She loathed this and had shamans perform rites, then moved to Penglai Palace, but the spirits appeared again—so she often stayed at the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 中宗即位，皆復其姓。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong took the throne, both surnames were restored.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong took the throne, both surnames were restored.

sentences.zh: 高宗則天武皇后高宗則天順聖皇后武氏，并州文水人。

translations.literal: Empress Zetian the Worthy and Sagely, consort of Emperor Gaozong: the Wu clan of Wenshui in Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zetian, the Worthy and Sagely consort of Emperor Gaozong, née Wu, was a native of Wenshui in Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 父士彠，見《外戚傳》。

translations.literal: Her father Shiyi is treated in the Biography of Maternal Kin.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Shiyi is treated in the Biography of Maternal Kin.

sentences.zh: 文德皇后崩，久之，太宗聞士彟女美，召為才人，方十四。

translations.literal: After Empress Wende died, some time passed; Taizong heard that Shiyi's daughter was beautiful and summoned her as a Talented Lady when she was just fourteen.
translations.idiomatic: Some time after Empress Wende's death, Taizong heard that Shiyi's daughter was beautiful and summoned her as a Talented Lady when she was only fourteen.

sentences.zh: 母楊，慟泣與訣，后獨自如，曰：「見天子庸知非福，何兒女悲乎？

translations.literal: Her mother the Yang clan wept and took leave in grief; the lady alone was composed, saying: "To see the Son of Heaven—how can one know it is not fortune? Why weep like a child?"
translations.idiomatic: Her mother Yang wept at parting; the girl alone remained composed, saying, "To see the Son of Heaven—how can that be anything but fortune? Why weep like a child?"

sentences.zh: 」母韙其意，止泣。

translations.literal: Her mother approved her intent and stopped weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother approved her words and stopped weeping.

sentences.zh: 既見帝，賜號武媚。

translations.literal: Once she saw the emperor, she was given the name Wumei.
translations.idiomatic: When she met the emperor, he gave her the name Wumei.

sentences.zh: 及帝崩，與嬪御皆為比丘尼。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, she and the consorts all became Buddhist nuns.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died, she and the other consorts were made Buddhist nuns.

sentences.zh: 高宗為太子時，入侍，悅之。

translations.literal: When Gaozong was heir apparent he entered to attend her and was pleased with her.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong was crown prince he visited her and was drawn to her.

sentences.zh: 王后後久無子，蕭淑妃方幸，后陰不悅。

translations.literal: Empress Wang had long been without a son; the Cultivated Consort Xiao was then favored, and the empress was secretly displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wang had long been childless; the Cultivated Consort Xiao then held favor, and the empress was secretly displeased.

sentences.zh: 它日，帝過佛廬，才人見且泣，帝感動。

translations.literal: Another day the emperor passed the Buddhist cloister; the Talented Lady saw him and wept, and the emperor was moved.
translations.idiomatic: One day the emperor passed the Buddhist cloister; the Talented Lady saw him and wept, and he was moved.

sentences.zh: 后廉知狀，引內後宮，以撓妃寵。

translations.literal: The empress secretly learned of this and brought her into the inner palace to check the consort's favor.
translations.idiomatic: The empress secretly learned of this and brought her into the inner palace to counter Xiao's favor.

sentences.zh: 才人有權數，詭變不窮。

translations.literal: The Talented Lady had stratagems and endless crafty shifts.
translations.idiomatic: The Talented Lady was resourceful and endlessly cunning.

sentences.zh: 始，下辭降體事后，后喜，數譽於帝，故進為昭儀。

translations.literal: At first she lowered her words and humbled her body before the empress; the empress was pleased and often praised her to the emperor, so she was advanced to Bright Lady.
translations.idiomatic: At first she humbled herself before the empress; the empress was pleased and often praised her to the emperor, and she was advanced to Bright Lady.

sentences.zh: 一旦顧幸在蕭右，寖與后不協。

translations.literal: One day the emperor's favor rested to Xiao's right; gradually she fell out with the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Once the emperor's favor shifted to her side, she gradually fell out with the empress.

sentences.zh: 后性簡重，不曲事上下，而母柳見內人尚宮無浮禮，故昭儀伺后所薄，必款結之，得賜予，盡以分遺。

translations.literal: The empress was by nature plain and grave and did not bend to serve those above and below; her mother Liu saw that the Chief of Palace among the inner attendants had no empty ceremony, so the Bright Lady watched whom the empress slighted and always won them over warmly, giving away all she received in gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was plain and dignified and did not court favor above or below. Her mother Liu noticed that the Chief of Palace scorned empty ceremony, so the Bright Lady cultivated everyone the empress slighted and gave away all her gifts.

sentences.zh: 由是后及妃所為必得，得輒以聞，然未有以中也。

translations.literal: Thus whatever the empress and consort did was always learned; once learned it was reported, yet nothing yet hit the mark.
translations.idiomatic: Thus whatever the empress and Xiao did was reported to her, yet she had found no decisive charge against them.

sentences.zh: 昭儀生女，后就顧弄，去，昭儀潛斃兒衾下，伺帝至，陽為歡言，發衾視兒，死矣。

translations.literal: The Bright Lady bore a daughter; the empress came to look and play with the child, then left. The Bright Lady secretly smothered the infant under the coverlet; when the emperor arrived she feigned cheerful talk, then lifted the coverlet—and the child was dead.
translations.idiomatic: The Bright Lady bore a daughter. The empress came to visit and play with the infant, then left. Wu secretly smothered the child under the coverlet; when the emperor arrived she spoke cheerfully, then lifted the coverlet—and the child was dead.

sentences.zh: 又驚問左右，皆曰：「后適來。

translations.literal: She feigned shock and asked those beside her; all said: "The empress just came."
translations.idiomatic: She feigned shock and asked her attendants; all said, "The empress just came."

sentences.zh: 」昭儀即悲涕，帝不能察，怒曰：「后殺吾女，往與妃相讒媢，今又爾邪！

translations.literal: The Bright Lady at once wept in grief; the emperor could not discern the truth and said in anger: "The empress killed my daughter! Before she slandered the consort with the consort—now again!"
translations.idiomatic: The Bright Lady wept. Unable to see through the ruse, the emperor raged, "The empress killed my daughter! She slandered the consort before—now this again!"

sentences.zh: 」由是昭儀得入其訾，后無以自解，而帝愈信愛，始有廢后意。

translations.literal: Thus the Bright Lady gained entry for her accusations; the empress had no way to clear herself, and the emperor trusted and loved her all the more, beginning to think of deposing the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Wu gained a hold over him; the empress could not defend herself, and the emperor trusted Wu all the more and began to consider deposing the empress.

sentences.zh: 久之，欲進號「宸妃」，侍中韓瑗、中書令來濟言：「妃嬪有數，今別立號，不可。

translations.literal: After some time he wished to advance her title to "Consort of the Inner Chamber." Attendant-in-ordinary Han Yuan and Grand Counselor Lai Ji said: "Consorts and concubines have fixed numbers; to establish a separate title now is not permissible."
translations.idiomatic: After some time he wished to create a new title, Consort of the Inner Chamber. Han Yuan and Lai Ji objected, "Consorts have fixed ranks; a separate title is not permissible."

sentences.zh: 」昭儀乃誣后與母厭勝，帝挾前憾，實其言，將遂廢之。

translations.literal: The Bright Lady then accused the empress and her mother of witchcraft; the emperor, bearing his earlier resentment, credited her words and was about to depose the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Wu then accused the empress and her mother of witchcraft. Bearing his earlier resentment, the emperor believed her and was about to depose the empress.

sentences.zh: 長孫無忌、褚遂良、韓瑗及濟瀕死固爭，帝猶豫；

translations.literal: Zhangsun Wuji, Chu Suiliang, Han Yuan, and Ji argued to the death in firm remonstrance; the emperor hesitated;
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Wuji, Chu Suiliang, Han Yuan, and Ji remonstrated fiercely to the death; the emperor hesitated;

sentences.zh: 而中書舍人李義府、衛尉卿許敬宗素險側，狙勢即表請昭儀為后，帝意決，下詔廢后。

translations.literal: but Secretariat Drafter Li Yifu and Commandant of the Guards Xu Jingzong, by nature treacherous and crafty, watching the trend at once memorialized asking that the Bright Lady be made empress; the emperor's mind was decided, and he issued an edict deposing the empress.
translations.idiomatic: but Li Yifu and Xu Jingzong, men of treacherous character, seized the moment and memorialized to make the Bright Lady empress. The emperor's mind was made up, and he issued an edict deposing the empress.

sentences.zh: 詔李勣、于志寧奉璽綬進昭儀為皇后，命群臣及四夷酋長朝后肅義門，內外命婦入謁。

translations.literal: He ordered Li Ji and Yu Zhining to present the seal and sash and advance the Bright Lady to empress, commanded ministers and chieftains of the four barbarians to attend the empress at Suyi Gate, and inner and outer titled ladies to enter in audience.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Li Ji and Yu Zhining to present the seal and sash and invest the Bright Lady as empress, commanded ministers and foreign chieftains to attend her at Suyi Gate, and required all titled ladies to pay homage.

sentences.zh: 朝皇后自此始。

translations.literal: Court audience for the empress began from this time.
translations.idiomatic: Court audience for the empress began from this time.

sentences.zh: 后見宗廟，再贈士彠至司徒，爵周國公，謚忠孝，配食高祖廟。

translations.literal: The empress appeared at the ancestral temple; Shiyi was twice ennobled posthumously to Minister of Education, enfeoffed as Duke of Zhou with the title Zhongxiao, and given paired sacrifice at Gaozu's temple.
translations.idiomatic: The empress appeared at the ancestral temple. Shiyi was posthumously honored as Minister of Education, enfeoffed as Duke of Zhou with the title Zhongxiao, and given paired sacrifice at Gaozu's temple.

sentences.zh: 母楊，再封代國夫人，家食魏千戶。

translations.literal: Her mother Yang was again enfeoffed as Lady of Dai, and the family received a thousand households' revenue from Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother Yang was again enfeoffed as Lady of Dai, and the family received a thousand households' revenue from Wei.

sentences.zh: 后乃製《外戚誡》獻諸朝，解釋譏譟。

translations.literal: The empress then composed the Admonition on Maternal Kin and presented it to the court to explain away the ridicule and uproar.
translations.idiomatic: The empress then composed the Admonition on Maternal Kin and presented it to the court to answer the criticism.

sentences.zh: 於是逐無忌、遂良，踵死徙，寵煽赫然。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wuji and Suiliang were driven out; one after another died or were exiled, and favor blazed conspicuously.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Wuji and Suiliang were driven out; one after another they died or were exiled, and Wu's power blazed conspicuously.

sentences.zh: 后城宇深，痛柔屈不恥，以就大事，帝謂能奉己，故扳公議立之。

translations.literal: The empress was deep in stratagem; she painfully bent and submitted without shame to achieve her great design. The emperor thought she could serve him, and therefore rallied public opinion to establish her.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was deep in stratagem and endured humiliation without shame to achieve her ends. The emperor thought she would serve him, and therefore rallied public opinion to establish her.

sentences.zh: 已得志，即盜威福，施施無憚避，帝亦懦昏，舉能鉗勒，使不得專，久稍不平。

translations.literal: Once her aim was achieved, she at once usurped authority and favor, proceeding without fear or avoidance. The emperor was also weak and dull; altogether he could clamp and restrain her so she could not monopolize power, but after long time he grew somewhat resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Once she had achieved her aim, she usurped authority without restraint. The emperor was weak and muddled; he could sometimes restrain her from monopolizing power, but in time he grew resentful.

sentences.zh: 麟德初，后召方士郭行真入禁中為蠱祝，宦人王伏勝發之，帝怒，因是召西臺侍郎上官儀，儀指言后專恣，失海內望，不可承宗廟，與帝意合，乃趣使草詔廢之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Linde the empress summoned the adept Guo Xingzhen into the forbidden quarters to perform witchcraft and prayer; the eunuch Wang Fusheng exposed it. The emperor was angry and therefore summoned Western Terrace Vice Director Shangguan Yi; Yi pointed out that the empress was willful and monopolistic, had lost the hope of the realm, and could not inherit the ancestral temples. This matched the emperor's mind, and he hurried him to draft an edict deposing her.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Linde era the empress summoned the adept Guo Xingzhen to perform witchcraft in the inner palace; the eunuch Wang Fusheng exposed it. The emperor was furious and summoned Shangguan Yi, who said the empress was willful, had lost the people's trust, and could not inherit the ancestral temples. The emperor agreed and ordered him to draft an edict deposing her.

sentences.zh: 左右馳告，后遽從帝自訴，帝羞縮，待之如初，猶意其恚，且曰：「是皆上官儀教我！

translations.literal: Those at his side rushed to inform her; the empress hastened to the emperor and pleaded in person. The emperor shrank in shame and treated her as before, still thinking her resentful, and said: "It was all Shangguan Yi who taught me!"
translations.idiomatic: Attendants rushed to inform her; the empress hurried to the emperor and pleaded in person. Ashamed, he treated her as before, still thinking her angry, and said, "It was all Shangguan Yi who put me up to this!"

sentences.zh: 」后諷許敬宗構儀，殺之。

translations.literal: The empress insinuated to Xu Jingzong to frame Yi, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The empress prompted Xu Jingzong to frame Shangguan Yi and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 初，元舅大臣怫旨，不閱歲屠覆，道路目語，及儀見誅，則政歸房帷，天子拱手矣。

translations.literal: At first, maternal uncles and great ministers who defied her will were slaughtered and overthrown within a year; people on the roads exchanged glances. When Yi was executed, government returned to the curtain chamber and the Son of Heaven merely folded his hands.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, maternal uncles and great ministers who crossed her were destroyed within the year; people whispered in the streets. Once Yi was killed, power passed to the inner quarters and the emperor became a figurehead.

sentences.zh: 群臣朝、四方奏章，皆曰「二聖」。

translations.literal: At ministers' audiences and in memorials from all directions, all spoke of "the Two Sages."
translations.idiomatic: At court and in memorials from every quarter, all referred to "the Two Sages."

sentences.zh: 每視朝，殿中垂簾，帝與后偶坐，生殺賞罰惟所命。

translations.literal: Each time they held court, curtains hung in the hall; the emperor and empress sat side by side, and life, death, reward, and punishment were solely at her command.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever they held audience, curtains hung in the hall while emperor and empress sat together; life, death, reward, and punishment were hers alone to decree.

sentences.zh: 當其忍斷，雖甚愛，不少隱也。

translations.literal: When she resolved to be ruthless, even those she greatly loved received no forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Once she set her mind to cruelty, even those she dearly loved won no mercy.

sentences.zh: 帝晚益病風不支，天下事一付后。

translations.literal: In his later years the emperor grew increasingly ill with wind disorder and could not sustain himself; all affairs under Heaven were entrusted to the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong's wind ailment worsened in his later years until he could no longer govern; the empress took charge of all state affairs.

sentences.zh: 后乃更為太平文治事，大集諸儒內禁殿，撰定《列女傳》、《臣軌》、《百僚新誡》、《樂書》等，大氐千餘篇。

translations.literal: The empress then turned to peaceful civil governance, gathering many scholars within the forbidden halls to compile the Biographies of Exemplary Women, Tracks for Ministers, New Admonitions for the Hundred Officials, Book of Music, and the like—altogether more than a thousand chapters.
translations.idiomatic: She then turned to civil administration, gathering scholars inside the palace to compile works such as the Biographies of Exemplary Women, Tracks for Ministers, New Admonitions for Officials, and Book of Music—more than a thousand chapters in all.

sentences.zh: 因令學士密裁可奏議，分宰相權。

translations.literal: She also had academicians secretly review what might be memorialized, dividing the chancellors' authority.
translations.idiomatic: She had palace scholars secretly vet memorials before they reached the throne, thereby splitting the chancellors' power.

sentences.zh: 始，士彠娶相里氏，生子元慶、元爽。

translations.literal: At first Shiyi married the Xiangli clan and had sons Yuangqing and Yuanshuang.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shiyi had first married into the Xiangli clan and fathered Yuangqing and Yuanshuang.

sentences.zh: 又娶楊氏，生三女：伯嫁賀蘭越石，蚤寡，封韓國夫人；

translations.literal: He also married the Yang clan and had three daughters: the eldest married Helan Yueshi, was widowed early, and was enfeoffed Lady of Han;
translations.idiomatic: He also married Lady Yang, who bore three daughters: the eldest married Helan Yueshi, was widowed young, and was enfeoffed as Lady of Han;

sentences.zh: 仲即后；

translations.literal: the second was the empress herself;
translations.idiomatic: the second was the future empress;

sentences.zh: 季嫁郭孝慎，前死。

translations.literal: the youngest married Guo Xiaoshen and had died earlier.
translations.idiomatic: the youngest had married Guo Xiaoshen and died before her.

sentences.zh: 楊以后故，寵日盛，徙封榮國。

translations.literal: Because of the empress, Yang's favor grew daily and her title was moved to Lady of Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to her daughter's position, Lady Yang's favor grew daily and she was promoted to Lady of Rong.

sentences.zh: 始，兄子惟良、懷運與元慶等遇楊及后禮薄，后銜不置。

translations.literal: At first her brother's sons Weiliang and Huaiyun, together with Yuangqing and the others, had treated Yang and the empress with scant courtesy; the empress harbored resentment she could not set aside.
translations.idiomatic: Her brother's sons Weiliang and Huaiyun, along with Yuangqing and the rest, had once slighted Lady Yang and the empress; she never forgot the insult.

sentences.zh: 及是，元慶為宗正少卿，元爽少府少監，惟良司衛少卿，懷運淄州刺史。

translations.literal: By this time Yuangqing was Vice Director of the Imperial Clan, Yuanshuang Vice Director of the Palace Stores, Weiliang Vice Director of the Imperial Guards, and Huaiyun prefect of Zi.
translations.idiomatic: By then Yuangqing was Vice Director of the Imperial Clan, Yuanshuang Vice Director of the Palace Stores, Weiliang Vice Director of the Imperial Guards, and Huaiyun prefect of Zi.

sentences.zh: 它日，夫人置酒，酣，謂惟良曰：「若等記疇日事乎？

translations.literal: One day the Lady set out wine; when drunk she said to Weiliang, "Do you remember affairs of other days?
translations.idiomatic: One day Lady Yang held a feast; when drunk she asked Weiliang, "Do you remember how things used to be?

sentences.zh: 今謂何？

translations.literal: What do you say now?"
translations.idiomatic: What do you say to that now?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「幸以功臣子位朝廷，晚緣戚屬進，憂而不榮也。

translations.literal: He replied, "Fortunate to hold office at court as a meritorious minister's son; advanced late through kinship—I am troubled, not honored."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I am fortunate to hold office as a meritorious minister's son, but to rise late only through kinship fills me with worry rather than pride."

sentences.zh: 」夫人怒，諷后偽為退讓，請惟良等外遷，無示天下私。

translations.literal: The Lady grew angry and prompted the empress to feign yielding, asking that Weiliang and the others be transferred outward so as not to show the realm favoritism.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yang flew into a rage and urged the empress to feign modesty by requesting that Weiliang and the others be posted away, lest the court appear partial.

sentences.zh: 繇是，惟良為始州刺史；

translations.literal: Thereupon Weiliang became prefect of Shizhou;
translations.idiomatic: Weiliang was then made prefect of Shizhou;

sentences.zh: 元慶，龍州；

translations.literal: Yuangqing, Longzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Yuangqing was sent to Longzhou;

sentences.zh: 元爽，濠州，俄坐事死振州。

translations.literal: Yuanshuang, Haozhou—soon he died at Zhenzhou for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshuang to Haozhou—soon he died at Zhenzhou after being charged with a crime.

sentences.zh: 元慶至州，憂死。

translations.literal: Yuangqing reached his prefecture and died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: Yuangqing reached his post and died of grief.

sentences.zh: 韓國出入禁中，一女國姝，帝皆寵之。

translations.literal: The Lady of Han came and went within the forbidden quarters; she had a daughter of surpassing national beauty, and the emperor favored them both.
translations.idiomatic: The Lady of Han moved freely within the inner palace; her daughter was famed as the empire's greatest beauty, and the emperor favored them both.

sentences.zh: 韓國卒，女封魏國夫人，欲以備嬪職，難於后，未決。

translations.literal: When the Lady of Han died, her daughter was enfeoffed Lady of Wei; they wished to make her a concubine, but this was difficult with the empress, so it remained undecided.
translations.idiomatic: After the Lady of Han died, her daughter was enfeoffed as Lady of Wei. The court wished to install her among the concubines, but the empress stood in the way and the matter hung unresolved.

sentences.zh: 后內忌甚，會封泰山，惟良、懷運以嶽牧來集，從還京師，后毒殺魏國，歸罪惟良等，盡殺之，氏曰「蝮」，以韓國子敏之奉士彠祀。

translations.literal: The empress was inwardly intensely jealous. During the Fengshan rites Weiliang and Huaiyun came as territorial governors; returning to the capital with them, she poisoned the Lady of Wei, blamed Weiliang and the others, and killed them all. The clan was called "Viper"; Minzhi, son of the Lady of Han, was made to conduct sacrifice for Shiyi.
translations.idiomatic: The empress burned with jealousy. When Weiliang and Huaiyun came to the capital for the Fengshan ceremony, she poisoned the Lady of Wei on their return, blamed them for the crime, and had the whole clan executed—henceforth called "the Vipers." Only Minzhi, the Lady of Han's son, was spared to tend Wu Shiyi's ancestral rites.

sentences.zh: 初，魏國卒，敏之入弔，帝為慟，敏之哭不對。

translations.literal: When the Lady of Wei first died, Minzhi came to mourn; the emperor was grief-stricken, but Minzhi wept without responding.
translations.idiomatic: When the Lady of Wei died, Minzhi came to mourn. The emperor wept bitterly, but Minzhi made no answering lament.

sentences.zh: 后曰：「兒疑我！

translations.literal: The empress said, "The boy suspects me!"
translations.idiomatic: The empress said, "The boy suspects me!"

sentences.zh: 」惡之。

translations.literal: She hated him.
translations.idiomatic: She came to hate him.

sentences.zh: 俄貶死。

translations.literal: Soon he was demoted and died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was demoted and put to death.

sentences.zh: 楊氏徙酇、衛二國，咸亨元年卒，追封魯國，謚忠烈，詔文武九品以上及五等親與外命婦赴弔，以王禮葬咸陽，給班劍、葆杖、鼓吹。

translations.literal: Yang was moved to the states of Bo and Wei; in the first year of Xianheng she died and was posthumously enfeoffed Lady of Lu with the title Zhonglie. An edict ordered civil and military officials of the ninth rank and above, fifth-rank kin, and outer titled ladies to attend the mourning. She was buried at Xianyang with princely rites, given ceremonial swords, mace-staff, and musical escort.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yang was promoted to Lady of Bo and then Lady of Wei. She died in the first year of Xianheng (670) and was posthumously enfeoffed as Lady of Lu with the posthumous title Zhonglie. An edict required officials of the ninth rank and above, fifth-rank relatives, and titled ladies to attend her funeral. She was buried at Xianyang with princely honors, escorted by ceremonial swords, mace-staffs, and musicians.

sentences.zh: 時天下旱，后偽表求避位，不許。

translations.literal: The realm was drought-stricken; the empress submitted a feigned memorial asking to yield her place, but permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: During a nationwide drought the empress submitted a feigned memorial offering to step down; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 俄又贈士彠太尉兼太子太師、太原郡王，魯國忠烈夫人為妃。
