translations.literal: Soon Shiyi was posthumously made Grand Mentor and concurrently Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and Prince of Taiyuan; the Lady of Lu Zhonglie became his consort.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Wu Shiyi was posthumously honored as Grand Mentor and Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and enfeoffed as Prince of Taiyuan; Lady of Lu Zhonglie was made his consort.

sentences.zh: 上元元年，進號天后，建言十二事：一、勸農桑，薄賦徭；

translations.literal: In the first year of Shangyuan she advanced to the title Heavenly Empress and proposed twelve measures: first, encourage agriculture and sericulture and lighten taxes and corvée;
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shangyuan (674) she took the title Heavenly Empress and proposed twelve reforms: first, promote farming and sericulture and reduce taxes and corvée labor;

sentences.zh: 二、給復三輔地；

translations.literal: second, grant tax relief on lands in the Three Metropolitan Districts;
translations.idiomatic: second, grant tax exemptions on land in the capital region;

sentences.zh: 三、息兵，以道德化天下；

translations.literal: third, cease warfare and transform the realm through moral virtue;
translations.idiomatic: third, halt military campaigns and govern the realm through moral example;

sentences.zh: 四、南北中尚禁浮巧；

translations.literal: fourth, in the northern, southern, and central inner workshops forbid frivolous and ingenious crafts;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, ban extravagant crafts in the imperial workshops of north, south, and center;

sentences.zh: 五、省功費力役；

translations.literal: fifth, reduce public works and corvée labor;
translations.idiomatic: fifth, cut public works and forced labor;

sentences.zh: 六、廣言路；

translations.literal: sixth, broaden channels for remonstrance;
translations.idiomatic: sixth, widen avenues for criticism and counsel;

sentences.zh: 七、杜讒口；

translations.literal: seventh, shut off slanderous tongues;
translations.idiomatic: seventh, suppress malicious slander;

sentences.zh: 八、王公以降皆習《老子》；

translations.literal: eighth, from princes and dukes downward all should study the Laozi;
translations.idiomatic: eighth, require princes, dukes, and all ranks below to study the Laozi;

sentences.zh: 九、父在為母服齊衰三年；

translations.literal: ninth, when the father is alive, observe three years of qi mourning for the mother;
translations.idiomatic: ninth, require three years of qi mourning for the mother even while the father lives;

sentences.zh: 十、上元前勛官已給告身者無追核；

translations.literal: tenth, for merit offices granted patent letters before Shangyuan, do not pursue retroactive verification;
translations.idiomatic: tenth, do not retroactively audit merit offices that received formal patents before Shangyuan;

sentences.zh: 十一、京官八品以上益稟入；

translations.literal: eleventh, increase grain stipends for capital officials of the eighth rank and above;
translations.idiomatic: eleventh, raise grain stipends for capital officials of the eighth rank and above;

sentences.zh: 十二、百官任事久，材高位下者得進階申滯。

translations.literal: twelfth, for officials long in service whose talent outstrips their rank, allow advancement to relieve stagnation.
translations.idiomatic: twelfth, allow long-serving officials of proven ability but low rank to advance and clear backlogs in promotion.

sentences.zh: 帝皆下詔略施行之。

translations.literal: The emperor issued edicts implementing them in summary.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued edicts broadly adopting these proposals.

sentences.zh: 蕭妃女義陽、宣城公主幽掖廷，幾四十不嫁，太子弘言於帝，后怒，酖殺弘。

translations.literal: Consort Xiao's daughters Princesses Yiyang and Xuancheng were confined in the Rear Court; for nearly forty years they went unmarried. Crown Prince Hong spoke to the emperor about it; the empress was angry and poisoned Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Xiao's daughters, Princesses Yiyang and Xuancheng, were shut away in the rear palace and went unmarried for nearly forty years. When Crown Prince Hong pleaded their case to the emperor, the empress flew into a rage and poisoned him.

sentences.zh: 帝將下詔遜位於后，宰相郝處俊固諫，乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to issue an edict yielding the throne to the empress; Chancellor Hao Chujun firmly remonstrated, and he desisted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was about to abdicate in the empress's favor, but Chancellor Hao Chujun remonstrated forcefully and he abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 后欲外示寬裕，劫人心使歸已，即奏言：「今群臣納半俸、百姓計口錢以贍邊兵，恐四方妄商虛實，請一罷之。

translations.literal: The empress wished outwardly to show generosity and compel hearts to turn to her; she memorialized, saying: "Now ministers contribute half their salaries and the people pay poll taxes to support border troops—I fear the four quarters will recklessly trade on false reports of strength or weakness. I ask that these be abolished altogether."
translations.idiomatic: Wanting to appear magnanimous and win popular loyalty, she memorialized: "Ministers now surrender half their salaries and the people pay poll taxes to support frontier troops. I fear distant regions will misread our strength. I ask that both levies be abolished."

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳三年，群臣、蕃夷長朝後於光順門。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yifeng, ministers and chieftains of the barbarians attended audience on the empress at Guangshun Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yifeng (678), ministers and foreign chieftains paid court to the empress at Guangshun Gate.

sentences.zh: 即并州建太原郡王廟。

translations.literal: At once a temple to the Prince of Taiyuan was built in Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: A temple to the Prince of Taiyuan was erected in Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝頭眩不能視，侍醫張文仲、秦鳴鶴曰：「風上逆，砭頭血可愈。

translations.literal: The emperor suffered dizziness and could not see; attending physicians Zhang Wenzhong and Qin Minghe said, "Wind is rising contrary; bleeding the head with a needle can cure it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suffered dizziness and could not see. His physicians Zhang Wenzhong and Qin Minghe said, "Wind is rising in the head; bleeding the scalp with a needle may cure it."

sentences.zh: 」后內幸帝殆，得自專，怒曰：「是可斬，帝體寧刺血處邪？

translations.literal: The empress inwardly rejoiced that the emperor was failing and she could monopolize power; angrily she said, "This man deserves execution—would you pierce the emperor's body with bloodletting?"
translations.idiomatic: Secretly glad that the emperor was failing so she could rule alone, the empress raged: "This man deserves death! Would you pierce the Son of Heaven's flesh?"

sentences.zh: 」醫頓首請命。

translations.literal: The physicians kowtowed begging for their lives.
translations.idiomatic: The physicians kowtowed and begged for their lives.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「醫議疾，烏可罪？

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Physicians discuss illness—how can they be punished?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Physicians speak of sickness—how can they be blamed?

sentences.zh: 且吾眩不可堪，聽為之！

translations.literal: Besides, my dizziness is unbearable; let them do it!"
translations.idiomatic: Besides, my dizziness is unbearable. Let them proceed!"

sentences.zh: 」醫一再刺，帝曰：「吾目明矣！

translations.literal: The physicians pricked again and again; the emperor said, "My eyes are clear!"
translations.idiomatic: The physicians needled him repeatedly. The emperor cried, "I can see clearly!"

sentences.zh: 」言未畢，后簾中再拜謝，曰：「天賜我師！

translations.literal: Before he had finished speaking, from behind the curtain the empress bowed twice in thanks and said, "Heaven has sent me a teacher!"
translations.idiomatic: Before he finished, the empress bowed twice from behind the curtain and said, "Heaven has given me a master physician!"

sentences.zh: 」身負繒寶以賜。

translations.literal: She personally bore silks and treasures to bestow.
translations.idiomatic: She personally presented silks and treasures as reward.

sentences.zh: 帝崩，中宗即位，天后稱皇太后，遺詔軍國大務聽參決。

translations.literal: The emperor died; Zhongzong succeeded; the Heavenly Empress styled herself Empress Dowager; the testamentary edict allowed her to participate in deciding great military and civil affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong died, Zhongzong ascended the throne. Wu Zetian took the title Empress Dowager, and the testamentary edict authorized her to decide major state affairs.

sentences.zh: 嗣聖元年，太后廢帝為廬陵王，自臨朝，以睿宗即帝位。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zongsheng she deposed the emperor as Prince of Luling, herself held court, and installed Ruizong as emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zongsheng (684) she deposed Zhongzong as Prince of Luling, took direct control of government, and installed Ruizong as emperor.

sentences.zh: 后坐武成殿，帝率群臣上號冊。

translations.literal: The empress sat in Wucheng Hall; the emperor led the ministers in presenting the title scroll.
translations.idiomatic: She sat in Wucheng Hall while Ruizong led the ministers in presenting her honorific titles.

sentences.zh: 越三日，太后臨軒，命禮部尚書攝太尉武承嗣、太常卿攝司空王德真冊嗣皇帝。

translations.literal: Three days later the empress dowager held court on the throne; she ordered Minister of Rites acting as Grand Mentor Wu Chengsi and Minister of Ceremonies acting as Minister of Works Wang Dezhen to invest the heir emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later the empress dowager held court and ordered Minister of Rites Wu Chengsi, acting as Grand Mentor, and Minister of Ceremonies Wang Dezhen, acting as Minister of Works, to invest the new emperor.

sentences.zh: 自是太后常御紫宸殿，施慘紫帳臨朝。

translations.literal: From this time the empress dowager regularly held court in Zichen Hall, with a dark purple curtain for audience.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter she regularly held court in Zichen Hall from behind a dark purple curtain.

sentences.zh: 追贈五世祖後魏散騎常侍克己為魯國公，妣裴即其國為夫人；

translations.literal: She posthumously enfeoffed her fifth-generation ancestor Kèjǐ of Northern Wei, Gentleman Attendant at the Imperial Secretariat, as Duke of Lu; his mother Pei was made Lady of that state;
translations.idiomatic: She posthumously enfeoffed her fifth-generation ancestor Kèjǐ, a Northern Wei Gentleman Attendant at the Imperial Secretariat, as Duke of Lu, with his mother Lady Pei as Duchess;

sentences.zh: 高祖齊殷州司馬居常為太尉、北平郡王，妣劉為王妃；

translations.literal: her great-great-grandfather Juchang, Northern Qi Vice Director of Yin Prefecture, as Grand Mentor and Prince of Beiping, his mother Liu as princess consort;
translations.idiomatic: her fourth-generation ancestor Juchang, a Northern Qi vice director, as Grand Mentor and Prince of Beiping, with Lady Liu as princess consort;

sentences.zh: 曾祖永昌王諮議參軍、贈齊州刺史儉為太尉、金城郡王，妣宋為王妃；

translations.literal: her great-grandfather Jian, Consultant of the Prince of Yongchang and posthumous Prefect of Qi, as Grand Mentor and Prince of Jincheng, his mother Song as princess consort;
translations.idiomatic: her third-generation ancestor Jian, consultant to the Prince of Yongchang and posthumous prefect of Qi, as Grand Mentor and Prince of Jincheng, with Lady Song as princess consort;

sentences.zh: 祖隋東郡丞、贈并州刺史、大都督華為太尉、太原郡王，妣趙為王妃。

translations.literal: her grandfather Hua, Sui Vice Prefect of Dong Commandery and posthumous Prefect of Bing and Grand Protector, as Grand Mentor and Prince of Taiyuan, his mother Zhao as princess consort.
translations.idiomatic: her grandfather Hua, a Sui vice prefect and posthumous prefect of Bing, as Grand Mentor and Prince of Taiyuan, with Lady Zhao as princess consort.

sentences.zh: 皆置園邑，戶五十。

translations.literal: For each she established an estate with fifty households.
translations.idiomatic: Each was granted an estate of fifty households.

sentences.zh: 考為太師、魏王，加實戶滿五千，妣為王妃，王園邑守戶百。

translations.literal: Her father was made Grand Preceptor and Prince of Wei, with actual households reaching five thousand; his consort was made princess; the prince's estate had a hundred guardian households.
translations.idiomatic: Her father was honored as Grand Preceptor and Prince of Wei with five thousand actual households; her mother became princess consort, and the princely estate was assigned a hundred guardian households.

sentences.zh: 時睿宗雖立，實囚之，而諸武擅命。

translations.literal: Though Ruizong was established, in fact he was imprisoned, while the various Wus issued commands at will.
translations.idiomatic: Although Ruizong sat on the throne, he was effectively a prisoner while the Wu clan issued orders at will.

sentences.zh: 又謚魯國公曰靖，裴為靖夫人；

translations.literal: She also gave posthumous titles: the Duke of Lu was called Jing, Pei Jing Lady;
translations.idiomatic: She also granted posthumous titles: the Duke of Lu was styled Jing, and Lady Pei Jing;

sentences.zh: 北平郡王曰恭肅，金城郡王曰義康，太原郡王曰安成，妃從夫謚。

translations.literal: the Prince of Beiping Gongsu, the Prince of Jincheng Yikang, the Prince of Taiyuan Ancheng—the consorts following their husbands' titles.
translations.idiomatic: the Prince of Beiping Gongsu, the Prince of Jincheng Yikang, and the Prince of Taiyuan Ancheng—with their consorts taking posthumous titles matching their husbands.

sentences.zh: 太后遣冊武成殿使者告五世廟室。

translations.literal: The empress dowager sent envoys from the investiture at Wucheng Hall to announce to the five-generation temple.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager sent messengers from the Wucheng Hall investiture ceremony to report to the five-generation ancestral shrine.

sentences.zh: 於是柳州司馬李敬業、括蒼令唐之奇、臨海丞駱賓王疾太后脅逐天子，不勝憤，乃募兵殺揚州大都督府長史陳敬之，據州欲迎廬陵王，眾至十萬。

translations.literal: Thereupon Li Jingye, Vice Magistrate of Liuzhou, Tang Zhiqi, Magistrate of Kuocang, and Luo Binwang, Assistant Magistrate of Linhai—unable to bear the empress dowager's coercion of the Son of Heaven—raised troops in fury, killed Chen Jingzhi, Chief Administrator of the Yangzhou Metropolitan Prefecture, seized the prefecture intending to welcome the Prince of Luling, and gathered a force of one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Then Li Jingye of Liuzhou, Tang Zhiqi of Kuocang, and Luo Binwang of Linhai—outraged that the empress dowager had forced aside the legitimate emperor—raised an army, killed Yangzhou's chief administrator Chen Jingzhi, seized the prefecture to restore the Prince of Luling, and mustered a hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 楚州司馬李崇福連和。

translations.literal: Li Chongfu, Vice Magistrate of Chuzhou, joined in alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chongfu, vice magistrate of Chuzhou, joined their cause.

sentences.zh: 盱眙人劉行舉嬰城不肯從，敬業攻之，不克。

translations.literal: Liu Xingju of Xuyi walled his city and refused to submit; Jingye attacked but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xingju of Xuyi shut his city and refused to follow; Jingye besieged him without success.

sentences.zh: 太后拜行舉遊擊將軍，擢其弟行實楚州刺史。

translations.literal: The empress dowager appointed Xingju General of Guerrilla Warfare and promoted his younger brother Xingshi to Prefect of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager named Xingju General of Guerrilla Warfare and promoted his brother Xingshi to prefect of Chu.

sentences.zh: 敬業南度江取潤州，殺刺史李思文，曲阿令尹元貞拒戰死。

translations.literal: Jingye crossed the Yangtze south and seized Runzhou, killing Prefect Li Siwen; Yin Yuanzhen, Magistrate of Qu'e, died resisting in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Jingye crossed the Yangtze, seized Runzhou, and killed Prefect Li Siwen; Magistrate Yin Yuanzhen of Qu'e died fighting in defense.

sentences.zh: 太后詔左玉鈐衛大將軍李孝逸為揚州道行軍大總管，率兵三十萬討之，戰於高郵，前鋒左豹韜果毅成三朗為唐之奇所殺。

translations.literal: The empress dowager ordered Left General of the Jade Bell Guard Li Xiaoyi Grand Commander of the Yangzhou Circuit Army, leading three hundred thousand troops to suppress them; at Gaoyou the vanguard Left Leopard-Tiger Commander Cheng Sanlang was killed by Tang Zhiqi.
translations.idiomatic: She appointed Li Xiaoyi of the Left Jade Bell Guard commander of the Yangzhou expedition with three hundred thousand troops. At Gaoyou the vanguard commander Cheng Sanlang was killed by Tang Zhiqi.

sentences.zh: 又以左鷹揚衛大將軍黑齒常之為江南道行軍大總管，並力。

translations.literal: She also made Left General of the Eagle-Flying Guard Heichi Changzhi Grand Commander of the Jiangnan Circuit Army, joining forces.
translations.idiomatic: She also named Heichi Changzhi of the Left Eagle-Flying Guard commander of the Jiangnan expedition, and the two armies combined.

sentences.zh: 敬業興三月敗，傳首東都，三州平。

translations.literal: Jingye rose in the third month and was defeated; his head was sent to the eastern capital; the three prefectures were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Jingye's rebellion lasted three months before he was crushed; his head was sent to Luoyang and the three prefectures were pacified.

sentences.zh: 始，武承嗣請太后立七廟，中書令裴炎沮止，及敬業之興，下炎獄，殺之，並殺左威衛大將軍程務挺。

translations.literal: At first Wu Chengsi had asked the empress dowager to establish seven temples; Chancellor Pei Yan had obstructed it. When Jingye rose, Yan was thrown into prison and killed, together with Left General of the Majestic Guard Cheng Wuting.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wu Chengsi had urged the empress dowager to establish seven ancestral temples; Chancellor Pei Yan had blocked the plan. When Jingye rebelled, Yan was imprisoned and executed, along with Left General Cheng Wuting.

sentences.zh: 太后方怫恚，一日，召群臣廷讓曰：「朕於天下無負，若等知之乎？

translations.literal: The empress dowager was just appeased of her anger; one day she summoned the ministers to rebuke them in court, saying: "I owe nothing to the realm under Heaven—do you know this?
translations.idiomatic: Still seething, the empress dowager one day summoned the court and demanded: "I owe the empire nothing—do you understand that?

sentences.zh: 」群臣唯唯。

translations.literal: The ministers murmured assent.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers murmured agreement.

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「朕輔先帝逾三十年，憂勞天下。

translations.literal: The empress dowager said: "I assisted the late emperor for more than thirty years, laboring in anxiety for the realm.
translations.idiomatic: She continued: "For more than thirty years I assisted the late emperor, bearing the empire's burdens in my own person.

sentences.zh: 爵位富貴，朕所與也；

translations.literal: Rank, title, wealth, and honor—I am the one who bestowed them;
translations.idiomatic: Your ranks, titles, wealth, and honors—I gave them to you;

sentences.zh: 天下安佚，朕所養也。

translations.literal: the realm's peace and ease—I am the one who nurtured them.
translations.idiomatic: the empire's peace and prosperity—I secured it.

sentences.zh: 先帝棄群臣，以社稷為托，朕不敢愛身，而知愛人。

translations.literal: The late emperor left the ministers and entrusted the altars of state to me; I dare not spare myself and know how to cherish others.
translations.idiomatic: When the late emperor entrusted me with the altars of state, I did not spare myself for your sake.

sentences.zh: 今為戎首者皆將相，何見負之遽？

translations.literal: Now those who lead the rebels are all generals and chancellors—why are you so quick to think me in your debt?
translations.idiomatic: Yet those who now rebel against me are generals and chancellors—why do you rush to think I owe you?

sentences.zh: 且受遺老臣伉扈難制有若裴炎乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, among the old ministers who received the testamentary charge, was there one so arrogant and hard to control as Pei Yan?
translations.idiomatic: Was there among the testamentary ministers anyone so arrogant and ungovernable as Pei Yan?

sentences.zh: 世將種能合亡命若徐敬業乎？

translations.literal: Among hereditary military houses, was there one who could rally fugitives like Xu Jingye?
translations.idiomatic: Among military clans, was there anyone who could rally outlaws as Li Jingye did?

sentences.zh: 宿將善戰若程務挺乎？

translations.literal: Among veteran generals skilled in war, was there one like Cheng Wuting?
translations.idiomatic: Among seasoned commanders, was there anyone as formidable in battle as Cheng Wuting?

sentences.zh: 彼皆人豪，不利於朕，朕能戮之。

translations.literal: They were all formidable men, harmful to me—I could destroy them.
translations.idiomatic: They were all dangerous men who threatened me—and I destroyed them.

sentences.zh: 公等才有過彼，蚤為之。

translations.literal: If your talents surpass theirs, act early.
translations.idiomatic: If any of you surpass them in ability, act now.

sentences.zh: 不然，謹以事朕，無詒天下笑。

translations.literal: If not, serve me diligently and do not invite the realm's laughter.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise serve me faithfully, lest the empire laugh at your folly.

sentences.zh: 」群臣頓首，不敢仰視，曰：「惟陛下命。

translations.literal: The ministers kowtowed, not daring to look up, and said: "We obey Your Majesty's command.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers kowtowed without daring to look up and said, "We obey Your Majesty's command."

sentences.zh: 久之，下詔陽若復辟者。

translations.literal: After long time she issued an edict feigning restoration of the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Before long she issued an edict that pretended to restore imperial authority to the throne.

sentences.zh: 睿宗揣非情，固請臨朝，制可。

translations.literal: Ruizong sensed it was not sincere and firmly requested to hold court; the order was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Ruizong sensed her insincerity and repeatedly asked to govern in person; the order was granted.

sentences.zh: 乃冶銅匭為一室，署東曰「延恩」，受干賞自言；

translations.literal: She then cast a bronze chest as a single chamber; the eastern side was labeled "Extended Grace," to receive self-recommendations seeking reward;
translations.idiomatic: She had a bronze chest cast with four slots: the east, labeled "Extended Grace," received self-recommendations seeking favor;

sentences.zh: 南曰「招諫」，受時政失得；

translations.literal: the southern, "Inviting Remonstrance," to receive gains and losses in current policy;
translations.idiomatic: the south, "Inviting Remonstrance," received criticism of current policy;

sentences.zh: 西曰「申冤」，受抑枉所欲言；

translations.literal: the western, "Pleading Wrongs," to receive what the suppressed and wronged wished to say;
translations.idiomatic: the west, "Pleading Wrongs," received grievances from the oppressed;

sentences.zh: 北曰「通玄」，受讖步秘策。

translations.literal: the northern, "Penetrating Mystery," to receive omens, divination, and secret stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: the north, "Penetrating Mystery," received omens, divination, and secret plots.

sentences.zh: 詔中書門下一官典領。

translations.literal: An edict ordered one official from the Secretariat and Chancellery to oversee it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict assigned a Secretariat-Chancellery official to administer it.

sentences.zh: 太后不惜爵位，以籠四方豪傑自為助，雖妄男子，言有所合，輒不次官之，至不稱職，尋亦廢誅不少縱，務取實材真賢。

translations.literal: The empress dowager did not spare ranks and titles to win heroes from the four quarters as her helpers; even reckless men—if their words suited her—were at once given extraordinary appointments. Even when they proved unfit, she soon dismissed and executed them without much leniency, striving to obtain men of real talent and true worth.
translations.idiomatic: She lavished ranks on talented men from every region to bind them to her cause. Even unworthy adventurers won rapid promotion if they pleased her; when they failed, she removed or executed them without mercy, yet still sought genuine ability.

sentences.zh: 又畏天下有謀反逆者，詔許上變，在所給輕傳，供五品食，送京師，即日召見，厚餌爵賞歆動之。

translations.literal: She also feared that rebels might arise under Heaven; an edict permitted reporting plots. Wherever such reports were made, light post-horses and fifth-rank provisions were supplied, and the informer was sent to the capital, summoned the same day, and richly fed with ranks and rewards to stir them.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing rebellion, she allowed anyone to report conspiracies. Local authorities had to provide swift transport and fifth-rank rations and send informers to the capital for immediate audience, tempting them with lavish rewards.

sentences.zh: 凡言變，吏不得何詰，雖耘夫蕘子必親延見，稟之客館。

translations.literal: For any report of a plot, officials might not interrogate; even plowmen and firewood gatherers were personally received and lodged in guest quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Officials could not question informers. Even farmers and woodcutters were received in person and lodged as guests.

sentences.zh: 敢稽若不送者，以所告罪之。

translations.literal: Those who dared delay or fail to forward reports were punished with the crime reported.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who delayed or refused to forward a report was punished for the alleged crime itself.

sentences.zh: 故上變者遍天下，人人屏息，無敢議。

translations.literal: Thus informers spread throughout the realm; everyone held their breath and none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Informers spread across the empire until everyone fell silent in fear.

sentences.zh: 新豐有山因震突出，太后以為美祥，赦其縣，更名慶山。

translations.literal: In Xinfeng a mountain suddenly thrust forth in an earthquake; the empress dowager took it as an auspicious sign, pardoned the county, and renamed it Celebration Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: When an earthquake thrust up a mountain in Xinfeng, she declared it auspicious, pardoned the county, and renamed it Celebration Mountain.

sentences.zh: 荊人俞文俊上言：「人不和，疣贅生；

translations.literal: Yu Wenjun of Jing submitted a memorial: "When people are not in harmony, warts and excrescences grow;
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wenjun of Jing memorialized: "When people fall out of harmony, excrescences appear on the body;

sentences.zh: 地不和，堆阜出。

translations.literal: when earth is not in harmony, mounds rise up.
translations.idiomatic: when earth falls out of harmony, mounds rise from the ground.

sentences.zh: 今陛下以女主處陽位，山變為災，非慶也。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty, a woman, occupies the yang position; the mountain's change is a calamity, not a celebration."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, a woman, holds the yang position. This mountain is a disaster, not a blessing."

sentences.zh: 」太后怒，投嶺外。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was angry and had him sent beyond the ranges.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, she exiled him beyond the southern frontier.

sentences.zh: 詔毀乾元殿為明堂，以浮屠薛懷義為使督作。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Qianyuan Hall destroyed to build the Bright Hall, with the monk Xue Huaiyi appointed commissioner to supervise construction.
translations.idiomatic: She ordered the Qianyuan Hall demolished to build the Bright Hall and appointed the monk Xue Huaiyi to supervise the work.

sentences.zh: 懷義，鄠人，本馮氏，名小寶，偉岸淫毒，佯狂洛陽市，千金公主嬖之。

translations.literal: Huaiyi was a native of E, originally of the Feng clan, named Xiaobao—huge in stature and licentiously cruel. He feigned madness in the Luoyang markets; the Princess of a Thousand Gold took him as favorite.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiyi, from E, was born Feng Xiaobao—massive and vicious. He played the madman in Luoyang markets until the Princess of a Thousand Gold took him as lover.

sentences.zh: 主上言：「小寶可入侍。

translations.literal: The princess reported upward: "Xiaobao can attend in the inner quarters."
translations.idiomatic: The princess told the empress dowager: "Xiaobao can serve in the inner palace."

sentences.zh: 」后召與私，悅之。

translations.literal: The empress dowager summoned him privately and was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: She summoned him privately and was delighted.

sentences.zh: 欲掩跡，得通籍出入，使祝髮為浮屠，拜白馬寺主。

translations.literal: To conceal the affair she had him registered for palace access, made him tonsured as a monk, and appointed him abbot of White Horse Temple.
translations.idiomatic: To hide the affair she had him tonsured, registered for palace access, and made him abbot of White Horse Temple.

sentences.zh: 詔與太平公主婿薛紹通昭穆，紹父事之。

translations.literal: An edict made him share clan seniority with Princess Taiping's husband Xue Shao; Shao treated him as a father.
translations.idiomatic: An edict linked him by clan rank to Princess Taiping's husband Xue Shao, whom he treated as a son.

sentences.zh: 給廄馬，中官為騶侍，雖承嗣、三思皆尊事惟謹。

translations.literal: Stable horses were given him; eunuchs served as outriders. Even Chengsi and Sansi honored him with utmost deference.
translations.idiomatic: He received imperial horses and eunuch outriders. Even Wu Chengsi and Wu Sansi treated him with exaggerated respect.

sentences.zh: 至是護作，士數萬，巨木率一章千人乃能引。

translations.literal: By this time he supervised construction; tens of thousands of laborers were employed; great timbers generally required a thousand men to move one beam.
translations.idiomatic: He now oversaw construction with tens of thousands of laborers; moving a single great timber required a thousand men.

sentences.zh: 又度明堂後為天堂，鴻麗巖奧次之。

translations.literal: Behind the Bright Hall he also planned Paradise Hall, second only to it in splendor and mystery.
translations.idiomatic: Behind the Bright Hall he built Paradise Hall, nearly as vast and ornate.

sentences.zh: 堂成，拜左威衛大將軍、梁國公。

translations.literal: When the hall was completed, he was made Left General of the Majestic Guard and Duke of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: When the hall was finished, he was made Left General of the Majestic Guard and Duke of Liang.

sentences.zh: 始作崇先廟於西京，享武氏。

translations.literal: She first built the Temple of Honoring Ancestors in the western capital to sacrifice to the Wu clan.
translations.idiomatic: She first built the Temple of Honoring Ancestors in Chang'an for Wu clan sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 承嗣偽款洛水石，導使為帝，遣雍人唐同泰獻之，后號為「寶圖」，擢同泰遊擊將軍。

translations.literal: Chengsi forged an inscription on a Luo River stone to guide people to proclaim her emperor; he sent Yong native Tang Tongtai to present it. She called it the "Treasured Chart" and promoted Tongtai to General of Guerrilla Warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chengsi forged a Luo River stone inscription prophesying her rule and had Tang Tongtai present it. She named it the "Treasured Chart" and promoted Tongtai to General of Guerrilla Warfare.

sentences.zh: 於是汜人又上瑞石，太后乃郊上帝謝況，自號聖母神皇，作神皇璽，改寶圖曰「天授聖圖」，號洛水曰永昌水，圖所曰聖圖泉，勒石洛壇左曰「天授聖圖之表」，改汜水曰廣武。

translations.literal: Thereupon people of Si also presented auspicious stones. The empress dowager then sacrificed to Heaven at the suburbs to give thanks, styled herself Sacred Mother and Divine Sovereign, made the Divine Sovereign seal, changed the Treasured Chart to "Heaven-Bestowed Sacred Chart," named the Luo River the Yongchang River and its source the Sacred Chart Spring, carved stone at the left of the Luo altar reading "Table of the Heaven-Bestowed Sacred Chart," and renamed Si Prefecture Guangwu.
translations.idiomatic: More auspicious stones followed from Si. She sacrificed to Heaven, took the title Sacred Mother and Divine Sovereign, created a new imperial seal, renamed the Treasured Chart the Heaven-Bestowed Sacred Chart, renamed the Luo the Yongchang River, carved a commemorative stone at the Luo altar, and renamed Si as Guangwu.

sentences.zh: 時柄去王室，大臣重將皆撓不得逞，宗室孤外無寄足地。

translations.literal: Power had left the imperial house; great ministers and leading generals were thwarted and could not act; the imperial clan was isolated with nowhere to stand.
translations.idiomatic: Power had drained from the Li house. Great ministers and generals were paralyzed; the imperial clan stood isolated with nowhere to turn.

sentences.zh: 於是，韓王元嘉等謀舉兵唱天下，迎還中宗。

translations.literal: Thereupon Prince of Han Yuangjia and others plotted to raise troops and proclaim throughout the realm, welcoming back Zhongzong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Han Yuangjia and others plotted to raise armies across the empire and restore Zhongzong.

sentences.zh: 瑯邪王沖、越王貞先發，諸王倉卒無應者，遂敗。

translations.literal: Prince of Langye Chong and Prince of Yue Zhen moved first; the other princes had no time to respond and were quickly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Langye Chong and Prince of Yue Zhen rose first, but the other princes could not respond in time and were swiftly crushed.

sentences.zh: 元嘉與魯王靈夔等皆自殺，餘悉坐誅，諸王牽連死滅殆盡，子孫雖嬰褓亦投嶺南。

translations.literal: Yuangjia and Prince of Lu Lingqi and the rest all killed themselves; the remainder were executed in succession. The princes were nearly exterminated in the chain of deaths; even infants in swaddling clothes were sent to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuangjia, Prince of Lu Lingqi, and the rest committed suicide; the others were executed until the imperial princes were nearly annihilated. Even infants were exiled to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 太后身拜洛受圖，天子率太子、群臣、蠻夷以次列，大陳珍禽、奇獸、貢物、鹵簿壇下，禮成去。

translations.literal: The empress dowager in person received the chart at Luo; the Son of Heaven led the crown prince, ministers, and barbarian chiefs in order; rare birds, strange beasts, tribute goods, and ceremonial guards were arrayed below the altar. When the rites were done they departed.
translations.idiomatic: She personally received the chart at the Luo. The emperor led the crown prince, ministers, and foreign chiefs in procession, with exotic tribute and full ceremonial display at the altar. When the rites ended, they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 永昌元年，享萬象神宮，改服袞冕，裯大圭，執鎮圭，睿宗亞獻，太子終獻。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongchang she sacrificed at the Palace of Myriad Images, changed to imperial robes and cap, wore the great jade tablet on her chest, held the stabilizing jade, with Ruizong as secondary offerer and the crown prince as final offerer.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongchang 1 (690) she sacrificed at the Palace of Myriad Images in full imperial regalia, holding the great jade tablets, with Ruizong as secondary offerer and the crown prince as final offerer.

sentences.zh: 合祭天地，五方帝、百神從，以高祖、太宗、高宗配，引魏王士彠從配。

translations.literal: She combined sacrifices to Heaven and Earth; the Five Directional Emperors and the hundred spirits followed; Gaozu, Taizong, and Gaozong were paired; Prince of Wei Shiyi was drawn in as secondary pairing.
translations.idiomatic: She combined sacrifices to Heaven and Earth with the Five Emperors and hundred spirits, pairing Gaozu, Taizong, and Gaozong, and adding Wu Shiyi as secondary spirit.

sentences.zh: 班九條，訓百官。

translations.literal: Nine regulations were promulgated to instruct the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: She issued nine regulations to instruct officials.

sentences.zh: 遂大饗群臣。

translations.literal: Then she gave a great feast to the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Then she feasted the ministers on a grand scale.

sentences.zh: 號士彠周忠孝太皇，楊忠孝太后。

translations.literal: Shiyi was titled Zhou Zhongxiao Grand Emperor; Yang was titled Zhongxiao Grand Empress.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shiyi was titled Zhou Zhongxiao Grand Emperor; Lady Yang was titled Zhongxiao Grand Empress.

sentences.zh: 以文水墓為章德陵，咸陽墓為明義陵。

translations.literal: The tomb at Wenshui was made Zhangde Mausoleum; the tomb at Xianyang was made Mingyi Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: The Wenshui tomb became Zhangde Mausoleum; the Xianyang tomb became Mingyi Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 太原安成王為周安成王，金城郡王為魏義康王，北平郡王為趙肅恭王，魯國公為太原靖王。

translations.literal: Prince of Taiyuan Ancheng became Zhou Prince of Ancheng; Prince of Jincheng Yikang became Wei Prince of Yikang; Prince of Beiping Gongsu became Zhao Prince of Gongsu; Duke of Lu Jing became Taiyuan Prince of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Titles were reshuffled: Taiyuan Prince of Ancheng became Zhou Prince of Ancheng; Jincheng became Wei Prince of Yikang; Beiping became Zhao Prince of Gongsu; Duke of Lu became Taiyuan Prince of Jing.

sentences.zh: 載初中，又享萬象神宮，以太穆、文德二皇后配皇地祗，引周忠孝太后從配。

translations.literal: In the early Zaiwu period she again sacrificed at the Palace of Myriad Images, pairing Grand Empresses Taumu and Wende with Earth, and drawing in Zhou Zhongxiao Grand Empress as secondary pairing.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zaiwu era she sacrificed again at the Palace of Myriad Images, pairing Empresses Taumu and Wende with Earth and adding Zhou Zhongxiao Grand Empress.

sentences.zh: 作曌、𠀑、埊、𡆠、囝、〇、𠺞、𢘑、𡕀、𡔈、𠡦、𠙺十有二文。

translations.literal: She created twelve graphs: Zhao and eleven others, twelve characters in all.
translations.idiomatic: She invented twelve new characters, including Zhao and eleven others, for a total of twelve graphs.

sentences.zh: 太后自名曌。

translations.literal: The empress dowager took Zhao as her personal name.
translations.idiomatic: She took Zhao as her personal name.

sentences.zh: 改詔書為制書。

translations.literal: Edicts were changed to "imperial orders."
translations.idiomatic: Edicts were renamed "imperial orders."

sentences.zh: 以周、漢為二王後，虞、夏、殷後為三恪，除唐屬籍。

translations.literal: Zhou and Han were made the Two Established Houses; Yu, Xia, and Yin descendants were the Three Honored Lines; Tang was removed from the imperial register.
translations.idiomatic: She made Zhou and Han the Two Established Houses, honored Yu, Xia, and Yin as the Three Honored Lines, and struck Tang from the imperial genealogy.

sentences.zh: 拜薛懷義輔國大將軍，封鄂國公，令與群浮屠作《大雲經》，言神皇受命事。

translations.literal: Xue Huaiyi was made Defender-General and Duke of E, and ordered with other monks to compile the Great Cloud Sutra, stating the matter of the Divine Sovereign receiving the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Huaiyi was made Defender-General and Duke of E and ordered to compile the Great Cloud Sutra proclaiming the Divine Sovereign's mandate.

sentences.zh: 春官尚書李思文詭言：「《周書·武成》為篇，辭有『垂拱天下治』，為受命之符。

translations.literal: Minister of Spring Offices Li Siwen deceptively said: "The Zhou Documents chapter 'Completion of War' contains the phrase 'drooping arch, all under Heaven governed'—a token of receiving the mandate."
translations.idiomatic: Li Siwen of the Ministry of Rites claimed the Zhou Documents' "Completion of War" contained the phrase "drooping arch, all under Heaven governed"—a sign of Heaven's mandate.

sentences.zh: 」后喜，皆班示天下，稍圖革命。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was pleased; all were displayed throughout the realm; she gradually plotted revolution.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, she had these omens published empire-wide and moved toward outright revolution.

sentences.zh: 然畏人心不肯附，乃陰忍鷙害，肆斬殺怖天下。

translations.literal: Yet she feared hearts would not willingly attach; she therefore concealed her cruelty and ruthlessly killed to terrify the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing popular resistance, she concealed her intentions while slaughtering freely to terrify the empire.

sentences.zh: 內縱酷吏周興、來俊臣等數十人為爪吻，有不慊若素疑憚者，必危法中之。

translations.literal: Within she unleashed cruel officials Zhou Xing, Lai Junchen, and several dozen others as her claws and teeth; anyone she was not pleased with or had long suspected and feared was inevitably trapped by harsh law.
translations.idiomatic: She unleashed cruel officials such as Zhou Xing and Lai Junchen as her enforcers; anyone she disliked or feared was ensnared by harsh laws.

sentences.zh: 宗姓侯王及它骨鯁臣將相駢頸就鈇，血丹狴戶，家不能自保。

translations.literal: Imperial clansmen, marquises, kings, and other stubborn ministers, generals, and chancellors went neck to neck to the axe; blood reddened the prison gates; families could not protect themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Princes, nobles, and outspoken ministers and generals fell to the executioner's block in droves until prison gates ran red and no family was safe.

sentences.zh: 太后操奩具坐重幃，而國命移矣。

translations.literal: The empress dowager sat behind heavy curtains with her toilet case; the fate of the state had shifted.
translations.idiomatic: She held court from behind heavy curtains with her toilet case at hand—the empire was already hers.

sentences.zh: 御史傅遊藝率關內父老請革命，改帝氏為武。

translations.literal: Censor Fu Youyi led elders of the Guanzhong region to request revolution and change the imperial surname to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Fu Youyi led Guanzhong elders to petition for revolution and the Wu surname.

sentences.zh: 又脅群臣固請，妄言鳳集上陽宮，赤雀見朝堂。

translations.literal: She also coerced the ministers to press firmly, falsely claiming phoenixes gathered at Shangyang Palace and red sparrows appeared in the court hall.
translations.idiomatic: She coerced ministers to insist further, falsely reporting phoenixes at Shangyang Palace and red sparrows in the audience hall.

sentences.zh: 天子不自安，亦請氏武，示一尊。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven was ill at ease himself and also requested the Wu surname to show unity.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor himself, uneasy on the throne, also petitioned to take the Wu surname to show unity.

sentences.zh: 太后知威柄在己，因大赦天下，改國號周，自稱聖神皇帝，旗幟尚赤，以皇帝為皇嗣。

translations.literal: The empress dowager knew power was in her hands; she therefore proclaimed a great amnesty, changed the dynastic title to Zhou, styled herself Sacred and Divine Emperor, made banners red, and made the emperor her imperial heir.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing power was hers, she proclaimed a great amnesty, changed the dynastic name to Zhou, took the title Sacred and Divine Emperor, adopted red banners, and made the emperor her heir.

sentences.zh: 立武氏七廟於神都。

translations.literal: She established seven Wu temples in the divine capital.
translations.idiomatic: She established seven Wu ancestral temples in the divine capital.

sentences.zh: 尊周文王為文皇帝，號始祖，妣姒曰文定皇后；

translations.literal: King Wen of Zhou was honored as Literary Emperor, styled Primordial Ancestor; his mother Si was titled Literary and Settled Empress;
translations.idiomatic: King Wen of Zhou was honored as Literary Emperor, Primordial Ancestor, with Lady Si as Literary and Settled Empress;

sentences.zh: 武王為康皇帝，號睿祖，妣姜曰康惠皇后；

translations.literal: King Wu as Kang Emperor, styled Sagacious Ancestor; his mother Jiang as Kang and Kind Empress;
translations.idiomatic: King Wu as Kang Emperor, Sagacious Ancestor, with Lady Jiang as Kang and Kind Empress;

sentences.zh: 太原靖王為成皇帝，號嚴祖，妣曰成莊皇后；

translations.literal: Taiyuan Prince of Jing as Cheng Emperor, styled Stern Ancestor; his consort as Cheng and Solemn Empress;
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan Prince of Jing as Cheng Emperor, Stern Ancestor, with his consort as Cheng and Solemn Empress;

sentences.zh: 趙肅恭王為章敬皇帝，號肅祖，妣曰章敬皇后；

translations.literal: Zhao Prince of Gongsu as Zhangjing Emperor, styled Solemn Ancestor; his consort as Zhangjing Empress;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Prince of Gongsu as Zhangjing Emperor, Solemn Ancestor, with his consort as Zhangjing Empress;

sentences.zh: 魏義康王為昭安皇帝，號烈祖，妣曰昭安皇后；

translations.literal: Wei Prince of Yikang as Zhao'an Emperor, styled Fiery Ancestor; his consort as Zhao'an Empress;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Prince of Yikang as Zhao'an Emperor, Fiery Ancestor, with his consort as Zhao'an Empress;

sentences.zh: 祖周安成王為文穆皇帝，號顯祖，妣曰文穆皇后；

translations.literal: Grandfather Zhou Prince of Ancheng as Wenmu Emperor, styled Luminous Ancestor; his consort as Wenmu Empress;
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Zhou Prince of Ancheng as Wenmu Emperor, Luminous Ancestor, with his consort as Wenmu Empress;

sentences.zh: 考忠孝太皇為孝明高皇帝，號太祖，妣曰孝明高皇后。

translations.literal: Father Zhongxiao Grand Emperor as Xiaoming Gao Emperor, styled Grand Ancestor; his consort as Xiaoming Gao Empress.
translations.idiomatic: Father Zhongxiao Grand Emperor as Xiaoming Gao Emperor, Grand Ancestor, with his consort as Xiaoming Gao Empress.

sentences.zh: 罷唐廟為享德廟，四時祠高祖以下三室，餘廢不享。

translations.literal: Tang temples were abolished and made the Temple of Honored Virtue; the three chambers below Gaozu were sacrificed to in the four seasons; the rest were abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Tang temples became the Temple of Honored Virtue, sacrificing only Gaozu and two others seasonally; the rest were abandoned.

sentences.zh: 至日，祀上帝萬象神宮，以始祖及考妣配，以百神從祀。

translations.literal: On the winter solstice she sacrificed to God at the Palace of Myriad Images, pairing the primordial ancestor and her parents, with the hundred spirits following.
translations.idiomatic: On the winter solstice she sacrificed to Heaven at the Palace of Myriad Images, pairing her earliest ancestors and parents, with the hundred spirits in attendance.

sentences.zh: 盡王諸武。

translations.literal: All the Wus were enfeoffed as kings.
translations.idiomatic: Every member of the Wu clan was enfeoffed as prince.

sentences.zh: 詔并州文水縣為武興，比漢豐、沛，百姓世給復。

translations.literal: An edict made Wenshui County in Bingzhou Wuxing, comparable to Han's Feng and Pei, with the people granted perpetual tax relief for generations.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshui County in Bingzhou was made Wuxing, like Han's Feng and Pei, with perpetual tax exemptions for its people.

sentences.zh: 以始祖冢為德陵，睿祖為喬陵，嚴祖為節陵，肅祖為簡陵，烈祖為靖陵，顯祖為永陵，章德陵為昊陵，明義陵為順陵。

translations.literal: The primordial ancestor's tomb was made Virtue Mausoleum; the sagacious ancestor's Qiao Mausoleum; the stern ancestor's Festival Mausoleum; the solemn ancestor's Simple Mausoleum; the fiery ancestor's Tranquil Mausoleum; the luminous ancestor's Eternal Mausoleum; Zhangde Mausoleum became Bright Mausoleum; Mingyi Mausoleum became Compliant Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Ancestral tombs were renamed: Virtue, Qiao, Festival, Simple, Tranquil, and Eternal mausoleums for successive ancestors; Zhangde became Bright Mausoleum and Mingyi became Compliant Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 太皇雖春秋高，善自塗澤，雖左右不悟其衰。

translations.literal: Though the Grand Empress was advanced in years, she was skilled at cosmetics; even those at her side did not perceive her decline.
translations.idiomatic: Though advanced in age, she painted and dressed with such skill that even attendants did not notice her decline.

sentences.zh: 俄而二齒生，下詔改元為長壽。

translations.literal: Soon two teeth grew anew; an edict changed the era name to Longevity.
translations.idiomatic: When two new teeth appeared, she changed the era name to Longevity.

sentences.zh: 明年，享神宮，自製大樂，舞工用九百人，以武承嗣為亞獻，三思為終獻。

translations.literal: The next year she sacrificed at the divine palace, composed great music herself, used nine hundred dancers, with Wu Chengsi as secondary offerer and Sansi as final offerer.
translations.idiomatic: The next year she sacrificed at the divine palace with music of her own composition, nine hundred dancers, Wu Chengsi as secondary offerer, and Sansi as final offerer.

sentences.zh: 帝之為皇嗣，公卿往往見之，會尚方監裴匪躬、左衛大將軍阿史那元慶、白澗府果毅薛大信、監門衛大將軍范雲仙潛謁帝，皆腰斬都市，自是公卿不復上謁。

translations.literal: When the emperor was heir, ministers often saw him. On one occasion Director of the Palace Workshops Pei Feigong, Left General Ashina Yuanqing, Baidian Commander Xue Daxin, and General of the Gate Guards Fan Yunxian secretly visited the emperor—all were cut in two at the waist in the market. From this ministers no longer paid court.
translations.idiomatic: While he was heir apparent, ministers still sometimes saw him—until Pei Feigong, Ashina Yuanqing, Xue Daxin, and Fan Yunxian visited him secretly and were all executed in the market. Thereafter no minister dared visit him.

sentences.zh: 有上封事言嶺南流人謀反者，太后遣攝右臺監察御史萬國俊就按，得實即論決。

translations.literal: A sealed memorial said exiles in Lingnan plotted rebellion; the empress dowager sent Acting Censor of the Right Platform Wan Guojun to investigate, with authority to decide and execute on the spot if true.
translations.idiomatic: When a memorial claimed Lingnan exiles were plotting rebellion, she sent Wan Guojun of the Right Censorate to investigate with power to execute immediately.

sentences.zh: 國俊至廣州，盡召流人，矯詔賜自盡，皆號哭不服，國俊驅之水曲，使不得逃，一日戮三百餘人。

translations.literal: Guojun reached Guangzhou, summoned all exiles, forged an edict ordering suicide. All wept and refused; Guojun drove them to a bend in the river so they could not escape and in one day slaughtered more than three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: At Guangzhou he summoned all exiles and forged an edict ordering suicide. When they refused, he drove them to a river bend and killed more than three hundred in a day.

sentences.zh: 乃誣奏流人怨望，請悉除之。

translations.literal: He then falsely memorialized that the exiles harbored resentment and asked that they all be eliminated.
translations.idiomatic: He then falsely reported that the exiles were resentful and asked that all be eliminated.

sentences.zh: 於是太后遣右衛翊府兵曹參軍劉光業、司刑評事王德壽、苑南面監丞鮑思恭、尚輦直長王大貞、右武衛兵曹參軍屈貞筠，皆攝監察御史，分往劍南、黔中、安南等六道訊鞫，而擢國俊左臺侍御史。

translations.literal: The empress dowager then sent Right Guard Aide Liu Guangye, Judicial Reviewer Wang Deshou, Southern Park Supervisor Bao Sigong, Palace Chariot Chief Wang Dazhen, and Right Martial Guard Aide Qu Zhenyun—all acting censors—to six circuits including Jiannan, Qianzhong, and Annan to interrogate, while promoting Guojun to Left Platform Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: She then sent Liu Guangye, Wang Deshou, Bao Sigong, Wang Dazhen, and Qu Zhenyun as acting censors to six circuits including Jiannan and Annan, while promoting Guojun.

sentences.zh: 光業等亦希功於上，惟恐殺人之少。

translations.literal: Guangye and the rest also sought merit from above and feared only that they had killed too few.
translations.idiomatic: They too sought credit and feared only that their body counts were too low.

sentences.zh: 光業殺者九百人，德壽殺七百人，其餘亦不減五百人。

translations.literal: Guangye killed nine hundred; Deshou seven hundred; the rest no fewer than five hundred each.
translations.idiomatic: Guangye killed nine hundred; Deshou seven hundred; the others at least five hundred each.

sentences.zh: 太后久乃知其冤，詔六道使所殺者還其家。

translations.literal: After long time the empress dowager knew of the injustice and ordered those killed by the six-circuit envoys restored to their families.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually she learned of the injustice and ordered the victims' families compensated.

sentences.zh: 國俊等亦相踵而死，皆見有物為厲云。

translations.literal: Guojun and the rest also died one after another; all were said to have seen apparitions tormenting them.
translations.idiomatic: Guojun and the others died in succession, reportedly haunted by their victims.

sentences.zh: 太后又自加號金輪聖神皇帝，置七寶於廷：曰金輪寶，曰白象寶，曰女寶，曰馬寶，曰珠寶，曰主兵臣寶，曰主藏臣寶，率大朝會則陳之。

translations.literal: The empress dowager also added to her title Golden-Wheel Sacred and Divine Emperor and set seven treasures in the hall: called Golden Wheel Treasure, White Elephant Treasure, Woman Treasure, Horse Treasure, Pearl Treasure, Minister-of-Arms Treasure, and Minister-of-Treasury Treasure—displayed at great court assemblies.
translations.idiomatic: She added Golden-Wheel Sacred and Divine Emperor to her titles and placed seven treasures in the hall—Golden Wheel, White Elephant, Woman, Horse, Pearl, Minister of Arms, and Minister of Treasury—displayed at major audiences.

sentences.zh: 又尊其顯祖為立極文穆皇帝，太祖為無上孝明皇帝。

translations.literal: She also honored her luminous ancestor as Establishing-Pole Literary and Mu Emperor and her grand ancestor as Unsurpassed Xiaoming Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: She further elevated her luminous ancestor to Establishing-Pole Literary and Mu Emperor and her grand ancestor to Unsurpassed Xiaoming Emperor.

sentences.zh: 延載二年，武三思率蕃夷諸酋及耆老請作天樞，紀太后功德，以黜唐興周，制可。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yanzai, Wu Sansi led barbarian chiefs and elders to request construction of the Heaven Axis commemorating the empress dowager's merit, to displace Tang and exalt Zhou; the order was approved.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanzai 2 (695) Wu Sansi led foreign chiefs and elders to petition for a Heaven Axis commemorating her merit and exalting Zhou over Tang; the order was granted.

sentences.zh: 使納言姚璹護作。

translations.literal: She made Censor-in-Chief Yao Shuang superintendent of construction.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Yao Shuang supervised construction.

sentences.zh: 乃大裒銅鐵合冶之，署曰「大周萬國頌德天樞」，置端門外。

translations.literal: Great quantities of copper and iron were gathered and smelted together; it was titled "Great Zhou Ten-Thousand States Praising Virtue Heaven Axis" and placed outside Duan Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Vast stores of copper and iron were smelted into the "Great Zhou Ten-Thousand States Praising Virtue Heaven Axis," erected outside Duan Gate.

sentences.zh: 其制若柱，度高一百五尺，八面，面別五尺，冶鐵象山為之趾，負以銅龍，石鑱怪獸環之。

translations.literal: Its form was like a pillar, one hundred fifty feet high, eight faces, each face five feet wide; iron cast like a mountain formed the base, borne on bronze dragons, with stone-carved strange beasts encircling it.
translations.idiomatic: Shaped like a pillar one hundred fifty feet tall and eight-sided, with an iron mountain base borne by bronze dragons and ringed with carved stone beasts.

sentences.zh: 柱顛為雲蓋，出大珠，高丈，圍三之。

translations.literal: The pillar top was a cloud canopy issuing a great pearl one zhang high, circumference three times that.
translations.idiomatic: Its summit was a cloud canopy holding a great pearl one zhang high and three zhang around.

sentences.zh: 作四蛟，度丈二尺，以承珠。

translations.literal: Four hornless dragons, one zhang two feet in measure, bore the pearl.
translations.idiomatic: Four hornless dragons twelve feet long supported the pearl.

sentences.zh: 其趾山周百七十尺，度二丈。

translations.literal: The mountain base was one hundred seventy feet in circumference, two zhang in measure.
translations.idiomatic: The base mountain measured one hundred seventy feet around and two zhang high.

sentences.zh: 無慮用銅鐵二百萬斤。

translations.literal: Altogether no less than two million jin of copper and iron were used.
translations.idiomatic: It consumed no less than two million jin of copper and iron.

sentences.zh: 乃悉鏤群臣、蕃酋名氏其上。

translations.literal: Then the names of all ministers and barbarian chiefs were carved upon it.
translations.idiomatic: The names of all ministers and foreign chiefs were carved upon it.

sentences.zh: 薛懷義寵稍衰，而御醫沈南璆進，懷義大望，因火明堂，太后羞之，掩不發。

translations.literal: Xue Huaiyi's favor gradually waned while Palace Physician Shen Nanqiu advanced; Huaiyi was deeply resentful and set fire to the Bright Hall. The empress dowager was shamed and concealed the matter without publicizing it.
translations.idiomatic: As Huaiyi's favor faded and Palace Physician Shen Nanqiu rose, Huaiyi burned the Bright Hall in rage. Ashamed, she concealed the arson.

sentences.zh: 懷義愈很恣怏怏。

translations.literal: Huaiyi grew ever more fierce and sullen.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiyi grew ever more violent and resentful.

sentences.zh: 乃密詔太平公主擇健婦縛之殿中，命建昌王武攸寧、將作大匠宗晉卿率壯士擊殺之，以畚車載屍還白馬寺。

translations.literal: She secretly ordered Princess Taiping to choose strong women to bind him in the hall, commanded Prince of Jianchang Wu Youning and Master of Works Zong Jinqing to lead stalwarts to beat him to death, and had his corpse carried back to White Horse Temple in a dustpan cart.
translations.idiomatic: She secretly ordered Princess Taiping's strong women to bind him in the hall, had Wu Youning and Zong Jinqing beat him to death, and carted his corpse back to White Horse Temple.

sentences.zh: 懷義負幸昵，氣蓋一時，出百官上，其徒多犯法。

translations.literal: Huaiyi, relying on favor, was intimate and overbearing; his arrogance covered an age; he stood above the hundred officials, and his followers often broke the law.
translations.idiomatic: In his heyday Huaiyi rode favor to insolence, towering over officials while his followers broke laws with impunity.

sentences.zh: 御史馮思勖劾其姦，懷義怒，遇諸道，命左右歐之，幾死，弗敢言。

translations.literal: Censor Feng Sijun impeached him for debauchery; Huaiyi was angry, met him on the road, and ordered attendants to beat him nearly to death—he dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: When Censor Feng Sijun impeached him for debauchery, Huaiyi had attendants beat him nearly to death on the road; Feng dared not report it.

sentences.zh: 默啜犯塞，拜新平、伐逆、朔方道大總管，提十八將軍兵擊胡，宰相李昭德、蘇味道至為之長史、司馬。

translations.literal: Mohechuo raided the frontier; Huaiyi was made Grand Commander of the Xinping, Fani, and Shuofang circuits, leading eighteen generals' troops against the barbarians; Chancellors Li Zhaode and Su Weidao even served as his chief administrator and aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Mohechuo raided the frontier, Huaiyi was made grand commander of three circuits with eighteen generals under him; even Chancellors Li Zhaode and Su Weidao served as his staff officers.

sentences.zh: 後猒入禁中，陰募力少年千人為浮屠，有逆謀。

translations.literal: Later he grew weary of entering the inner palace, secretly recruited a thousand strong youths as monks, and had treasonous designs.
translations.idiomatic: Later, weary of the inner palace, he secretly recruited a thousand strong youths as monks and plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 侍御史周矩劾狀請治驗，太后曰：「第出，朕將使詣獄。

translations.literal: Attending censor Zhou Ju impeached him and requested investigation; the empress dowager said, "Just go out—I will have him sent to prison."
translations.idiomatic: Attending Censor Zhou Ju memorialized for investigation. The empress dowager said, "Go—I will have him sent to prison."

sentences.zh: 」矩坐臺，少選，懷義怒馬造廷，直往坐大榻上，矩召吏受辭，懷義即乘馬去。

translations.literal: Ju sat at the bureau; after a short while Huaiyi came furiously on horseback to the court, went straight to sit on the great couch. Ju summoned clerks to take his statement; Huaiyi at once rode away.
translations.idiomatic: Ju was at his desk when Huaiyi galloped into court and seated himself on the great couch. Ju called clerks to take his statement; Huaiyi rode off immediately.

sentences.zh: 矩以聞，太后曰：「是道人素狂，不足治，力少年聽窮劾。

translations.literal: Ju reported it; the empress dowager said, "This Daoist has always been wild—not worth prosecuting. You strong youths may exhaust yourselves impeaching."
translations.idiomatic: Ju reported the incident. She replied, "This monk has always been mad—not worth punishing. You young men may wear yourselves out with impeachments."

sentences.zh: 」矩悉投放醜裔。

translations.literal: Ju had them all sent to the remote borderlands.
translations.idiomatic: Ju had them all exiled to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 懷義構矩，俄免官。

translations.literal: Huaiyi framed Ju; soon Ju was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiyi framed Ju, who was soon dismissed.

sentences.zh: 太后祀天南郊，以文王、武王、士彠與唐高祖並配。

translations.literal: The empress dowager sacrificed to Heaven at the southern suburb, pairing King Wen, King Wu, and Shiyi with Tang Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: She sacrificed to Heaven at the southern suburb, pairing King Wen, King Wu, and Wu Shiyi with Tang Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 太后加號天冊金輪聖神皇帝。

translations.literal: The empress dowager added the title Heaven-Register Golden-Wheel Sacred and Divine Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: She added the title Heaven-Register Golden-Wheel Sacred and Divine Emperor.

sentences.zh: 遂封嵩山，禪少室，冊山之神為帝，配為后。

translations.literal: Then she performed feng on Mount Song and shan on Lesser Room, enfeoffing the mountain spirit as emperor and pairing a consort as empress.
translations.idiomatic: She performed feng on Mount Song and shan on Lesser Room, enfeoffing the mountain spirit as emperor with a consort as empress.

sentences.zh: 封壇南有大槲，赦日置雞其杪，賜號「金雞樹」。

translations.literal: South of the altar was a great catalpa; on the day of amnesty a cock was placed on its top and the tree was given the name "Golden Cock Tree."
translations.idiomatic: South of the altar stood a great catalpa; on amnesty day a cock was placed atop it and the tree was named the Golden Cock Tree.

sentences.zh: 自制《升中述志》，刻石示後。

translations.literal: She herself composed "Ascending the Center and Stating My Will" and carved stone to show posterity.
translations.idiomatic: She composed "Ascending the Center and Stating My Will" and had it carved in stone for posterity.

sentences.zh: 改明堂為通天宮，鑄九州鼎，各位其方，列廷中。

translations.literal: The Bright Hall was changed to Palace of Reaching Heaven; the Nine Provinces cauldrons were cast, each placed in its direction and arrayed in the court.
translations.idiomatic: The Bright Hall was renamed Palace of Reaching Heaven; the Nine Provinces cauldrons were cast and arrayed in the hall by direction.

sentences.zh: 又斂天下黃金作大儀鐘，不克。

translations.literal: She also gathered gold from the realm to make a great ceremonial bell but could not complete it.
translations.idiomatic: She also collected gold empire-wide for a great ceremonial bell but failed to finish it.

sentences.zh: 久之，以崇先廟為崇尊廟，禮視太廟，旋復崇尊廟為太廟。

translations.literal: After long time the Temple of Honoring Ancestors was made the Temple of Honored Reverence, with rites like the Grand Temple; soon the Temple of Honored Reverence was restored as the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: The Temple of Honoring Ancestors became the Temple of Honored Reverence with Grand Temple rites, then was restored as the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 自懷義死，張易之、昌宗得幸，乃置控鶴府，有監，有丞及主簿、錄事等，監三品，以易之為之。

translations.literal: After Huaiyi's death, Zhang Yizhi and Changzong won favor; she then established the Crane-Controlling Office with a director, vice directors, chief clerk, recorder, and the like—the director being third rank, with Yizhi in the post.
translations.idiomatic: After Huaiyi died, Zhang Yizhi and Changzong won favor. She established the Crane-Controlling Office with Zhang Yizhi as third-rank director.

sentences.zh: 太后自見諸武王非天下意，前此中宗自房州還，復為皇太子，恐百歲後為唐宗室躪藉無死所，即引諸武及相王、太平公主誓明堂，告天地，為鐵券使藏史館。

translations.literal: The empress dowager herself saw that the various Wus were not the will of the realm; earlier Zhongzong had returned from Fang Prefecture and been made crown prince again. Fearing that after a hundred years the Tang imperial clan would be trampled with nowhere to die, she led the Wus together with the Prince of Xiang and Princess Taiping to swear at the Bright Hall, inform Heaven and Earth, and made iron covenant documents stored in the History Office.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that the Wu clan lacked popular support, and fearing the Li house would be destroyed after her death, she led the Wus, Prince of Xiang, and Princess Taiping to swear at the Bright Hall before Heaven and Earth and deposited iron covenants in the History Office.

sentences.zh: 改昊陵署為攀龍臺。

translations.literal: Bright Mausoleum office was changed to Dragon-Ascending Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: The Bright Mausoleum office was renamed Dragon-Ascending Terrace.

sentences.zh: 久視初，以控鶴監為天驥府，又改奉宸府，罷監為令，以左右控鶴為奉宸大夫，易之復為令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Long Vision the Crane-Controlling Office became Heavenly Steed Office, then Serving-the-Palace Office; the director was abolished for a commandant, with left and right Crane-Controllers as Serving-the-Palace Grand Masters; Yizhi again became commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Long Vision (700) the Crane-Controlling Office became the Serving-the-Palace Office; Yizhi again headed it.

sentences.zh: 神龍元年，太后有疾，久不平，居迎仙院。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shenlong the empress dowager was ill for long without recovery and dwelt in Welcome-Immortals Court.
translations.idiomatic: In Shenlong 1 (705) she fell gravely ill and remained in Welcome-Immortals Court.

sentences.zh: 宰相張柬之與崔玄暐等建策，請中宗以兵入誅易之、昌宗，於是羽林將軍李多祚等帥兵自玄武門入，斬二張於院左。

translations.literal: Chancellor Zhang Jianzhi with Cui Xuanwei and others devised a plan asking Zhongzong to enter with troops and execute Yizhi and Changzong. Thereupon General of the Feathered Forest Li Duozuo and others led troops through the Xuanwu Gate and beheaded the two Zhangs at the left of the court.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Zhang Jianzhi and Cui Xuanwei persuaded Zhongzong to enter with troops. General Li Duozuo led soldiers through Xuanwu Gate and beheaded the Zhang brothers beside the court.

sentences.zh: 太后聞變而起，桓彥範進請傳位，太后返臥，不復語。

translations.literal: The empress dowager heard the disturbance and rose; Huan Yanfan advanced to request the transfer of power; the empress dowager returned to lie down and spoke no more.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the uproar, she rose; Huan Yanfan asked her to yield power. She lay down again and said nothing more.

sentences.zh: 中宗於是復即位。

translations.literal: Zhongzong thereupon resumed the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong thereupon resumed the throne.

sentences.zh: 徙太后上陽宮，帝率百官詣觀風殿問起居，後率十日一詣宮，俄朝朔、望。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was moved to Shangyang Palace; the emperor led the hundred officials to Wind-Viewing Hall to inquire after her health. Later she came to the palace every ten days; soon she attended on the first and fifteenth.
translations.idiomatic: She was moved to Shangyang Palace. The emperor led officials to Wind-Viewing Hall to inquire after her; later she visited every ten days, then on the first and fifteenth of each month.

sentences.zh: 廢奉宸府官，選東都武氏廟於崇尊廟，更號崇恩，復唐宗廟。

translations.literal: Serving-the-Palace offices were abolished; the eastern capital Wu temple was chosen over the Temple of Honored Reverence, renamed Temple of Honored Grace, and Tang ancestral temples were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Serving-the-Palace offices were abolished; the Wu temple was renamed Temple of Honored Grace and Tang ancestral temples restored.

sentences.zh: 諸武王者咸降爵。

translations.literal: All who had been enfeoffed kings among the Wus had their ranks reduced.
translations.idiomatic: All Wu princes were demoted.

sentences.zh: 是歲，后崩，年八十一。

translations.literal: That year the empress dowager died, aged eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: That year she died at eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 遺制稱則天大聖皇太后，去帝號。

translations.literal: Her testament styled her Zetian Grand Sacred Empress Dowager and removed the imperial title.
translations.idiomatic: Her testament styled her Zetian Grand Sacred Empress Dowager and dropped the imperial title.

sentences.zh: 謚曰則天大聖后，祔乾陵。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Zetian Grand Sacred Empress; she was paired at Qian Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: She was posthumously titled Zetian Grand Sacred Empress and paired at Qianling.

sentences.zh: 會武三思蒸韋庶人，復用事。

translations.literal: When Wu Sansi debauched Consort Wei and again held power,
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sansi debauched Consort Wei and regained power,

sentences.zh: 於是大旱，祈陵輒雨。

translations.literal: there was great drought; praying at her mausoleum brought rain at once.
translations.idiomatic: a great drought ended as soon as prayers were offered at her tomb.

sentences.zh: 三思訹帝詔崇恩廟祠如太廟，齋郎用五品子。

translations.literal: Sansi induced the emperor to decree that the Temple of Honored Grace be sacrificed to like the Grand Temple, with ritual officers drawn from fifth-rank sons.
translations.idiomatic: Sansi induced the emperor to decree Temple of Honored Grace sacrifices equal to the Grand Temple, with fifth-rank sons as ritual officers.

sentences.zh: 博士楊孚言：「太廟諸郎取七品子，今崇恩取五品，不可。

translations.literal: Erudite Yang Fu said: "Grand Temple ritual officers take seventh-rank sons; now Honored Grace takes fifth-rank—this cannot be."
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Yang Fu objected: "Grand Temple officers use seventh-rank sons; Honored Grace cannot use fifth."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「太廟如崇恩可乎？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Can the Grand Temple be like Honored Grace?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Can the Grand Temple match Honored Grace?"

sentences.zh: 」孚曰：「崇恩太廟之私，以臣準君則僭，以君準臣則惑。

translations.literal: Fu said: "Honored Grace is private to the Grand Temple; measured by subject against ruler it is usurpation; measured by ruler against subject it is confusion."
translations.idiomatic: Fu replied: "Honored Grace is the Grand Temple's private shrine—to compare subject with ruler is usurpation; to compare ruler with subject is confusion."

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: Thereupon it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 及韋、武黨誅，詔則天大聖皇后復號天后，廢崇恩廟及陵。

translations.literal: When the Wei and Wu factions were executed, an edict restored the title Heavenly Empress for Zetian Grand Sacred Empress and abolished the Temple of Honored Grace and its mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei and Wu factions were destroyed, an edict restored the title Heavenly Empress and abolished the Temple of Honored Grace.

sentences.zh: 景雲元年，號大聖天后。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingyun she was titled Grand Sacred Heavenly Empress.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingyun 1 (710) she was titled Grand Sacred Heavenly Empress.

sentences.zh: 太平公主奸政，請復二陵官，又尊后曰天后聖帝，俄號聖后。

translations.literal: Princess Taiping perverted government and requested restoration of the two mausoleum offices; she also honored the empress as Heavenly Empress Sacred Emperor; soon Sacred Empress.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Taiping, corrupting government, restored the two mausoleum offices and briefly titled her Sacred Emperor, then Sacred Empress.

sentences.zh: 太平誅，詔黜周孝明皇帝號，復為太原郡王，后為妃，罷昊、順等陵。

translations.literal: When Taiping was executed, an edict removed Zhou Xiaoming Emperor's title and restored Taiyuan Prince, the empress as consort, and abolished Bright and Compliant mausoleums.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiping was executed, Zhou Xiaoming Emperor's title was removed, Taiyuan Prince restored, and Bright and Compliant mausoleums abolished.

sentences.zh: 開元四年，追號則天皇后。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaiyuan she was posthumously titled Empress Zetian.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 4 (716) she was posthumously titled Empress Zetian.

sentences.zh: 太常卿姜晈建言：「則天皇后配高宗廟，主題天后聖帝，非是，請易題為則天皇后武氏。

translations.literal: Minister of Ceremonies Jiang Jiao memorialized: "Empress Zetian paired at Gaozong's temple with the tablet title Sacred Emperor Heavenly Empress is incorrect; please change the tablet to Empress Zetian of the Wu clan."
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Ceremonies Jiang Jiao urged changing her temple tablet from Sacred Emperor Heavenly Empress to Empress Zetian of the Wu clan.

sentences.zh: 」制可。

translations.literal: The order was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The order was approved.

sentences.zh: 中宗和思趙皇后中宗和思順聖皇后趙氏，京兆長安人。

translations.literal: Empress Heosi of Zhongzong—Empress Heosi Shunsheng of the Zhao clan—was a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Heosi Shunsheng Zhao of Zhongzong was from Chang'an in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 祖綽，武德中，戰有功，終右領軍將軍。

translations.literal: Her grandfather Chuo had merit in battle in the Wude era and ended as General of the Right Insignia Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Her grandfather Chuo fought with merit in the Wude era and rose to General of the Right Insignia Guard.

sentences.zh: 父瓌，尚高祖常樂公主。

translations.literal: Her father Gui married Emperor Gaozu's daughter Princess Changle.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Gui married Emperor Gaozu's daughter Princess Changle.

sentences.zh: 帝為英王，聘后為妃。

translations.literal: When the emperor was Prince of Ying he betrothed the empress as consort.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong was Prince of Ying, she became his consort.

sentences.zh: 高宗於公主恩尤隆。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong's favor for the princess was especially abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong favored Princess Changle especially.

sentences.zh: 武后不喜，乃幽妃內侍省。

translations.literal: Empress Wu disliked this; she confined the consort in the Palace Domestic Service.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu disliked her and confined her in the Palace Domestic Service.

sentences.zh: 瓌自定州刺史、駙馬都尉貶括州，絕主朝謁，隨瓌之官。

translations.literal: Gui was demoted from Prefect of Dingzhou and Commandant of the Horse Guards to Kuozhou; audiences with the princess were cut off; she followed Gui to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was demoted from Dingzhou prefect and Commandant of Horse Guards to Kuozhou; the princess could no longer attend court, and the consort followed Gui.

sentences.zh: 妃既囚，扃鍵牢謹，日給飼料。

translations.literal: Once the consort was imprisoned, bolts and locks were strict; daily fodder was supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Imprisoned, she was locked under strict guard with daily rations supplied.

sentences.zh: 衛者候其突煙數日不出，披戶視之，死腐矣，瓌以壽州刺史與主預越王事，死。

translations.literal: Guards waited several days without smoke from her cooking fire, broke open the door and looked—she had rotted dead. Gui died with the princess in the Prince of Yue affair as Prefect of Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guards noticed no cooking smoke for days; opening the door they found her rotted corpse. Gui died with the princess in the Prince of Yue affair as Shouzhou prefect.

sentences.zh: 神龍元年，追謚妃曰恭皇后，贈瓌左衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shenlong the consort was posthumously titled Respectful Empress; Gui was posthumously made Left General of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Shenlong 1 (705) she was posthumously titled Respectful Empress; Gui was made Left General of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 中宗崩，蕆陵事，韋庶人不臣，不得祔，有司加上尊謚，以后祔定陵。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong died and Ding Mausoleum affairs were arranged, Consort Wei was disloyal and could not be paired; the relevant offices added honorific posthumous titles and paired the empress at Ding Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhongzong's burial Consort Wei was too disloyal to be paired; offices added honorific titles and paired the empress at Dingling.

sentences.zh: 中宗韋皇后中宗庶人韋氏，京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: Empress Wei of Zhongzong—Commoner Wei of Zhongzong—was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wei of Zhongzong, née Wei, was from Wannian in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 祖弘表，貞觀中曹王府典軍。

translations.literal: Her grandfather Hongbiao was Army Aide of Prince Cao's household in the Zhenguan era.
translations.idiomatic: Her grandfather Hongbiao was an army aide in Prince Cao's household under Zhenguan.

sentences.zh: 帝在東宮，后被選為妃。

translations.literal: When the emperor was crown prince she was chosen as consort.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong was crown prince she was chosen as his consort.

sentences.zh: 嗣聖初，立為皇后。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zongsheng she was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zongsheng (684) she was made empress.

sentences.zh: 俄與帝處房陵，每使至，帝輒恐，欲自殺。

translations.literal: Soon she dwelt with the emperor at Fang Prefecture; whenever messengers arrived the emperor was afraid and wanted to kill himself.
translations.idiomatic: Soon she joined him in exile at Fang Prefecture; whenever messengers arrived he feared for his life and wanted suicide.

sentences.zh: 後止曰：「禍福何常，早晚等死耳，無遽！

translations.literal: The empress stopped him, saying: "Fortune and calamity have no constancy—sooner or later death is the same; do not hurry!"
translations.idiomatic: She stopped him: "Fortune and disaster are alike—death comes soon or late alike. Do not rush!"

sentences.zh: 」及帝復即位，后居中宮。

translations.literal: When the emperor again took the throne the empress occupied the central palace.
translations.idiomatic: When he regained the throne she occupied the central palace.

sentences.zh: 是時，上官昭容與政事，方敬暉等將盡誅諸武，武三思懼，乃因昭容入請，得幸於后，卒謀暉等誅之。

translations.literal: At this time Shangguan Zhaorong shared in government; Fang Jinghui and others were about to execute all the Wus; Wu Sansi was afraid and therefore entered through Zhaorong to win the empress's favor, and finally plotted Jinghui's execution.
translations.idiomatic: Shangguan Zhaorong held power; Fang Jinghui planned to destroy the Wu clan. Wu Sansi, terrified, won the empress through Zhaorong and had Jinghui executed.

sentences.zh: 初，帝幽廢，與后約：「一朝見天日，不相制。

translations.literal: At first when the emperor was deposed he agreed with the empress: "Once we see the light of day again, we will not restrain each other."
translations.idiomatic: During exile they had agreed: "Once restored, neither will control the other."

sentences.zh: 」至是與三思升御床博戲，帝從旁典籌，不為忤。

translations.literal: By now he gambled on the imperial couch with Sansi while the empress joined; the emperor kept score at their side and showed no offense.
translations.idiomatic: Now he gambled with Sansi on the imperial couch while the empress joined in; he kept score and showed no displeasure.

sentences.zh: 三思諷群臣上后號為順天皇后。

translations.literal: Sansi induced the ministers to petition for the empress the title Heaven-Compliant Empress.
translations.idiomatic: Sansi induced ministers to petition for the title Heaven-Compliant Empress.

sentences.zh: 乃親謁宗廟，贈父玄貞上洛郡王。

translations.literal: She then personally visited the ancestral temple and posthumously enfeoffed her father Xuanzhen as Prince of Shangluo.
translations.idiomatic: She visited the ancestral temple and posthumously enfeoffed her father Xuanzhen as Prince of Shangluo.

sentences.zh: 左拾遺賈虛己建言：「非李氏王者，盟書共棄之。

translations.literal: Remonstrance Officer Jia Xuji memorialized: "For non-Li kings, the covenant text says all shall abandon them together.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Officer Jia Xuji warned: "The iron covenant says all shall abandon any non-Li king.

sentences.zh: 今復國未幾，遽私后家，且先朝禍鑒未遠，甚可懼也。

translations.literal: The state has barely been restored; to favor the empress's family so hastily—and the recent court disaster is not far—this is greatly to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty has barely been restored; to favor the empress's clan so soon, with recent disasters still fresh, is terrifying.

sentences.zh: 如今皇后固辭，使天下知後宮謙讓，不亦善乎？

translations.literal: If now the empress firmly declines, letting the realm know the inner palace's modesty—would that not be good?"
translations.idiomatic: If the empress firmly declines, showing the inner palace's modesty—would that not be wise?"

sentences.zh: 」不聽。

translations.literal: He was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: He was ignored.

sentences.zh: 神龍三年，節愍太子舉兵敗。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shenlong the Indignant Crown Prince raised troops and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In Shenlong 3 (707) the Indignant Crown Prince's rebellion failed.

sentences.zh: 宗楚客率群臣請加號「翊聖」，詔可。

translations.literal: Zong Chuke led the ministers to request adding the title "Assisting Sage"; the edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Chuke led ministers to add the title Assisting Sage; the edict approved.

sentences.zh: 禁中謬傳有五色雲起后衣笥，帝圖以示諸朝，因大赦天下，賜百官母、妻封號。

translations.literal: In the palace a false report spread of five-colored clouds rising from the empress's clothes chest; the emperor drew it to show the court and proclaimed a great amnesty, bestowing titles on officials' mothers and wives.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors spread of five-colored clouds rising from her wardrobe; the emperor displayed it at court, proclaimed amnesty, and bestowed titles on officials' mothers and wives.

sentences.zh: 太史迦葉志忠表上《桑條歌》十二篇，言后當受命，曰：「昔高祖時，天下歌《桃李》；

translations.literal: Grand Astrologer Ye Zhizhong submitted the twelve chapters of "Mulberry Branch Song," saying the empress was to receive the mandate: "In Gaozu's time the realm sang 'Peach and Plum';
translations.idiomatic: Grand Astrologer Ye Zhizhong submitted twelve "Mulberry Branch Songs" prophesying her mandate: "Under Gaozu the realm sang 'Peach and Plum';

sentences.zh: 太宗時，歌《秦王破陣》；

translations.literal: in Taizong's time, 'Breaking the Enemy Array of the Prince of Qin';
translations.idiomatic: under Taizong, 'Breaking the Enemy Array';

sentences.zh: 高宗歌《堂堂》；

translations.literal: in Gaozong's time, 'Lofty and Grand';
translations.idiomatic: under Gaozong, 'Lofty and Grand';

sentences.zh: 天后世，歌《武媚娘》；

translations.literal: in the Heavenly Empress's age, 'Lady Wu Meiniang';
translations.idiomatic: under the Heavenly Empress, 'Lady Wu Meiniang';

sentences.zh: 皇帝受命，歌《英王石州》；

translations.literal: when the emperor received the mandate, 'Stone Prefecture of Prince Ying';
translations.idiomatic: when the emperor received the mandate, 'Stone Prefecture of Prince Ying';

sentences.zh: 后今受命，歌《桑條韋》，蓋后妃之德專蠶桑，共宗廟事也。

translations.literal: now that the empress receives the mandate, 'Mulberry Branch Wei'—for the empress's virtue lies in sericulture alone, sharing in ancestral temple affairs."
translations.idiomatic: now the empress receives the mandate, 'Mulberry Branch Wei'—for her virtue is sericulture and ancestral rites."

sentences.zh: 」乃賜志忠第一區，綵七百段。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhizhong was given a first-rank residence and seven hundred bolts of colored silk.
