translations.idiomatic: Zhizhong received a first-rank residence and seven hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 太常少卿鄭愔因之被樂府。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Ceremonies Zheng Yin thereby entered the Music Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Zheng Yin entered the Music Bureau through this.

sentences.zh: 楚客又諷補闕趙延禧離釋《桑條》為九十八代，帝大喜，擢延禧諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Chuke also induced Remonstrance Officer Zhao Yanxi to interpret "Mulberry Branch" as ninety-eight generations; the emperor was greatly pleased and promoted Yanxi to Remonstrance Officer.
translations.idiomatic: Chuke had Zhao Yanxi interpret the song as ninety-eight generations; delighted, the emperor promoted him to Remonstrance Officer.

sentences.zh: 於是昭容以武氏事動后。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhaorong moved the empress with Wu clan affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaorong then pressed Wu clan interests on the empress.

sentences.zh: 即表增出母服；

translations.literal: She memorialized at once to extend mourning for mothers;
translations.idiomatic: She memorialized to extend mourning for mothers;

sentences.zh: 民以二十三為丁，限五十九免；

translations.literal: the people take twenty-three as adult age and are exempt at fifty-nine;
translations.idiomatic: set adult age at twenty-three and tax exemption at fifty-nine;

sentences.zh: 五品而上母、妻不繇夫、子封者，喪得用鼓吹。

translations.literal: for fifth-rank and above whose mothers and wives do not receive titles through husbands or sons, funerals may use musical escort.
translations.idiomatic: allowed fifth-rank officials' mothers and wives funeral musical escort even without titles through husbands or sons.

sentences.zh: 數改制度，陰儲人望。

translations.literal: Regulations were changed several times to store up popular esteem in secret.
translations.idiomatic: She changed regulations repeatedly to win popular favor.

sentences.zh: 稍寵樹親屬，封拜之。

translations.literal: She gradually favored and enfeoffed kin.
translations.idiomatic: She gradually favored and enfeoffed relatives.

sentences.zh: 昭容與母及尚宮賀婁等多受金錢。

translations.literal: Zhaorong with her mother and Senior Palace Attendant He Lou and others received much gold.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaorong, her mother, and Senior Palace Attendant He Lou accepted large bribes.

sentences.zh: 封巫趙隴西夫人，出入禁中，勢與上官埒。

translations.literal: The shaman Zhao was enfeoffed Lady of Longxi; entering and leaving the forbidden quarters, her power rivaled Shangguan's.
translations.idiomatic: Shaman Zhao was enfeoffed Lady of Longxi and moved freely in the palace with power rivaling Shangguan's.

sentences.zh: 繇是墨敕斜封出矣。

translations.literal: From this black-edict appointments issued at a slant.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth appointments came through slanted-seal edicts.

sentences.zh: 三年，帝親郊，引后亞獻。

translations.literal: In the third year the emperor sacrificed at the suburban altar and led the empress as secondary offerer.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the emperor sacrificed at the suburbs with the empress as secondary offerer.

sentences.zh: 明年，正月望夜，帝與后微服過市，彷徉觀覽，縱宮女出遊，皆淫奔不還。

translations.literal: The next year, on the first full moon night, the emperor and empress went in plain dress through the markets, strolling to view sights; palace women were released to roam—all ran off in debauchery and did not return.
translations.idiomatic: The next Lantern Night the emperor and empress went abroad in disguise; palace women released to roam never returned.

sentences.zh: 國子祭酒葉靜能善禁架，常侍馬秦客高醫，光祿少卿楊均善烹調，皆引入後廷。

translations.literal: Libationer Ye Jingneng was skilled in forbidden arts; Regular Attendant Ma Qinke was a fine physician; Vice Director of the Palace Provision Yang Jun was skilled in cooking—all were brought into the rear court.
translations.idiomatic: Libationer Ye Jingneng knew forbidden arts; Ma Qinke was a fine physician; Yang Jun was a skilled cook—all entered the rear court.

sentences.zh: 均、秦客蒸於后，嘗喪免，不歷旬輒起。

translations.literal: Jun and Qinke debauched the empress; even when mourning ended they were raised within ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Jun and Qinke debauched her; even after mourning they were restored within ten days.

sentences.zh: 帝遇弒，議者讙咎秦客及安樂公主。

translations.literal: When the emperor met assassination, critics blamed Qinke and Princess Anle.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was assassinated, critics blamed Qinke and Princess Anle.

sentences.zh: 后大懼，引所親議計，乃以刑部尚書裴談、工部尚書張錫輔政，留守東都，詔將軍趙承福、薛簡以兵五百衛譙王重福，與兄溫定策，立溫王重茂為皇太子，列府兵五萬分二營屯京師，然後發喪。

translations.literal: The empress was greatly afraid and gathered intimates to plot; she made Minister of Punishments Pei Tan and Minister of Works Zhang Xi auxiliary ministers, left to guard the eastern capital, ordered Generals Zhao Chenfu and Xue Jian with five hundred troops to guard Prince Chongfu of Qiao, and with her brother Wen settled on establishing Wen's son Chongmao as crown prince, divided fifty thousand garrison troops into two camps at the capital, then announced the death.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, she made Pei Tan and Zhang Xi regents, stationed troops to guard Prince Chongfu, and with her brother Wen planned to install Chongmao as heir before announcing the death.

sentences.zh: 太子即位，是為殤帝。

translations.literal: The crown prince succeeded—the Shang Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince succeeded as the Shang Emperor.

sentences.zh: 皇太后臨朝，溫總內外兵，檢護宮省。

translations.literal: The empress dowager held court; Wen controlled inner and outer troops and inspected the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager ruled; Wen controlled troops and inspected the palace.

sentences.zh: 族弟濯、播，宗子捷、璿，璿甥高崇及武延秀，分領左右屯營、羽林、飛騎、萬騎。

translations.literal: Clan younger brothers Zhuo and Bo, clan sons Jie and Xuan, Xuan's nephew Gao Chong and Wu Yanxiu, each commanded left and right encampments, Feathered Forest, Flying Cavalry, and Ten Thousand Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Relatives Zhuo, Bo, Jie, Xuan, Gao Chong, and Wu Yanxiu each commanded encampments and guards.

sentences.zh: 京師大恐，傳言且革命。

translations.literal: The capital was greatly afraid; rumors spread of imminent revolution.
translations.idiomatic: The capital panicked; rumors spread of revolution.

sentences.zh: 播、璿入軍中，鞭督萬騎欲立威，士怨不為用。

translations.literal: Bo and Xuan entered the army, whipping and urging the Ten Thousand Cavalry to establish authority; the soldiers resented it and would not serve.
translations.idiomatic: Bo and Xuan entered camp, lashing the Ten Thousand Cavalry to assert authority; the soldiers resented them and refused to obey.

sentences.zh: 俄而臨淄王引兵夜披玄武門入羽林，殺璿、播、崇於寢，斧關叩太極殿，后遁入飛騎營，為亂兵所殺。

translations.literal: Soon the Prince of Linzi led troops by night, broke through Xuanwu Gate into the Feathered Forest, killed Xuan, Bo, and Chong in their quarters, axed the gate and knocked at Taiji Hall; the empress fled into the Flying Cavalry camp and was killed by mutinous soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Prince of Linzi Li Longji led troops through Xuanwu Gate at night, killed Xuan, Bo, and Chong, and stormed Taiji Hall. The empress fled to the Flying Cavalry camp and was killed by mutineers.

sentences.zh: 斬延秀、安樂公主。

translations.literal: Yanxiu and Princess Anle were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yanxiu and Princess Anle were beheaded.

sentences.zh: 分捕諸韋、諸武與其支黨，悉誅之，梟后及安樂首東市。

translations.literal: All Weis and Wus and their branches were hunted and executed; the empress's and Anle's heads were displayed at the eastern market.
translations.idiomatic: All Wei and Wu kin and followers were hunted down and executed; the empress's and Anle's heads were displayed at the eastern market.

sentences.zh: 翌日，追貶為庶人，葬以一品禮。

translations.literal: The next day she was posthumously demoted to commoner and buried with first-rank rites.
translations.idiomatic: The next day she was posthumously demoted to commoner and buried with first-rank honors.

sentences.zh: 上官昭容上官昭容者，名婉兒，西臺侍郎儀之孫。

translations.literal: Shangguan Zhaorong—named Wan'er—was granddaughter of Western Terrace Vice Director Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Shangguan Zhaorong, named Wan'er, was granddaughter of Vice Director Shangguan Yi.

sentences.zh: 父廷芝，與儀死武后時。

translations.literal: Her father Tingzhi died with Yi in Empress Wu's time.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Tingzhi died with Yi during Empress Wu's reign.

sentences.zh: 母鄭，太常少卿休遠之姊。

translations.literal: Her mother Zheng was younger sister of Vice Minister of Ceremonies Xiuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother Zheng was sister of Vice Minister of Ceremonies Zheng Xiuyuan.

sentences.zh: 婉兒始生，與母配掖廷。

translations.literal: When Wan'er was born she and her mother were assigned to the Rear Court.
translations.idiomatic: At birth she and her mother were assigned to the Rear Court.

sentences.zh: 天性韶警，善文章。

translations.literal: By nature she was graceful and alert, skilled in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Naturally graceful and quick-witted, she excelled at writing.

sentences.zh: 年十四，武后召見，有所制作，若素構。

translations.literal: At fourteen Empress Wu summoned her; whatever she composed seemed pre-arranged.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen Empress Wu summoned her; whatever she wrote seemed effortless.

sentences.zh: 自通天以來，內掌詔命，掞麗可觀。

translations.literal: From the Tongtian era onward she managed edicts within the palace—brilliant and splendid to view.
translations.idiomatic: From the Tongtian era she drafted palace edicts of brilliant polish.

sentences.zh: 嘗忤旨當誅，後惜其才，止黥而不殺也。

translations.literal: Once she offended and was to be executed; the empress dowager prized her talent and only tattooed her face without killing her.
translations.idiomatic: Once she offended and faced execution; Empress Wu spared her for her talent and only tattooed her face.

sentences.zh: 然群臣奏議及天下事皆與之。

translations.literal: Yet ministers' memorials and all affairs under Heaven passed through her.
translations.idiomatic: Yet all ministerial memorials and state affairs passed through her hands.

sentences.zh: 帝即位，大被信任，進拜昭容，封鄭沛國夫人。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne she was greatly trusted, advanced to Bright Lady, and enfeoffed Lady of Zheng and Pei.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong took the throne she won great trust, was made Bright Lady, and enfeoffed Lady of Zheng and Pei.

sentences.zh: 婉兒通武三思，故詔書推右武氏，抑唐家，節愍太子不平。

translations.literal: Wan'er was intimate with Wu Sansi; therefore edicts favored the Wu clan and suppressed the Tang house; the Indignant Crown Prince was resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Intimate with Wu Sansi, she drafted edicts favoring the Wu clan over the Tang; the Indignant Crown Prince grew resentful.

sentences.zh: 及舉兵，叩肅章門索婉兒，婉兒曰：「我死，當次索皇后、大家矣！

translations.literal: When he raised troops he knocked at Suyi Gate demanding Wan'er; Wan'er said: "If I die, next they will demand the empress and Her Majesty!"
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince rebelled he demanded Wan'er at Suyi Gate. She cried, "If I die, next they will demand the empress and Her Majesty!"

sentences.zh: 」以激怒帝，帝與后挾婉兒登玄武門避之。

translations.literal: to enrage the emperor; the emperor and empress took Wan'er up Xuanwu Gate to escape.
translations.idiomatic: Enraging the emperor, who fled with the empress and Wan'er to Xuanwu Gate.

sentences.zh: 會太子敗，乃免。

translations.literal: When the crown prince was defeated she was spared.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince failed she was spared.

sentences.zh: 婉兒勸帝侈大書館，增學士員，引大臣名儒充選。

translations.literal: Wan'er urged the emperor to expand the Academy and increase academicians, drawing famous ministers and great scholars as selections.
translations.idiomatic: She urged expanding the Academy, increasing scholars, and appointing eminent ministers and Confucians.

sentences.zh: 數賜宴賦詩，群臣賡和，婉兒常代帝及后、長寧安樂二主，眾篇並作，而采麗益新。

translations.literal: Feasts with poetry were often bestowed; ministers answered in turn; Wan'er often composed in place of the emperor, empress, and Princesses Changning and Anle—all pieces together, and the literary color grew ever fresher.
translations.idiomatic: At imperial poetry feasts she often composed for the emperor, empress, and Princesses Changning and Anle, setting a brilliant court fashion.

sentences.zh: 又差第群臣所賦，賜金爵，故朝廷靡然成風。

translations.literal: She also ranked ministers' compositions and bestowed gold cups; thus the court became wholly devoted to the trend.
translations.idiomatic: She ranked ministers' poems and bestowed gold cups, making poetry the court fashion.

sentences.zh: 當時屬辭者，大抵雖浮靡，然所得皆有可觀，婉兒力也。

translations.literal: Writers of the time, though mostly florid, yet produced work worth viewing—Wan'er's doing.
translations.idiomatic: Though court writing grew florid, much remained worth reading—thanks to Wan'er.

sentences.zh: 鄭卒，謚節義夫人。

translations.literal: When Zheng died she was posthumously titled Lady of Chaste Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng died she received the posthumous title Lady of Chaste Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 婉兒請降秩行服，詔起為婕妤，俄還昭容。

translations.literal: Wan'er asked to lower her rank to observe mourning; an edict raised her to Fair Lady; soon she returned to Bright Lady.
translations.idiomatic: Wan'er asked to lower rank for mourning; an edict made her Fair Lady, then soon restored her as Bright Lady.

sentences.zh: 帝即婉兒居穿沼築巖，窮飾勝趣，即引侍臣宴其所。

translations.literal: The emperor at Wan'er's residence dug a pond and built rockeries, exhausting decorative splendor, and led attending ministers to feast there.
translations.idiomatic: At her residence the emperor dug ponds and built rockeries of extravagant beauty and held feasts for ministers there.

sentences.zh: 是時，左右內職皆聽出外，不何止。

translations.literal: At this time inner attendants of left and right were all permitted to go outside without restriction.
translations.idiomatic: Inner attendants were then permitted to leave the palace freely.

sentences.zh: 婉兒與近嬖至皆營外宅，衺人穢夫爭候門下，肆狎昵，因以求劇職要官。

translations.literal: Wan'er and close favorites all maintained outer residences; debauched men and corrupt husbands vied at their gates with intimate familiarity, seeking important offices thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Wan'er and favorites kept outer residences where corrupt men vied for favor to win high office.

sentences.zh: 與崔湜亂，遂引知政事。

translations.literal: She debauched with Cui Shi and therefore introduced him to know government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: She debauched with Cui Shi and brought him into government.

sentences.zh: 湜開商山道，未半，因帝遺制，虛列其功，加甄賞。

translations.literal: Shi opened the Shangshan road; halfway through, exploiting the emperor's testamentary edict, he falsely listed merit and received enhanced reward.
translations.idiomatic: Shi opened the Shangshan road; exploiting the testamentary edict he falsely claimed merit and was richly rewarded.

sentences.zh: 韋后之敗，斬闕下。

translations.literal: At Empress Wei's defeat he was beheaded below the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wei fell he was beheaded at the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 初，鄭方妊，夢巨人畀大稱曰：「持此稱量天下。

translations.literal: At first when Zheng was pregnant she dreamed a giant gave her a great steelyard saying: "With this weigh all under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: While pregnant Zheng dreamed a giant gave her a steelyard saying, "Weigh all under Heaven with this."

sentences.zh: 」婉兒生逾月，母戲曰：「稱量者豈爾邪？

translations.literal: When Wan'er was over a month old her mother jested: "Can the weigher be you?"
translations.idiomatic: When Wan'er was a month old her mother jested, "Can the weigher be you?"

sentences.zh: 」輒啞然應。

translations.literal: She at once responded intelligibly.
translations.idiomatic: The infant responded intelligibly.

sentences.zh: 後內秉機政，符其夢云。

translations.literal: Later holding power within, it matched her dream.
translations.idiomatic: Later wielding inner power, she fulfilled the dream.

sentences.zh: 景雲中，追復昭容，謚惠文。

translations.literal: In Jingyun she was posthumously restored as Bright Lady with posthumous title Huiven.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingyun (710) she was posthumously restored as Bright Lady with title Huiven.

sentences.zh: 始，從母子王昱為拾遺，昱戒曰：「上往囚房陵，武氏得志矣，卒而中興，天命所在，不可幸也。

translations.literal: At first her cousin Wang Yu was Remonstrance Officer; Yu admonished: "When the emperor was imprisoned at Fang Prefecture the Wu clan had their way, yet at last there was restoration—the mandate of Heaven is fixed; one must not presume.
translations.idiomatic: Her cousin Wang Yu warned her: "When Zhongzong was exiled the Wu clan ruled, yet Heaven restored the Tang. Do not presume on fortune.

sentences.zh: 三思雖乘釁，天下知必敗，今昭容上所信，而附之，且滅族！

translations.literal: Though Sansi seized the moment, all under Heaven knew he must fail; now Zhaorong is trusted by the emperor yet attached to him—you will destroy your clan!"
translations.idiomatic: Sansi's rise was fleeting and doomed. You are trusted yet cling to him—you will destroy your clan!"

sentences.zh: 」鄭以責婉兒，不從。

translations.literal: Zheng reproached Wan'er; she would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng reproached her; she would not listen.

sentences.zh: 節愍誅三思，果索之，始憂懼。

translations.literal: When the Indignant Prince executed Sansi he indeed sought her; she first grew fearful.
translations.idiomatic: When the Indignant Prince killed Sansi he sought her too; she grew fearful.

sentences.zh: 及草遺制，即引相王輔政。

translations.literal: When drafting the testamentary edict she at once brought in the Prince of Xiang as regent.
translations.idiomatic: Drafting the testamentary edict she named the Prince of Xiang regent.

sentences.zh: 臨淄王兵起，被收。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Linzi's troops rose she was seized.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Linzi's troops rose she was seized.

sentences.zh: 婉兒以詔草示劉幽求，幽求言之王，王不許，遂誅。

translations.literal: Wan'er showed the draft to Liu Youqiu; Youqiu spoke to the prince; the prince would not agree; she was thereupon executed.
translations.idiomatic: She showed the draft to Liu Youqiu, who urged mercy; the prince refused and had her executed.

sentences.zh: 開元初，裒次其文章，詔張說題篇。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan her writings were collected; Zhang Yue was ordered to compose the preface.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyuan her writings were collected with a preface by Zhang Yue.

sentences.zh: 睿宗肅明劉皇后睿宗肅明順聖皇后劉氏，祖德威，自有傳。

translations.literal: Empress Suming Liu of Ruizong—Empress Suming Shunsheng Liu of Ruizong—her grandfather Dewei has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Suming Shunsheng Liu of Ruizong—her grandfather Dewei has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳中，帝在籓，納為孺人，俄為妃。

translations.literal: In Yifeng when the emperor was in the domain he took her as Lady; soon she became consort.
translations.idiomatic: In Yifeng (676-679) when Ruizong was a prince he took her as Lady, soon consort.

sentences.zh: 生寧王、壽昌代國二公主。

translations.literal: She bore the Prince of Ning and Princesses Shouchang and Dai of the State.
translations.idiomatic: She bore Prince of Ning and Princesses Shouchang and Dai.

sentences.zh: 帝即位，為皇后。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne she became empress.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong took the throne she became empress.

sentences.zh: 會帝降號皇嗣，復為妃。

translations.literal: When the emperor lowered his title to imperial heir she again became consort.
translations.idiomatic: When he became heir apparent she was reduced to consort.

sentences.zh: 長壽二年，為戶婢誣與竇德妃挾蠱道祝詛武后，並殺之宮中，葬秘莫知。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longevity a palace woman falsely accused her and Consort Dou of witchcraft cursing Empress Wu; both were killed in the palace and buried in secret, none knowing where.
translations.idiomatic: In Longevity 2 (693) a palace woman accused her and Consort Dou of witchcraft against Empress Wu; both were killed secretly.

sentences.zh: 景雲元年，追謚肅明皇后。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingyun she was posthumously titled Empress Suming.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingyun 1 (710) she was posthumously titled Empress Suming.

sentences.zh: 睿宗昭成竇皇后睿宗昭成順聖皇后竇氏，曾祖抗，父孝諶，自有傳。

translations.literal: Empress Zhaocheng Dou of Ruizong—Empress Zhaocheng Shunsheng Dou—her great-grandfather Kang and father Xiaochen have their own biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhaocheng Shunsheng Dou of Ruizong—her great-grandfather Kang and father Xiaochen have separate biographies.

sentences.zh: 后婉淑，尤循禮則。

translations.literal: The empress was gentle and refined, especially observant of ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Gentle and refined, she was especially observant of ritual.

sentences.zh: 帝為相王，納為孺人；

translations.literal: When the emperor was Prince of Xiang he took her as Lady;
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong was Prince of Xiang he took her as Lady;

sentences.zh: 即位，進德妃。

translations.literal: when he took the throne she was advanced to Cultivated Consort.
translations.idiomatic: when he took the throne she became Cultivated Consort.

sentences.zh: 生玄宗及金仙、玉真二公主。

translations.literal: She bore Xuanzong and Princesses Jinxian and Yuzhen.
translations.idiomatic: She bore Xuanzong and Princesses Jinxian and Yuzhen.

sentences.zh: 與肅明同追謚，並招魂葬東都之南，肅明曰惠陵，後曰靖陵，立別廟曰儀坤以享云。

translations.literal: With Suming she received posthumous titles together; souls were summoned and buried south of the eastern capital—Suming's tomb called Hui Mausoleum, hers Jing Mausoleum; separate temples called Yikun were established for sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Both received posthumous titles; their souls were summoned and buried south of Luoyang—Hui Mausoleum for Suming, Jing for Dou—with Yikun temples for sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 帝崩，追稱皇太后，與肅明祔橋陵。

translations.literal: When the emperor died she was posthumously titled empress dowager and paired at Qiao Mausoleum with Suming.
translations.idiomatic: At Ruizong's death she was titled empress dowager and paired with Suming at Qiaoling.

sentences.zh: 後以子貴，故先祔睿宗室。

translations.literal: Later because her son was exalted she was first paired in Ruizong's temple.
translations.idiomatic: Because her son became emperor she was first enshrined in Ruizong's temple.

sentences.zh: 肅明以開元二十年乃得祔廟。

translations.literal: Suming was not paired in the temple until the twentieth year of Kaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Suming was not enshrined until Kaiyuan 20 (732).

sentences.zh: 初，太常加謚後曰「大昭成」。

translations.literal: At first the Minister of Ceremonies added to the empress's posthumous title "Great Zhaocheng."
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Ceremonies first added "Great Zhaocheng" to her posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 或言：「法宜引『聖真』冠謚，而曰『大昭成』，非也。

translations.literal: Someone said: "By law one should place 'Sacred Truth' at the head of the posthumous title; to say 'Great Zhaocheng' is incorrect.
translations.idiomatic: Critics said "Sacred Truth" should head the title; "Great Zhaocheng" was incorrect.

sentences.zh: 以單言配之，應曰『聖昭』若『睿成』；

translations.literal: With single terms paired it should be 'Sacred Zhao' or 'Sagacious Cheng';
translations.idiomatic: With single terms it should be Sacred Zhao or Sagacious Cheng;

sentences.zh: 以復言配之，應曰『大聖昭成』、『聖真昭成』。

translations.literal: with compound pairing it should be 'Great Sacred Zhaocheng' or 'Sacred Truth Zhaocheng.'"
translations.idiomatic: with compound terms Great Sacred Zhaocheng or Sacred Truth Zhaocheng."

sentences.zh: 」又引太穆皇后始謚穆，及高祖崩，合帝謚曰太穆，追增太穆神皇后；

translations.literal: They also cited Grand Empress Taumu's initial posthumous title Mu, and when Gaozu died the combined imperial posthumous title made Great Taumu Divine Empress;
translations.idiomatic: They cited Grand Empress Taumu, initially titled Mu, later Great Taumu Divine Empress after Gaozu's death;

sentences.zh: 文德皇后始謚文德，及太宗崩，合謚文德聖皇后。

translations.literal: Cultivated Virtue Empress's initial posthumous title Cultivated Virtue, and when Taizong died the combined title Cultivated Virtue Sacred Empress.
translations.idiomatic: and Cultivated Virtue Empress, later Cultivated Virtue Sacred Empress after Taizong's death.

sentences.zh: 又援范曄著漢光烈等為比。

translations.literal: They also cited Fan Ye's use of Han Guanglie and the like as comparison.
translations.idiomatic: They cited Fan Ye's Guanglie and similar Han titles.

sentences.zh: 太常謂：「曄以帝號標后謚，是史家記事體，婦人非必與夫同也。

translations.literal: The Minister of Ceremonies said: "Ye used the emperor's title to mark the empress's posthumous name—that is the historian's narrative form; a woman need not necessarily follow her husband.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Ceremonies replied: "Fan Ye used the emperor's title in posthumous names—that is historiography; a woman need not follow her husband.

sentences.zh: 入廟稱后，繫夫；

translations.literal: In the temple she is called empress, tied to the husband;
translations.idiomatic: In temple she is called empress, tied to her husband;

sentences.zh: 在朝稱太，繫子。

translations.literal: in court she is called Grand, tied to the son.
translations.idiomatic: in court she is called Grand, tied to her son.

sentences.zh: 『文母』，生號也；

translations.literal: 'Cultured Mother' is a living title;
translations.idiomatic: 'Cultured Mother' is a living title;

sentences.zh: 『文王』，既沒謚也。

translations.literal: 'Cultured King' is a posthumous title after death.
translations.idiomatic: 'Cultured King' is a posthumous title after death.

sentences.zh: 周公豈以夫從婦乎？

translations.literal: Would the Duke of Zhou follow the wife from the husband?
translations.idiomatic: Would the Duke of Zhou take his title from his wife?

sentences.zh: 漢法不可以為據。

translations.literal: Han law cannot serve as precedent."
translations.idiomatic: Han precedents do not apply."

sentences.zh: 」制曰「可」。

translations.literal: The order said "Approved."
translations.idiomatic: The order approved.

sentences.zh: 天寶八載制詔，自太穆而下六皇后，並增上「順聖」二謚云。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tianbao an imperial edict added "Shunsheng" to the posthumous titles of the six empresses from Taumu downward.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 8 (749) an edict added Shunsheng to six empresses from Taumu downward.

sentences.zh: 玄宗王皇后玄宗皇后王氏，同州下邽人。

translations.literal: Empress Wang of Xuanzong—Empress Wang of Xuanzong—was a native of Xiaqi in Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wang of Xuanzong was from Xiaqi in Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 梁冀州刺史神念之裔孫。

translations.literal: Descendant of Liang Prefect Shennian of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: She descended from Liang Prefect Wang Shennian of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 帝為臨淄王，聘為妃。

translations.literal: When the emperor was Prince of Linzi he betrothed her as consort.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong was Prince of Linzi he betrothed her as consort.

sentences.zh: 將清內難，預大計。

translations.literal: About to settle inner turmoil, she shared in the great plan.
translations.idiomatic: She shared in planning the coup that settled inner turmoil.

sentences.zh: 先天元年，立為皇后。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiantian she was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiantian 1 (712) she was made empress.

sentences.zh: 久無子，而武妃稍有寵，后不平，顯詆之。

translations.literal: Long without sons while Consort Wu gradually won favor, the empress was resentful and openly slandered her.
translations.idiomatic: Childless while Consort Wu gained favor, she grew resentful and openly slandered her.

sentences.zh: 然撫下素有恩，終無肯譖短者。

translations.literal: Yet in treating subordinates she had always been gracious; in the end none would speak ill of her.
translations.idiomatic: Yet she had always treated subordinates kindly; none would speak ill of her.

sentences.zh: 帝密欲廢后，以語姜晈。

translations.literal: The emperor secretly wished to depose the empress and told Jiang Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong secretly wished to depose her and told Jiang Jiao.

sentences.zh: 晈漏言，即死。

translations.literal: Jiao leaked the words; he died at once.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao leaked the plan and died immediately.

sentences.zh: 后兄守一懼，為求厭勝，浮屠明悟教祭北斗，取霹靂木刻天地文及帝諱合佩之，曰：「後有子，與則天比。

translations.literal: The empress's brother Shouyi was afraid and sought sorcery; the monk Mingwu taught sacrifice to the Big Dipper, taking thunderwood carved with Heaven-and-Earth text and the emperor's taboo name combined as talisman, saying: "Later there will be a son, comparable to Wu Zetian."
translations.idiomatic: Her brother Shouyi sought sorcery; monk Mingwu taught Big Dipper sacrifice with thunderwood talismans carved with imperial names, promising sons like Wu Zetian.

sentences.zh: 」開元十二年，事覺，帝自臨劾有狀，乃制詔有司：「皇后天命不祐，華而不實，有無將之心，不可以承宗廟、母儀天下，其廢為庶人。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Kaiyuan the matter was exposed; the emperor personally interrogated and found evidence; he then decreed to the relevant offices: "The empress lacks Heaven's blessing, is flowery without substance, has the heart of one who will not submit—she cannot inherit the ancestral temples or mother the realm; she is deposed as commoner."
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 12 (724) the plot was exposed. Xuanzong decreed: "The empress lacks Heaven's blessing, is flowery without substance, harbors defiance—she cannot mother the realm" and deposed her.

sentences.zh: 」賜守一死。

translations.literal: Shouyi was sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyi was executed.

sentences.zh: 始，后以愛弛，不自安。

translations.literal: At first because favor waned the empress was ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: As favor waned she grew uneasy.

sentences.zh: 承閒泣曰：「陛下獨不念阿忠脫紫半臂易斗麵，為生日湯餅邪？

translations.literal: Seizing an interval she wept: "Does Your Majesty not remember A-Zhong trading half a purple sleeve for a peck of flour to make birthday noodles?"
translations.idiomatic: She wept: "Does Your Majesty not remember A-Zhong trading half a purple sleeve for flour to make your birthday noodles?"

sentences.zh: 」帝憫然動容。

translations.literal: The emperor was moved and showed it on his face.
translations.idiomatic: Moved, the emperor's expression softened.

sentences.zh: 阿忠，后呼其父仁皎云。

translations.literal: A-Zhong was what the empress called her father Renjiao.
translations.idiomatic: A-Zhong was her name for her father Renjiao.

sentences.zh: 繇是久乃廢。

translations.literal: From this the deposition was long delayed.
translations.idiomatic: This delayed her deposition for years.

sentences.zh: 當時王諲作《翠羽帳賦》諷帝。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Yin composed "Green Feather Canopy Rhapsody" to admonish the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yin composed the Green Feather Canopy Rhapsody to admonish the emperor.

sentences.zh: 未幾卒，以一品禮葬。

translations.literal: Before long she died and was buried with first-rank rites.
translations.idiomatic: Soon she died and was buried with first-rank honors.

sentences.zh: 後宮思慕之，帝亦悔。

translations.literal: The inner palace mourned her; the emperor also regretted.
translations.idiomatic: The inner palace mourned her; the emperor regretted as well.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年，追復后號。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoying her empress title was posthumously restored.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoying 1 (762) her empress title was restored.

sentences.zh: 玄宗貞順武皇后玄宗貞順皇后武氏，恒安王攸止女，幼入宮。

translations.literal: Empress Zhenshun Wu of Xuanzong—Empress Zhenshun Wu of Xuanzong—daughter of Prince of Heng'an Youzhi; she entered the palace young.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhenshun Wu of Xuanzong, daughter of Prince of Heng'an Youzhi, entered the palace young.

sentences.zh: 帝即位，寖得幸。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne she gradually won favor.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong took the throne she gradually won favor.

sentences.zh: 時王皇后廢，故進冊惠妃，其禮秩比皇后。

translations.literal: At the time Empress Wang was deposed; therefore she was advanced to Cultivated Consort with ritual rank equal to empress.
translations.idiomatic: With Empress Wang deposed she was made Cultivated Consort with empress-level honors.

sentences.zh: 初，帝在潞，趙麗妃以倡幸，有容止，善歌舞。

translations.literal: At first when the emperor was in Lu, Concubine Zhao Liji won favor by her singing; she had graceful bearing and was skilled in song and dance.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong was in Lu, Concubine Zhao Liji, a singing girl, won favor for her beauty and skill in song and dance.

sentences.zh: 開元初，父兄皆美官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan her father and brothers all held fine offices.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyuan her father and brothers all held prestigious posts.

sentences.zh: 及妃進，麗妃恩亦弛，以十四年卒，謚曰和。

translations.literal: When the consort was advanced, Concubine Li's favor also slackened; she died in the fourteenth year and was given the posthumous name He.
translations.idiomatic: When Consort Wu rose, Liji's favor waned; she died in Kaiyuan 14 with posthumous name He.

sentences.zh: 生太子瑛。

translations.literal: She bore Crown Prince Ying.
translations.idiomatic: She bore Crown Prince Ying.

sentences.zh: 而皇甫德儀生鄂王，劉才人生光王，皆藩邸之舊，後愛薄，而妃乃專寵。

translations.literal: Yet Huangfu Deyi bore Prince E and Liu Cairen bore Prince Guang—all old companions from the princely residence whose favor later thinned, while the consort alone held exclusive favor.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Deyi bore Prince E and Liu Cairen bore Prince Guang—old favorites from his princely days whose favor faded, while Consort Wu held exclusive favor.

sentences.zh: 封所生母楊鄭國夫人，弟忠國子祭酒，信秘書監。

translations.literal: Her birth mother Yang was enfeoffed as Lady of Zheng; her brother Zhong was made Director of the Imperial University and Xin Secretariat Director.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother Yang was made Lady of Zheng; brother Zhong became Director of the Imperial University and Xin Secretariat Director.

sentences.zh: 將遂立皇后，御史潘好禮上疏曰：「《禮》，父母讎，不共天。

translations.literal: They were about to establish her as empress when Censor Pan Haoli submitted a memorial saying: "In the Rites, a parent's enemy—one does not share Heaven with them.
translations.idiomatic: About to make her empress, Censor Pan Haoli memorialized: "The Rites say one does not share Heaven with a parent's enemy.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》，子不復讎，不子也。

translations.literal: In the Spring and Autumn Annals, a son who does not avenge his parent is no son.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals say a son who will not avenge his parent is no son.

sentences.zh: 陛下欲以武氏為后，何以見天下士！

translations.literal: Your Majesty wishes to make the Wu clan empress—how can you face the gentlemen of the realm!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty wishes to make Lady Wu empress—how can you face the scholars of the realm!

sentences.zh: 妃再從叔三思也，從父延秀也，皆干紀亂常，天下共疾。

translations.literal: The consort's second cousin Sansi and cousin by the father's line Yanxiu both violated norms and disturbed order; all under Heaven loathed them together.
translations.idiomatic: Her second cousin Sansi and paternal cousin Yanxiu both violated norms; the realm despised them.

sentences.zh: 夫惡木垂蔭，志士不息；

translations.literal: A wicked tree casting shade—a man of resolve will not rest beneath it;
translations.idiomatic: Beneath a wicked tree's shade a resolute man will not rest;

sentences.zh: 盜泉飛溢，廉夫不飲。

translations.literal: the Thieving Spring overflowing—a man of integrity will not drink.
translations.idiomatic: at the Thieving Spring's overflow an upright man will not drink.

sentences.zh: 匹夫匹婦尚相擇，況天子乎？

translations.literal: Common men and women still choose one another—how much more the Son of Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Even commoners choose their mates—how much more the Son of Heaven?

sentences.zh: 願慎選華族，稱神祇之心。

translations.literal: I pray Your Majesty carefully select a noble clan, fitting the hearts of the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: I pray you choose carefully from noble houses, as Heaven and the spirits desire.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》：宋人夏父之會，無以妾為夫人；

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals: at the meeting of Xiafu of Song, no concubine was made lady;
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals: at Xiafu of Song's meeting, no concubine was made lady;

sentences.zh: 齊桓公誓葵丘曰：『無以妾為妻。

translations.literal: Duke Huan of Qi swore at Kuiqiu: "No concubine shall be made wife.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Huan of Qi swore at Kuiqiu: "No concubine shall be made wife.

sentences.zh: 』此聖人明嫡庶之分。

translations.literal: " This is how the sages clarified the distinction between principal wife and concubine.
translations.idiomatic: " Thus the sages clarified principal wife from concubine.

sentences.zh: 分定，則窺競之心息矣。

translations.literal: Once the distinction is fixed, the heart of encroaching rivalry will cease.
translations.idiomatic: Once ranks are fixed, rivalry will cease.

sentences.zh: 今人間咸言右丞相張說欲取立后功圖復相，今太子非惠妃所生，而妃有子，若一儷宸極，則儲位將不安。

translations.literal: Now people everywhere say Right Chancellor Zhang Yue wishes to gain merit by establishing an empress and plot return to the chancellorship; the crown prince was not born of Cultivated Consort, yet the consort has a son—if she shares the imperial seat as equal, the heir's position will not be secure.
translations.idiomatic: Rumor says Zhang Yue seeks credit for making her empress to regain office; the crown prince is not her son, yet she has sons—if she becomes empress the heir's place will be insecure.

sentences.zh: 古人所以諫其漸者，有以也！

translations.literal: The ancients admonished against gradual encroachment for good reason!
translations.idiomatic: The ancients warned against such gradual encroachment for good reason!

sentences.zh: 」遂不果立。

translations.literal: " Thus she was not established after all.
translations.idiomatic: The appointment did not take place.

sentences.zh: 妃生子必秀嶷，凡二王、一主，皆不育。

translations.literal: When the consort bore sons they were invariably handsome and lofty; of two princes and one princess, none survived.
translations.idiomatic: Sons she bore were handsome and tall; two princes and one princess all died young.

sentences.zh: 及生壽王，帝命寧王養外邸。

translations.literal: When she bore Prince Shou the emperor ordered Prince of Ning to raise him in an outer residence.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Shou was born the emperor had the Prince of Ning raise him outside the palace.

sentences.zh: 又生盛王、咸宜太華二公主。

translations.literal: She also bore Prince Sheng and the two princesses of Xianyi and Taihua.
translations.idiomatic: She also bore Prince Sheng and Princesses Xianyi and Taihua.

sentences.zh: 後李林甫以壽王母愛，希妃意陷太子、鄂光二王，皆廢死。

translations.literal: Later Li Linfu, because Prince Shou's mother was favored, curried the consort's favor and framed the crown prince and Princes E and Guang—all were deposed and died.
translations.idiomatic: Later Li Linfu, courting her through Prince Shou's mother, framed the crown prince and Princes E and Guang—all were deposed and died.

sentences.zh: 會妃薨，年四十餘，贈皇后及謚，葬敬陵。

translations.literal: When the consort died, aged forty-odd, she was posthumously given empress rank and a posthumous name and was buried at Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: She died in her forties, was posthumously made empress, and was buried at Jingling.

sentences.zh: 玄宗元獻楊皇后玄宗元獻皇后楊氏，華州華陰人。

translations.literal: Empress Yuanxian Yang of Xuanzong—Empress Yuanxian Yang of Xuanzong—was a native of Huayin in Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yuanxian Yang of Xuanzong, a native of Huayin in Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 曾祖士達，為隋納言。

translations.literal: Her great-grandfather Shida was Director of the Secretariat under Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Her great-grandfather Shida was Sui Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 天授中，以武后母黨，追封士達為鄭王，父知慶太尉。

translations.literal: In the Tianshou era, as kin of Empress Wu's mother's clan, Shida was posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Zheng and her father Zhiqing made Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianshou, as Wu's maternal kin, Shida was posthumously made Prince of Zheng and father Zhiqing Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 帝在東宮，后以景雲初入宮為良媛。

translations.literal: When the emperor was heir apparent the empress entered the palace in the first year of Jingyun as Lady of Grace.
translations.idiomatic: When he was crown prince she entered in Jingyun 1 as Lady of Grace.

sentences.zh: 時太平公主忌帝，而宮中左右持兩端，纖悉必聞。

translations.literal: At the time Princess Taiping resented the emperor, while palace attendants on either side held to both factions and reported every detail.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Taiping opposed him; palace attendants played both sides and reported everything.

sentences.zh: 媛方娠，帝不自安，密語侍讀張說曰：「用事者不欲吾多子，奈何？

translations.literal: The lady was pregnant; the emperor was ill at ease and secretly told Attendant Reader Zhang Yue: "Those in power do not wish me many sons—what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: Pregnant, he confided to Zhang Yue: "Those in power do not want me many sons—what can I do?

sentences.zh: 」命說挾劑以入，帝於曲室自煮之。

translations.literal: " He ordered Yue to bring in medicine; the emperor boiled it himself in a side room.
translations.idiomatic: " He had Yue bring medicine and boiled it himself in a side room.

sentences.zh: 夢若有介而戈者環鼎三，而三煮盡覆。

translations.literal: He dreamed of one bearing a spear who circled the cauldron three times, and all three boilings were overturned.
translations.idiomatic: He dreamed a spear-bearer circled the cauldron thrice and overturned all three boilings.

sentences.zh: 以告說，說曰：「天命也！

translations.literal: He told Yue, who said: "It is Heaven's mandate!
translations.idiomatic: Yue said: "It is Heaven's mandate!

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: He stopped.
translations.idiomatic: And he stopped.

sentences.zh: 生男，是為肅宗。

translations.literal: She bore a son—this was Suzong.
translations.idiomatic: She bore a son—Suzong.

sentences.zh: 帝即位，為貴嬪。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne she became Honored Consort.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong took the throne she became Honored Consort.

sentences.zh: 其姊，節愍太子妃也。

translations.literal: Her elder sister was consort to the Jiemin crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Her elder sister was consort to Crown Prince Jiemin.

sentences.zh: 初，肅宗生，卜云：「不宜養。

translations.literal: At first when Suzong was born, divination said: "He should not be raised.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong was born, divination said: "He should not be raised in the palace.

sentences.zh: 」乃命王皇后舉之。

translations.literal: " He was therefore entrusted to Empress Wang to raise.
translations.idiomatic: " Empress Wang was ordered to raise him.

sentences.zh: 后無子，撫肅宗如所生。

translations.literal: The empress had no sons and nurtured Suzong as if he were her own.
translations.idiomatic: Childless, the empress raised Suzong as her own.

sentences.zh: 後又生寧親公主，乃薨。

translations.literal: Later she also bore Princess Ningqin, then died.
translations.idiomatic: She later bore Princess Ningqin, then died.

sentences.zh: 說以舊恩，故子垍得尚寧親。

translations.literal: Because of old favor Yue's son Kui was able to marry Ningqin.
translations.idiomatic: Through old favor Yue's son Kui married Ningqin.

sentences.zh: 肅宗即位，至德二載，太上皇自蜀誥有司「其議尊稱」，遂上冊謚。

translations.literal: When Suzong took the throne, in the second year of Zhide the retired emperor from Shu ordered the relevant offices to "deliberate honored titles," and she was given posthumous enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhide 2 the retired emperor ordered honors deliberated and she received posthumous enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 寶應末，祔泰陵。

translations.literal: At the end of Baoying she was enshrined at Tailing.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Baoying she was enshrined at Tailing.

sentences.zh: 玄宗貴妃楊氏玄宗貴妃楊氏，隋梁郡通守汪四世孫。

translations.literal: Imperial Consort Yang of Xuanzong—Imperial Consort Yang of Xuanzong—was fourth-generation descendant of Wang, Commandant of Liang Prefecture under Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Consort Yang of Xuanzong, fourth-generation descendant of Sui Liang Prefecture Commandant Wang.

sentences.zh: 徙籍蒲州，遂為永樂人。

translations.literal: Her household register was moved to Puzhou and she became a native of Yongle.
translations.idiomatic: Her register was moved to Puzhou; she became a native of Yongle.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，養叔父家。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, she was raised in her uncle's household.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, she was raised by her uncle.

sentences.zh: 始為壽王妃。

translations.literal: At first she was consort to Prince Shou.
translations.idiomatic: She was first Princess Shou's consort.

sentences.zh: 開元二十四年，武惠妃薨，後廷無當帝意者。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Kaiyuan Cultivated Consort Wu died and thereafter none in the rear court suited the emperor's mind.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 24 Cultivated Consort Wu died; none in the inner palace pleased him.

sentences.zh: 或言妃姿質天挺，宜充掖廷，遂召內禁中，異之，即為自出妃意者，丐籍女官，號「太真」，更為壽王聘韋昭訓女，而太真得幸。

translations.literal: Some said the consort's bearing was heaven-endowed and fit to fill the rear apartments; she was summoned into the inner palace and he marveled at her; one who came out on the consort's behalf begged registry as a palace woman with the name "Great Perfection"; Prince Shou was given Wei Zhaoxun's daughter in marriage instead, and Great Perfection won favor.
translations.idiomatic: Said to be heaven-endowed, she was summoned within; registered as palace woman "Taizhen," Prince Shou wed Wei Zhaoxun's daughter instead, and Taizhen won favor.

sentences.zh: 善歌舞，邃曉音律，且智算警穎，迎意輒悟。

translations.literal: Skilled in song and dance, thoroughly versed in music, and moreover clever and alert in calculation, she grasped his intent as soon as it arose.
translations.idiomatic: She excelled at song and dance and music, clever and quick to read his wishes.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，遂專房宴，宮中號「娘子」，儀體與皇后等。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and henceforth feasted with her alone; within the palace she was called "Lady" and her ceremonial standing equaled the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, he kept her to himself; the palace called her "Lady" with empress-level ceremony.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，進冊貴妃。

translations.literal: In the first years of Tianbao she was advanced and enfeoffed as imperial consort.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianbao she was made imperial consort.

sentences.zh: 追贈父玄琰太尉、齊國公。

translations.literal: Her father Xuanyan was posthumously made Grand Marshal and Duke of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Father Xuanyan was posthumously Grand Marshal and Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 擢叔玄珪光祿卿，宗兄銛鴻臚卿，錡侍御史，尚太華公主。

translations.literal: Uncle Xuangui was promoted Director of the Imperial Household; clan elder brother Xian Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; Xi Vice Censor and married to Princess Taihua.
translations.idiomatic: Uncle Xuangui became Director of the Imperial Household; Xian Director of Imperial Entertainments; Xi Vice Censor, wed Princess Taihua.

sentences.zh: 主，惠妃所生，最見寵遇。

translations.literal: The princess, born of Cultivated Consort, received the greatest favor.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Taihua, Cultivated Consort's daughter, was most favored.

sentences.zh: 而釗亦寖顯。

translations.literal: And Zhao also gradually rose to prominence.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao also gradually rose.

sentences.zh: 釗，國忠也。

translations.literal: Zhao was Guozhong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was Guozhong.

sentences.zh: 三姊皆美劭，帝呼為姨，封韓、虢、秦三國，為夫人，出入宮掖，恩寵聲焰震天下。

translations.literal: All three elder sisters were beautiful; the emperor called them "Aunt" and enfeoffed the states of Han, Guo, and Qin as ladies; entering and leaving the palace apartments, their favor and renown shook all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Three elder sisters, called "Aunt," were made Ladies of Han, Guo, and Qin; their favor shook the realm.

sentences.zh: 每命婦入班，持盈公主等皆讓不敢就位。

translations.literal: Whenever appointed ladies took their places in court, Princess Chiying and others yielded and dared not take their seats.
translations.idiomatic: At court assemblies even Princess Chiying yielded her seat to them.

sentences.zh: 臺省、州縣奉請托，奔走期會過詔敕。

translations.literal: Provincial and prefectural offices fulfilled their requests; they rushed to appointments surpassing imperial edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Provinces and prefectures rushed their requests ahead of imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 四方獻餉結納，門若市然。

translations.literal: Tribute and gifts from the four quarters bound them by obligation; their gates were like a market.
translations.idiomatic: Gifts from every quarter packed their gates like a market.

sentences.zh: 建平、信成二公主以與妃家忤，至追內封物，駙馬都尉獨孤明失官。

translations.literal: Princesses Jianping and Xincheng, having offended the consort's family, had even their inner stipends reclaimed and Chief Commandant of the Horse Dugu Ming lost his office.
translations.idiomatic: Princesses Jianping and Xincheng, offending her kin, lost stipends; Chief Commandant Dugu Ming lost office.

sentences.zh: 它日，妃以譴還銛第，比中仄，帝尚不御食，笞怒左右。

translations.literal: Another day the consort was sent back in reprimand to Xian's residence; past midday the emperor still would not eat and beat and raged at attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Once sent home in disgrace, past noon he still would not eat and raged at attendants.

sentences.zh: 高力士欲驗帝意，乃白以殿中供帳、司農酒餼百餘車送妃所，帝即以御膳分賜。

translations.literal: Gao Lishi wished to test the emperor's intent and reported sending over a hundred carts of palace furnishings and imperial granary wine and food to the consort's place; the emperor at once shared his own meal.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lishi sent a hundred carts of furnishings and provisions; the emperor shared his meal.

sentences.zh: 力士知帝旨，是夕，請召妃還，下鑰安興坊門馳入。

translations.literal: Lishi knew the emperor's intent; that night he asked to summon the consort back, unlocked the Anxing Ward gate and galloped her in.
translations.idiomatic: Lishi summoned her back that night, opening Anxing Ward gate at a gallop.

sentences.zh: 妃見帝，伏地謝，帝釋然，撫尉良渥。

translations.literal: Seeing the emperor she prostrated herself in thanks; the emperor was relieved and comforted her generously.
translations.idiomatic: She prostrated herself; he was mollified and comforted her lavishly.

sentences.zh: 明日，諸姨上食，樂作，帝驟賜左右不可貲。

translations.literal: The next day when the aunts presented food and music played, the emperor suddenly bestowed on attendants gifts beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Next day when the aunts presented food with music, he showered attendants with gifts.

sentences.zh: 由是愈見寵，賜諸姨錢歲百萬為脂粉費。

translations.literal: From this she was favored all the more; the aunts were granted a million cash yearly for rouge and powder.
translations.idiomatic: Favor deepened; each aunt received a million cash yearly for cosmetics.

sentences.zh: 銛以上柱國門列戟，與銛、國忠、諸姨五家第舍聯亙，擬憲宮禁，率一堂費緡千萬。

translations.literal: Xian was given the upper pillar rank with halberds at his gate; with Xian, Guozhong, and the aunts—five households—their mansions stretched in succession rivaling the imperial precincts, each hall costing ten million strings.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's gate bore halberds; five mansions stretched in a row rivaling the palace, each hall costing ten million.

sentences.zh: 見它第有勝者，輒壞復造，務以瓌侈相誇詡，土木工不息。

translations.literal: Seeing another residence surpass theirs, they would demolish and rebuild, striving to outdo one another in splendor; builders of earth and wood never rested.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing a finer house they demolished and rebuilt, vying in luxury without cease.

sentences.zh: 帝所得奇珍及貢獻分賜之，使者相銜於道，五家如一。

translations.literal: Rare treasures the emperor obtained and tribute shares were bestowed on them; messengers lined the road one after another—the five households alike.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial treasures and tribute went to all five alike, messengers lining the roads.

sentences.zh: 妃每從遊幸，乘馬則力士授轡策。

translations.literal: Whenever the consort accompanied on tours, if she rode a horse Lishi handed her bridle and whip.
translations.idiomatic: On outings Lishi held her bridle when she rode.

sentences.zh: 凡充錦繡官及冶瑑金玉者，大抵千人，奉須索，奇服秘玩，變化若神。

translations.literal: All who served as brocade officers and workers in gold and jade numbered roughly a thousand, supplying her needs; rare garments and secret curios changed as if by spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly a thousand craftsmen supplied brocades and jeweled ornaments; her wardrobe seemed magical.

sentences.zh: 四方爭為怪珍入貢，動駭耳目。

translations.literal: The four quarters vied to offer strange treasures in tribute, startling eye and ear.
translations.idiomatic: Every region vied in strange tribute that dazzled the senses.

sentences.zh: 於是嶺南節度使張九章、廣陵長史王翼以所獻最，進九章銀青階，擢翼戶部侍郎，天下風靡。

translations.literal: Thereupon Military Commissioner Zhang Jiuzhang of Lingnan and Chief Administrator Wang Yi of Guangling, for having offered the finest tribute, won Jiuzhang silver and cyan rank and Yi promotion to Vice Minister of Revenue—the realm took it as fashion.
translations.idiomatic: Best tribute won Zhang Jiuzhang promotion and Wang Yi a ministry post; the realm followed suit.

sentences.zh: 妃嗜荔支，必欲生致之，乃置騎傳送，走數千里，味未變已至京師。

translations.literal: The consort craved lychees and they had to be brought fresh; post-horses were set running thousands of li so the flavor was unchanged when they reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: She craved fresh lychees; relay horses ran thousands of li so flavor was unchanged at court.

sentences.zh: 天寶九載，妃復得譴還外第，國忠謀於吉溫。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Tianbao the consort was again sent back to an outer residence; Guozhong plotted with Ji Wen.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 9 she was banished again; Guozhong plotted with Ji Wen.

sentences.zh: 溫因見帝曰：「婦人過忤當死，然何惜宮中一席廣為鈇鑕地，更使外辱乎？

translations.literal: Wen therefore saw the emperor and said: "When a woman greatly offends she should die—but why spare a palace couch's breadth to broaden the ground for axe and sword, and further suffer outer disgrace?
translations.idiomatic: Ji Wen said: "A woman who offends deserves death—but why spare palace space only to suffer public shame?

sentences.zh: 」帝感動，輟食，詔中人張韜光賜之。

translations.literal: " Moved, the emperor stopped eating and ordered the eunuch Zhang Taoguang to bestow gifts on her.
translations.idiomatic: Moved, he stopped eating and sent eunuch Zhang Taoguang with gifts.

sentences.zh: 妃因韜光謝帝曰：「妾有罪當萬誅，然膚髮外皆上所賜，今且死，無以報。

translations.literal: Through Taoguang the consort thanked the emperor: "Your servant has crimes deserving ten thousand deaths, yet skin and hair without are all bestowed by Your Majesty; now about to die, there is no way to repay.
translations.idiomatic: She thanked him through Taoguang: "I deserve death, yet skin and hair are yours; facing death I cannot repay.

sentences.zh: 」引刀斷一繚髮奏之，曰：「以此留訣。

translations.literal: " She took a knife and cut off a lock of hair to present, saying: "With this I leave farewell.
translations.idiomatic: " She cut a lock of hair: "Take this as farewell.

sentences.zh: 」帝見駭惋，遽召入，禮遇如初。

translations.literal: " The emperor, startled and grieved, summoned her back at once; courtesy was as before.
translations.idiomatic: Startled and grieving, he summoned her back with former honors.

sentences.zh: 因又幸秦國及國忠第，賜兩家鉅萬。

translations.literal: He again visited the Qin and Guozhong residences and bestowed tens of millions on both households.
translations.idiomatic: He visited the Qin and Guozhong mansions and gave each tens of millions.

sentences.zh: 國忠既遙領劍南，每十月，帝幸華清宮，五宅車騎皆從，家別為隊，隊一色，俄五家隊合，爛若萬花，川谷成錦繡，國忠導以劍南旗節。

translations.literal: Once Guozhong held distant command of Jiannan, every tenth month when the emperor visited Huaqing Palace the five mansions' carriages and horsemen all followed; each household formed its own column in one color, then the five columns merged, brilliant as ten thousand flowers, valleys and streams become brocade; Guozhong led with Jiannan banners and insignia.
translations.idiomatic: Each tenth month at Huaqing the five households' cavalcades merged in five colors like ten thousand flowers; Guozhong led with Jiannan insignia.

sentences.zh: 遺鈿墮舄，瑟瑟璣琲，狼藉於道，香聞數十里。

translations.literal: Dropped hairpins and fallen shoes, sasa beads and fine jade, littered the road; fragrance was smelled for tens of li.
translations.idiomatic: Hairpins and shoes, sasa and jade littered the road; fragrance carried for miles.

sentences.zh: 十載正月望夜，妃家與廣寧主僮騎爭闤門，鞭挺讙競，主墮馬，僅得去。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth-night watch of the first month in the tenth year, the consort's household and Princess Guangning's servants and riders fought at the market gate with whips and cudgels in uproar; the princess fell from her horse and barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth of the first month, Tianbao 10, her household fought Guangning Princess at the market gate; the princess fell but escaped.

sentences.zh: 主見帝泣，乃詔殺楊氏奴，貶駙馬都尉程昌裔官。

translations.literal: The princess saw the emperor weeping; he then decreed execution of the Yang household slave and demoted Chief Commandant Cheng Changyi.
translations.idiomatic: She wept before the emperor; he executed a Yang slave and demoted Chief Commandant Cheng Changyi.

sentences.zh: 國忠之輔政，其息昢尚萬春公主，暄尚延和郡主；

translations.literal: In Guozhong's assisting government his son Fen married Princess Wanchun and Xuan married Princess Yanhe of Yanhe Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong's son Fen married Princess Wanchun and Xuan married Princess Yanhe;

sentences.zh: 弟鑑尚承榮郡主。

translations.literal: younger brother Jian married Princess Chengrong.
translations.idiomatic: brother Jian married Princess Chengrong.

sentences.zh: 又詔為玄琰立家廟，帝自書其碑。

translations.literal: He also decreed a clan temple for Xuanyan; the emperor personally wrote its stele.
translations.idiomatic: A clan temple was built for Xuanyan; the emperor wrote its stele.

sentences.zh: 銛、秦國早死，故韓、虢與國忠貴最久。

translations.literal: Xian and Qin died early, so Han, Guo, and Guozhong were exalted longest.
translations.idiomatic: Xian and Lady Qin died early; Han, Guo, and Guozhong lasted longest.

sentences.zh: 而虢國素與國忠亂，頗為人知，不恥也。

translations.literal: Yet Lady Guo had long been in illicit relations with Guozhong, widely known, yet unashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Guo and Guozhong were known to be lovers, yet unashamed.

sentences.zh: 每入謁，並驅道中，從監、侍姆百餘騎，炬蜜如盡，靚妝盈里，不施幃障，時人謂為「雄狐」。

translations.literal: Whenever they entered audience they drove abreast in the road, with over a hundred riders of stewards and matron-attendants; torches and honey lamps like day, splendid makeup filling the lane, no curtain screens—people of the time called them "male foxes."
translations.idiomatic: They rode abreast with a hundred attendants, torches bright as day, splendid and uncurtained—called "male foxes."

sentences.zh: 諸王子孫凡婚聘，必先因韓、虢以請，輒皆遂，至數百千金以謝。

translations.literal: Princes and grandsons seeking marriage first petitioned through Han and Guo and always succeeded, giving hundreds and thousands in gold in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Royal kin seeking marriage went through Han and Guo, paying hundreds of thousands in gold.

sentences.zh: 初，安祿山有邊功，帝寵之，詔與諸姨約為兄弟，而祿山母事妃，來朝，必宴餞結歡。

translations.literal: At first An Lushan had frontier merit and the emperor favored him, decreeing he become sworn brother to the aunts; Lushan treated the consort as mother, and whenever he came to court there were always feasts and farewells binding joy.
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan, favored for frontier merit, swore brotherhood with the aunts and treated the consort as mother, feasted on every visit.

sentences.zh: 祿山反，以誅國忠為名，且指言妃及諸姨罪。

translations.literal: Lushan rebelled, naming execution of Guozhong as pretext and also pointing to crimes of the consort and the aunts.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan rebelled to kill Guozhong, also denouncing the consort and aunts.

sentences.zh: 帝欲以皇太子撫軍，因禪位，諸楊大懼，哭於廷。

translations.literal: The emperor wished the crown prince to pacify the army and thereby abdicate; the Yang clan were greatly afraid and wept in the court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished the crown prince to command troops and abdicate; the Yangs wept in terror at court.

sentences.zh: 國忠入白妃，妃銜塊請死，帝意沮，乃止。

translations.literal: Guozhong entered and told the consort; she held a clod and begged death; the emperor's intent was dampened and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong told her; she begged death with a clod in her mouth; he abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 及西幸至馬嵬，陳玄禮等以天下計誅國忠，已死，軍不解。

translations.literal: When the western flight reached Mawei, Chen Xuanli and others executed Guozhong for the realm's sake; he was already dead yet the army would not disperse.
translations.idiomatic: At Mawei, Chen Xuanli and others killed Guozhong for the realm; he was dead but the army would not disband.

sentences.zh: 帝遣力士問故，曰：「禍本尚在！

translations.literal: The emperor sent Lishi to ask the reason; they said: "The root of the calamity still remains!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Gao Lishi to ask why; they said: "The root of the disaster remains!

sentences.zh: 」帝不得已，與妃訣，引而去，縊路祠下，裹屍以紫茵，瘞道側，年三十八。

translations.literal: " The emperor had no choice; he took leave of the consort and led her away; she was strangled beneath the roadside shrine, the corpse wrapped in purple matting and buried beside the road—aged thirty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Forced to part with her, he had her strangled at a roadside shrine, wrapped in purple matting and buried by the road. She was thirty-eight.

sentences.zh: 帝至自蜀，道過其所，使祭之，且詔改葬。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned from Shu he passed her place on the road, sent offerings, and decreed reburial.
translations.idiomatic: Returning from Shu he passed the site, made offerings, and decreed a proper reburial.

sentences.zh: 禮部侍郎李揆曰：「龍武將士以國忠負上速亂，為天下殺之。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Rites Li Kui said: "The Longwu guardsmen killed Guozhong because he betrayed Your Majesty and hastened rebellion, doing so for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kui of the Ministry of Rites said: "The Longwu guards killed Guozhong for betraying you and hastening rebellion—for the realm.

sentences.zh: 今葬妃，恐反仄自疑。

translations.literal: Now to bury the consort may make them turn suspicious against themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Burying the consort now may make them suspect us in turn.

sentences.zh: 」帝乃止。

translations.literal: " The emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor desisted.

sentences.zh: 密遣中使者具棺槨它葬焉。

translations.literal: Secretly he sent palace emissaries to prepare coffin and inner and outer coffins and bury her elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly sent eunuchs to bury her elsewhere with full rites.

sentences.zh: 啟瘞，故香囊猶在，中人以獻，帝視之，淒感流涕，命工貌妃於別殿，朝夕往，必為鯁欷。

translations.literal: Opening the burial, her old perfume pouch was still there; the eunuch presented it; the emperor looked and wept in grief, ordered craftsmen to paint her likeness in a separate hall, and morning and evening when he went he always choked with sobs.
translations.idiomatic: Opening the grave he found her perfume pouch, wept, had her portrait painted in a side hall, and sobbed whenever he visited.

sentences.zh: 馬嵬之難，虢國與國忠妻裴柔等奔陳倉，縣令率吏追之，意以為賊，棄馬走林。

translations.literal: In the Mawei crisis Lady Guo and Guozhong's wife Pei Rou and others fled to Chencang; the magistrate led clerks in pursuit, thinking them bandits; they abandoned their horses and ran into the woods.
translations.idiomatic: At Mawei Lady Guo and Pei Rou fled to Chencang; the magistrate pursued them as bandits; they fled into the woods.

sentences.zh: 虢國先殺其二子，柔曰：「丐我死！

translations.literal: Lady Guo first killed her two sons; Rou said: "Grant me death!
translations.idiomatic: Lady Guo killed her two sons first; Pei Rou begged: "Let me die!

sentences.zh: 」即並其女刺殺之，乃自剄，不殊，吏載置於獄，問曰：「國家乎？

translations.literal: " She then stabbed her daughter together with her, then cut her own throat—not quite dead; the clerks loaded her into prison and asked: "For the state?
translations.idiomatic: " She stabbed her daughter too, then cut her throat; barely alive, clerks jailed her and asked: "For the state?

sentences.zh: 賊乎？

translations.literal: Or for bandits?
translations.idiomatic: Or for rebels?

sentences.zh: 」吏曰：「互有之。

translations.literal: " The clerks said: "Both in part.
translations.idiomatic: " They said: "A bit of both.

sentences.zh: 」乃死，瘞陳倉東郭外。

translations.literal: " She then died and was buried outside Chencang's eastern wall.
translations.idiomatic: She died and was buried outside Chencang's east gate.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：或稱武、韋亂唐同一轍，武持久，韋亟滅，何哉？

translations.literal: The commentator says: Some call the disorders of Wu and Wei the same track in ruining Tang—Wu endured long, Wei perished swiftly—why?
translations.idiomatic: The commentator asks: Wu and Wei both threw Tang into chaos—why did Wu last and Wei fall so fast?

sentences.zh: 議者謂否。

translations.literal: Discussants say no.
translations.idiomatic: Critics disagree.

sentences.zh: 武后自高宗時挾天子威福，脅制四海，雖逐嗣帝，改國號，然賞罰己出，不假借群臣，僭於上而治於下，故能終天年，阽亂而不亡。

translations.literal: From Gaozong's time Empress Wu wielded the Son of Heaven's authority and blessings, coercing the four seas; though she drove out the heir and changed the dynastic name, rewards and punishments issued from herself without borrowing ministers—usurping above yet governing below—therefore she could end her natural years, teetering on chaos yet not perishing.
translations.idiomatic: From Gaozong onward Wu Zetian wielded imperial power, drove out heirs and changed the dynastic name, yet ruled directly without relying on ministers—usurping from above while governing below—so she lived out her years though the realm teetered.

sentences.zh: 韋氏乘夫，淫蒸於朝，斜封四出，政放不一，既鴆殺帝，引睿宗輔政，權去手不自知，戚地已疏，人心相挻，玄宗藉其事以撼豪英，故取若掇遺，不旋踵宗族夷丹，勢奪而事淺也。

translations.literal: The Wei clan rode on the husband, wantonness steaming in court, slanting-seal appointments going out in all directions, government scattered and not unified; having poisoned the emperor she drew Ruizong to assist government—power left her hands yet she did not know it, her kin's ground already thin, hearts pulling one another apart; Xuanzong used the affair to shake the mighty, therefore taking them was like picking up what was left—before a turn of the heel the clan was exterminated to the last, power seized yet the affair shallow.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei clan leapt on their husband, debauched the court, sold offices widely, poisoned the emperor yet summoned Ruizong—power slipped from their hands unawares; Xuanzong seized the moment and extinguished the clan almost overnight, for their sway was broad but shallow.

sentences.zh: 然二后遺後王戒，顧不厚哉！

translations.literal: Yet the two empresses left warnings for later kings—is not the lesson weighty!
translations.idiomatic: Yet both empresses left stern warnings for later rulers—how weighty a lesson!
